title.zh: 卷四十三 列傳第三十一: 郭祚 張彝 邢巒 李崇
title.en: Volume 43 Biographies 31: Gao Zuo, Zhang Yi, Xing Luan, Li Chong
title.raw: 卷四十三 列傳第三十一: 郭祚 張彝 邢巒 李崇 Volume 43 Biographies 31: Gao Zuo, Zhang Yi, Xing Luan, Li Chong

sentences.zh: 郭祚 張彝 邢巒 李崇

translations.literal: Guo Zuo, Zhang Yi, Xing Luan, Li Chong
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zuo, Zhang Yi, Xing Luan, and Li Chong

sentences.zh: 列傳三十一

translations.literal: Biography 31
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 31

sentences.zh: 郭祚張彝孫晏之曾孫乾威邢巒弟子昕族孫臧邵李崇從弟平平子獎諧

translations.literal: Guo Zuo, Zhang Yi; Sun Yanzhi's great-grandson Qianwei; Xing Luan's disciple Xin, clansman Zang Shao; Li Chong's younger cousin from the same branch Ping, Ping's son Jiang, and He
translations.idiomatic: This chapter treats Guo Zuo and Zhang Yi; Sun Yanzhi's great-grandson Qianwei; Xing Luan's disciple Xin and his clansman Zang Shao; and Li Chong's younger cousin Ping, Ping's son Jiang, and He

sentences.zh: 郭祚，字季祐，太原晉陽人，魏車騎將軍淮弟亮之後也。

translations.literal: Guo Zuo, styled Jiyou, was a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan and a descendant of Liang, younger brother of Guo Huai, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zuo, whose style name was Jiyou, came from Jinyang in Taiyuan. He was descended from Liang, the younger brother of Guo Huai, who had served as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry under Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖逸，本州別駕，前後以二女妻司徒崔浩，一女妻浩弟上党太守恬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi had been an aide-de-camp of the province and, in succession, gave two daughters in marriage to the Minister of Works Cui Hao and one daughter to Hao's younger brother Tian, Governor of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi had served as provincial aide-de-camp and, one after another, married two daughters to the Minister of Works Cui Hao and a third to Hao's younger brother Tian, governor of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 太武時，浩親寵用事，拜逸徐州刺史，假榆次侯，贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Taiwu, when Hao was intimate and wielded power, Yi was appointed Governor of Xuzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuci in name, and posthumously honored as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Taiwu, when Cui Hao enjoyed the emperor's favor and held real power, Yi was appointed governor of Xuzhou, granted the nominal title Marquis of Yuci, and later posthumously honored as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 父洪之，坐浩事誅。

translations.literal: His father Hongzhi was executed on account of the affair of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hongzhi was put to death in connection with the Cui Hao affair.

sentences.zh: 祚亡竄得免。

translations.literal: Zuo fled into hiding and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo went into hiding and so escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，姿貌不偉，鄉人莫之識。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned and poor; his appearance was not imposing, and the people of his district did not know him.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in his youth, he was not striking in appearance, and his neighbors scarcely noticed him.

sentences.zh: 有女巫相祚後當富貴。

translations.literal: A witch divined that Zuo would later become rich and noble.
translations.idiomatic: A village witch foretold that Zuo would one day rise to wealth and high rank.

sentences.zh: 祚涉歷經史，習崔浩之書，尺牘文章見稱於世。

translations.literal: Zuo ranged through the classics and histories and studied the writings of Cui Hao; his letters and essays won praise in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He steeped himself in the classics and histories, studied Cui Hao's literary models, and gained a reputation for skill in correspondence and composition.

sentences.zh: 弱冠為州主簿，刺史孫小委之書記。

translations.literal: At his coming of age he became chief clerk of the province, and the governor Sun Xiao entrusted him with secretarial duties.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached manhood he was appointed chief clerk of the province, and Governor Sun Xiao put him in charge of his correspondence.

sentences.zh: 又太原太守王希彥，逸妻之侄也，共相賙恤，乃振。

translations.literal: Moreover, Wang Xiyan, Governor of Taiyuan and a nephew of Yi's wife, together gave mutual aid and relief, and he was thereby revived.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiyan, governor of Taiyuan and a nephew of Yi's wife, also helped support him, and in this way he slowly recovered his footing.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，舉秀才，對策上第，拜中書博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was recommended as a xiucai, placed first in the policy examination, and appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Xiaowen he was presented as a provincial graduate, ranked first in the palace examination, and appointed an erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 轉中書侍郎，遷尚書左丞，長兼給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat, promoted to Left Assistant of the Ministry, and for a long time concurrently served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made a gentleman of the Secretariat, promoted to left assistant director of the Ministry, and for a long stretch also held the concurrent post of attendant gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 祚清勤在公，夙夜匪懈，帝甚賞之。

translations.literal: Zuo was pure and diligent in office, toiling early and late without slackening, and the emperor greatly prized him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo served with scrupulous diligence, working from dawn to dusk without slackening, and the emperor held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 從南征，及還，正黃門。

translations.literal: He followed the southern campaign, and upon return was made Regular Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the southern campaign, and after their return was appointed regular attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸長安，行經渭橋，過淮廟，問祚曰：「是卿祖宗所承邪？」

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Chang'an and passed the temple of Huai on the Wei Bridge, the emperor asked Zuo, "Is this the line your ancestors received?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Chang'an and crossed the Wei Bridge, he passed the shrine of Huai and asked Zuo, "Is this the ancestor your family claims?

sentences.zh: 祚曰：「是臣七世伯祖。」

translations.literal: Zuo said, "He is my seventh-generation grand-uncle."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo replied, "He is my great-great-great-great-great-great-uncle."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「先賢後哲，頓在一門。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Former worthies and later talents, all in one gate."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Worthies of old and talent of today, gathered in a single household."

sentences.zh: 祚對曰：「昔臣先人以通儒英博，唯事魏文。

translations.literal: Zuo replied, "Formerly my forebear, a broadly learned master, served only Emperor Wen of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo answered, "In former times my ancestor, a scholar of wide learning, served none but Emperor Wen of Wei.

sentences.zh: 微臣虛薄，遭奉聖明，自惟幸甚。」

translations.literal: Your humble servant is shallow and slight, yet meets this sage clarity; I consider myself most fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: As for me, shallow and slight as I am, I have the good fortune to serve Your Sage Majesty; I can only count myself blessed."

sentences.zh: 因敕乙太牢祭淮廟，令祚自撰祭文。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the second bull to be sacrificed at the temple of Huai and commanded Zuo himself to compose the sacrificial text.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered a great offering at Huai's shrine and told Zuo to compose the sacrificial text himself.

sentences.zh: 以贊遷洛之規，賜爵東光子。

translations.literal: For his support of the plan to move the capital, he was granted the title of Viscount of Dongguang.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had supported the plan to transfer the capital, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Dongguang.

sentences.zh: 孝文曾幸華林園，因觀故景陽山。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen once visited the Hualin Garden and there viewed the old Jingyang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen once visited the Hualin Garden and gazed upon the old site of Jingyang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 祚曰：「山以仁靜，水以智流，願陛下修之。」

translations.literal: Zuo said, "Mountains rest through benevolence, waters flow through wisdom; I hope Your Majesty will cultivate them.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo said, "Mountains embody tranquil benevolence, waters embody flowing wisdom—may Your Majesty nurture both.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「魏明以奢失於前，朕何為襲之於後？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Emperor Ming of Wei lost the realm through extravagance in the past; why should I follow him in the future?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Emperor Ming of Wei ruined himself through luxury; why should I repeat his example?"

sentences.zh: 祚曰：「高山仰止。」

translations.literal: Zuo said, "The lofty mountain—one looks up and stops."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo answered, "As the ode says, one gazes up at the lofty mountain and halts in awe."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「得非景行之謂？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Can this mean the phrase 'worthy path'?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Do you mean the 'worthy path' of the ode?"

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，仍領黃門。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and still headed the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regular attendant-in-ordinary while continuing to head the yellow gate office.

sentences.zh: 是時，孝文銳意典禮，兼銓鏡九流，又遷都草創，征討不息；

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowen was keen on ritual and institutions, and at the same time weighed the Nine Ranks; moreover the transfer of the capital was newly begun and campaigns unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xiaowen was intent on reforming ritual and institutions, re-examining the nine-rank system, founding a new capital, and waging campaigns without pause.

sentences.zh: 內外規略，號為多事。

translations.literal: Plans within and without were called many affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Domestic and military planning alike were said to keep everyone fully occupied.

sentences.zh: 祚與黃門宋弁參謀帷幄，隨其才用，各有委寄。

translations.literal: Zuo and Song Bian of the Yellow Gate deliberated within the command tent, and according to each man's talent they were given separate charges.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo and Song Bian of the yellow gate advised within the command tent, and each was entrusted with duties suited to his abilities.

sentences.zh: 祚承稟注疏，特成勤劇。

translations.literal: Zuo received and carried out annotated orders, especially achieving strenuous diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo above all took charge of annotated orders and bore an especially heavy share of the work.

sentences.zh: 嘗以立馮昭儀，百官夕飲清徽後園。

translations.literal: Once, when Lady Feng was established as imperial consort, all officials drank in the evening in the Qingwei rear garden.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when Lady Feng was installed as imperial consort, the officials were given an evening banquet in the Qingwei rear garden.

sentences.zh: 孝文舉觴賜祚及崔光曰：「郭祚憂勤庶事，獨不欺我。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen raised his cup and bestowed it on Zuo and Cui Guang, saying, "Guo Zuo toils anxiously over the myriad affairs and never deceives me.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen raised his goblet and offered a toast to Zuo and Cui Guang, saying, "Guo Zuo labors tirelessly over every affair and never deceives me.

sentences.zh: 崔光溫良博物，朝之儒秀。

translations.literal: Cui Guang is gentle, good, and broadly learned—the Confucian ornament of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang is mild, learned, and broad in knowledge—the court's leading scholar.

sentences.zh: 不勸此兩人，當勸誰也！」

translations.literal: If I do not encourage these two men, whom should I encourage!
translations.idiomatic: If I do not reward these two men, whom else should I reward?

sentences.zh: 其見知若此。

translations.literal: Such was the degree to which he was known and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the measure of esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 初，孝文以李彪為散騎常侍，祚因入見，帝謂祚曰：「朕昨誤授一人官。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Xiaowen had appointed Li Biao Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary; when Zuo entered for an audience, the emperor said to Zuo, "Yesterday I mistakenly granted a man an office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had appointed Li Biao regular attendant-in-ordinary. When Zuo came in for an audience, the emperor told him, "Yesterday I mistakenly gave a man an appointment.

sentences.zh: 祚對曰：「豈容聖詔一行，而有差異！」

translations.literal: Zuo replied, "How could a sacred edict once issued admit any discrepancy!"
translations.idiomatic: Zuo replied, "Surely a sacred edict, once issued, cannot be altered!"

sentences.zh: 帝沈吟曰：「此自應有讓，因讓，朕欲別授一官。」

translations.literal: The emperor pondered and said, "This ought naturally to have a declination; through declination I wish to grant another office."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated and said, "He ought by rights to decline; once he declines, I mean to give him a different post."

sentences.zh: 須臾，彪有啟云：「伯石辭卿，子產所惡，臣欲之已久，不敢辭讓。」

translations.literal: In a moment Biao submitted a memorial saying, "Bo Shi declined the rank of minister—this is what Zichan hated; I have long desired the post and dare not decline."
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Biao submitted a memorial: "When Bo Shi refused the ministry, Zichan condemned him; I have wanted this post for a long time and dare not decline it."

sentences.zh: 帝歎謂祚曰：「卿之忠諫，李彪正辭，使朕遲回，不能復決。」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said to Zuo, "Your loyal remonstrance and Li Biao's upright words make me hesitate and unable to decide again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said to Zuo, "Your loyal counsel and Li Biao's forthright reply leave me unable to settle the matter."

sentences.zh: 遂不換李彪官也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not change Li Biao's office.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not change Li Biao's appointment.

sentences.zh: 乘輿南討，祚以兼侍中從，拜尚書，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Zuo followed as concurrent Palace Attendant and was appointed Minister; his enfeoffment was advanced to that of a count.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south on campaign, Zuo accompanied him as concurrent palace attendant, was appointed a minister, and advanced to the rank of count.

sentences.zh: 孝文崩，咸陽王禧等奏祚兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen died, the Prince of Xianyang, Xi, and others memorialized that Zuo should concurrently serve as Minister of the Ministry of Officials.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowen's death, the Prince of Xianyang, Xi, and others recommended that Zuo concurrently hold the post of minister of the ministry of officials.

sentences.zh: 尋除長兼吏部尚書、并州大中正。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed and made long-term concurrent Minister of the Ministry of Officials and Grand Rectifier of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was relieved of other duties and made long-term concurrent minister of the ministry of officials and grand rectifier of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣武詔以奸吏逃刑，縣配遠戍，若永避不出，兄弟代之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu decreed that corrupt officials who fled punishment should have their districts assigned to distant garrison duty, and if they forever avoided appearing, their brothers should replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu decreed that when corrupt officials fled to escape punishment, their home districts should be assigned to distant frontier service, and if they never came forward, their brothers should serve in their place.

sentences.zh: 祚奏曰：「若以奸吏逃竄，徙其兄弟，罪人妻子，復應徙之，此則一人之罪，禍傾二室。

translations.literal: Zuo memorialized, "If because corrupt officials flee their brothers are relocated, then the criminals' wives and children should also be relocated; thus one man's crime would bring disaster on two households.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo submitted a memorial: "If fleeing corrupt officials cause their brothers to be banished, then the criminals' wives and children must be banished as well—one man's offense would then ruin two families.

sentences.zh: 愚謂罪人既逃，止徙妻子，走者之身，縣名永配，於眚不免，奸途自塞。」

translations.literal: I humbly consider that once the criminal has fled, only his wife and children should be moved; the fugitive himself should have his name permanently registered for assignment in his district, so that he cannot escape guilt and the path of corruption is blocked.
translations.idiomatic: I suggest that once the guilty party has fled, only his wife and children be relocated; the fugitive's own name should remain permanently on the district rolls for assignment, so that he can never escape punishment and the road to corruption is closed.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The decree followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 尋正吏部。

translations.literal: Soon he was made regular Minister of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed regular minister of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 祚持身潔清，重惜官位。

translations.literal: Zuo maintained himself in purity and held office in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo conducted himself with scrupulous integrity and treasured his official position.

sentences.zh: 至於銓授，假令得人，必徘徊久之，然後下筆，下筆即云：「此人便以貴矣。」

translations.literal: As to appointments and conferrals, even when he had found the right man he would ponder a long time before setting brush to paper; once he wrote he would say, "This man is already ennobled.
translations.idiomatic: When making appointments, even after he had found the right candidate he would hesitate a long time before putting pen to paper, and once he wrote he would say, "This man is already raised in rank.

sentences.zh: 由是事頗稽滯，當時每招怨讟。

translations.literal: Because of this affairs were rather delayed, and at the time he often drew complaints.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason business often dragged on, and at the time he frequently drew complaints.

sentences.zh: 然所拔用者，皆量才稱職，時又以此歸之。

translations.literal: Yet those he promoted and employed were all measured for office according to talent, and the age for this reason also gave him credit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those he selected were all fitted to their posts by ability, and contemporaries for that reason also gave him credit.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、鎮北將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Commissioner with Imperial Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital as commissioner bearing the imperial staff, general who pacifies the north, and governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及太極殿成，祚朝于京師，轉鎮東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Hall of Supreme Ultimate was completed, Zuo attended court in the capital and was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hall of Supreme Ultimate was completed, Zuo came to court in the capital and was transferred to general who pacifies the east and governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 祚逢歲不稔，闔境饑弊，矜傷愛下，多所振恤，雖斷決淹留，號為煩緩，然士女懷其德澤。

translations.literal: Zuo encountered years of poor harvest; the whole region was hungry and distressed; he pitied and cared for those below and gave much relief, and although his judgments were delayed and he was called troublesome and slow, yet men and women cherished his benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: His tenure coincided with famine; the whole province was hungry and destitute. He showed compassion for the people and gave extensive relief. Though his legal decisions were slow and he was criticized as dilatory, the common people cherished his kindness.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中、金紫光祿大夫、并州大中正。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Palace Attendant, Grand Master for the Golden Bell and Purple Canopy, and Grand Rectifier of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as palace attendant, grand master for the golden bell and purple canopy, and grand rectifier of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice director of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 時議定新令，詔祚與侍中、黃門參議刊正。

translations.literal: At that time the new statutes were being deliberated, and the emperor ordered Zuo, together with palace attendants and the yellow gate, to participate in discussion and revision.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a new code was under discussion, and the emperor ordered Zuo, together with palace attendants and officials of the yellow gate, to join in revising it.

sentences.zh: 故事，令、僕、中丞騶唱而入宮門，至於馬道。

translations.literal: By precedent, directors, vice directors, and the imperial censor were announced by outriders as they entered the palace gate, up to the horse road.
translations.idiomatic: By long-standing custom, directors, vice directors, and the imperial censor were heralded by outriders from the palace gate all the way to the horse road.

sentences.zh: 及祚為僕射，以為非盡敬之宜，言於帝，納之。

translations.literal: When Zuo became vice director, he considered this not fully proper to reverence and spoke to the emperor, who accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuo became vice director, he held that this was not fully proper to reverence and spoke to the emperor, who agreed.

sentences.zh: 下詔禦在太極，騶唱至止車門；

translations.literal: An edict was issued: when the emperor was in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, the outriders should announce only to the carriage-halting gate;
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued: when the emperor was in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, the outriders should announce only as far as the carriage-halting gate;

sentences.zh: 禦在朝堂，至司馬門。

translations.literal: when the emperor was in the audience hall, only to the Sima Gate.
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor was in the audience hall, only as far as the Sima Gate.

sentences.zh: 騶唱不入宮，自此始也。

translations.literal: Outriders not entering the palace began from this.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward outriders no longer entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 詔祚本官領太子少師。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zuo to retain his original office and concurrently serve as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zuo to keep his existing post and also serve as junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 祚曾從幸東宮，明帝幼弱，祚持一黃㼐出奉之。

translations.literal: Zuo once followed in attendance at the Eastern Palace; Emperor Ming was still young, and Zuo took out a yellow pear and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo once accompanied the emperor to the Eastern Palace. Emperor Ming was still a child, and Zuo brought out a yellow pear and offered it to him.

sentences.zh: 時應詔左右趙桃弓與御史中尉王顯迭相脣齒，深為帝所信，祚私事之，時人謗祚者，號為桃弓僕射、黃㼐少師。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Taogong of the attendants at imperial command and Wang Xian, Imperial Censor, took turns as each other's mouthpiece and were deeply trusted by the emperor; Zuo privately cultivated them, and those who slandered Zuo at the time called him Vice Director Taogong and Junior Tutor Yellow Pear.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao Taogong, an attendant at imperial command, and Wang Xian, the imperial censor, backed each other in court and enjoyed the emperor's deep trust. Zuo cultivated them in private, and critics nicknamed him Vice Director Taogong and Junior Tutor Yellow Pear.

sentences.zh: 祚奏曰：「謹案前後考格，雖班天下，如臣愚短，猶有未悟。

translations.literal: Zuo memorialized, "I respectfully examine the former and present examination regulations, though promulgated throughout the realm, yet such as my dull shortness still has points not understood.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo submitted a memorial: "I have reviewed the examination regulations issued in former times and at present. Though they have been promulgated throughout the realm, one as dull as I still finds points that remain unclear.

sentences.zh: 今須定職人遷轉由狀，超越階級者即須量折。

translations.literal: Now it is necessary to fix the transfer of regular officials by dossier; those who leap over ranks must have their grades reduced accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: We must now fix how regular officials are transferred on the basis of their dossiers, and those who skip ranks must have their seniority reduced accordingly.

sentences.zh: 景明初考格，五年者得一階半。

translations.literal: In the examination regulations at the beginning of the Jingming era, after five years one gained one and a half ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jingming examination rules, after five years one advanced one and a half ranks.

sentences.zh: 正始中，故尚書、中山王英奏考格，被旨：「但可正滿三周為限，不得計殘年之勤。」

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era, the former Minister and Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, memorialized on the examination regulations and received the imperial rescript: "Only a full three cycles may serve as the limit; partial years of service must not be counted."
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era the former minister and Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, submitted regulations and received the rescript: 'Only three full cycles may count as the limit; leftover years of service may not be tallied.'

sentences.zh: 又去年中，以前二制不同，奏請裁決。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the middle of last year, because the two former systems differed, a memorial was submitted requesting a decision.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, midway through last year, because the two earlier systems differed, a memorial was submitted asking for a ruling.

sentences.zh: 旨云：「黜陟之體，知依舊來恆斷。」

translations.literal: The rescript said, "The substance of promotion and demotion is to be decided according to the constant practice of old."
translations.idiomatic: "The rescript stated: 'The principles of promotion and demotion are to follow the standing practice of former times.'"

sentences.zh: 今未審舊來之旨，為從景明之斷？

translations.literal: Now I do not yet ascertain whether the intent of former times follows the Jingming ruling,
translations.idiomatic: I am still uncertain whether the intent of former times is to follow the Jingming ruling,

sentences.zh: 為從正始為限？

translations.literal: or takes the Zhengshi limit?
translations.idiomatic: or to apply the Zhengshi limit?

sentences.zh: 景明考法，東西省文武閑官悉為三等，考同任事。

translations.literal: The Jingming examination method ranked all civil and military idle offices of the eastern and western secretariats in three grades, examining them the same as active posts.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jingming method, all civil and military sinecures of the eastern and western secretariats were placed in three grades and examined on the same footing as active posts.

sentences.zh: 而前尚書盧昶奏，上等之人三年轉半階。

translations.literal: Yet the former Minister Lu Chang memorialized that men of the upper grade should advance half a rank in three years.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the former minister Lu Chang memorialized that those in the upper grade should advance half a rank every three years.

sentences.zh: 今之考格，復分為九等，前後不同，參差無准。」

translations.literal: The present examination regulations again divide into nine grades; former and present differ, without uniform standard.
translations.idiomatic: The present regulations again divide candidates into nine grades; the earlier and later systems conflict and lack a single standard.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「考在上中者，得泛以前，有六年以上遷一階，三年以上遷半階，殘年悉除。

translations.literal: The edict said, "Those whose examination is upper-middle may, counting broadly from before, advance one rank after six or more years and half a rank after three or more years; leftover years are all struck.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Those rated upper-middle may, counting broadly from earlier service, advance one full rank after six or more years and half a rank after three or more years; partial years are all disregarded.

sentences.zh: 考在上下者，得泛以前，六年以上遷半階，不滿者除。

translations.literal: Those whose examination is upper-lower may, counting broadly from before, advance half a rank after six or more years; those not reaching this are struck.
translations.idiomatic: Those rated upper-lower may, counting broadly from earlier service, advance half a rank after six or more years; those who fall short are disregarded.

sentences.zh: 其得泛以後，考在上下者，三年遷一階。

translations.literal: After they may count broadly, those whose examination is upper-lower advance one rank in three years.
translations.idiomatic: Once they may count broadly from earlier service, those rated upper-lower advance one rank every three years.

sentences.zh: 散官從盧昶所奏。」

translations.literal: Idle offices follow what Lu Chang memorialized."
translations.idiomatic: Sinecure officials follow Lu Chang's memorial."

sentences.zh: 祚又奏言：「考察令：公清獨著、德績超倫而無負殿者為上上，一殿為上中，二殿為上下，累計八殿，品降至九。

translations.literal: Zuo again memorialized, saying, "The examination ordinance states: upper-upper is for those whose public purity is uniquely manifest and whose virtue and achievement surpass the norm without any demerit marks; one demerit mark is upper-middle, two are upper-lower, and accumulating eight marks reduces the grade to nine.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo submitted again: "The examination ordinance states that upper-upper is for those of outstanding public integrity whose virtue and achievement surpass the norm without a single demerit mark; one mark is upper-middle, two are upper-lower, and eight accumulated marks reduce the grade to the ninth.

sentences.zh: 未審今諸曹府寺，凡考，在事公清，然才非獨著；

translations.literal: I do not yet ascertain whether, in the examinations of all the bureaus and directorates in general, those who in office are publicly pure yet whose talent is not uniquely manifest;
translations.idiomatic: I am still unclear whether, in the examinations of all bureaus and directorates, an official who is publicly upright in office yet whose talent is not uniquely outstanding;

sentences.zh: 績行稱務，而德非超倫；

translations.literal: whose achievement and conduct answer to their duties yet whose virtue does not surpass the norm;
translations.idiomatic: whose performance meets his duties yet whose virtue does not surpass the norm;

sentences.zh: 幹能粗可，而守平堪任；

translations.literal: whose competence is roughly adequate and who in keeping office is equal to the task;
translations.idiomatic: whose competence is roughly adequate and who can hold office competently;

sentences.zh: 或人用小劣，處官濟事並全無負殿之徒：為依何第？

translations.literal: or men with slight petty faults who yet in office accomplish affairs and altogether have no demerit marks—under what grade should they be placed?
translations.idiomatic: or men with minor faults who nonetheless accomplish their work in office and have no demerit marks at all—under which grade should they be placed?

sentences.zh: 景明三年以來，至今十有一載，准限而判，三應升退。

translations.literal: From the third year of Jingming until now there have been eleven years; judged by the standard limit, there should have been three promotions or demotions.
translations.idiomatic: From the third year of Jingming until now eleven years have passed; by the standard term there should have been three rounds of promotion or demotion.

sentences.zh: 今既通考，未審為十年之中，通其殿最，積以為第？

translations.literal: Now that examinations are unified, I do not yet ascertain whether, within the ten years, their demerit marks should be totaled to form the grade,
translations.idiomatic: Now that examinations are unified, I do not know whether, within those ten years, demerit marks should be totaled to determine the grade,

sentences.zh: 隨前後年斷，各自除其善惡而為升降？

translations.literal: or whether each preceding and following year should be judged separately, each clearing its good and bad to form promotion or demotion?
translations.idiomatic: or whether each year should be judged on its own, with good and bad struck separately to determine promotion or demotion?

sentences.zh: 且負注之章，數成殿為差，此條以寡愆為最，多戾為殿。

translations.literal: Moreover, the article on demerit marks counts several marks forming a demerit; this article takes few faults as best and many offenses as demerit.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the article on demerit marks counts a set number of faults as one mark; it treats few faults as best and many offenses as demerits.

sentences.zh: 未審取何行是寡愆？

translations.literal: I do not yet ascertain what conduct counts as few faults?
translations.idiomatic: I do not yet know what conduct counts as few faults,

sentences.zh: 何坐為多戾？

translations.literal: What offense counts as many violations?
translations.idiomatic: or what offenses count as many violations?

sentences.zh: 結累品次，復有幾等？

translations.literal: When grades are totaled, how many grades are there again?
translations.idiomatic: When grades are totaled, how many grades are there in all?

sentences.zh: 諸文案失衷應杖十者為一負，罪依律次，過隨負記。

translations.literal: Documents and cases that miss the standard and merit ten blows count as one demerit; offenses follow the sequence of the law, and excess passes with the demerit record.
translations.idiomatic: For documents and cases that miss the standard and merit ten blows of the staff, one counts as one demerit; offenses follow the gradations of the law, and excess is recorded with the demerit.

sentences.zh: 十年之中，三經肆眚，赦前之罪，不問輕重，皆蒙宥免。

translations.literal: Within ten years there were three general amnesties; offenses before the amnesty, regardless of severity, all received pardon and exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten years there have been three general amnesties; offenses before an amnesty, regardless of severity, were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 或為御史所彈，案驗未周，遇赦復任者，未審記殿得除以不？」

translations.literal: Or if impeached by the censor, the case not yet fully investigated, and on meeting an amnesty he is reappointed—whether demerit marks may be struck is not yet clear?
translations.idiomatic: Or if an official is impeached by the censor, the case is not yet fully investigated, and he is reappointed after an amnesty—may his demerit marks be struck off or not?

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「獨著、超倫及才備、寡咎，皆謂文武兼上上之極言耳。

translations.literal: The edict said, "Uniquely manifest, surpassing the norm, and talent complete with few faults—all refer to the utmost words for civil and military upper-upper together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Uniquely outstanding merit, surpassing the norm, and full talent with few faults are terms reserved for the highest civil and military grade together.

sentences.zh: 自此以降，猶有八等，隨才為次，令文已具。

translations.literal: From this downward there are still eight grades, following talent in order; the text is already complete.
translations.idiomatic: Below that there are still eight grades, arranged according to ability; the regulations already set this forth.

sentences.zh: 其積負累殿及守平得濟，皆含在其中，何容別疑也？

translations.literal: Those who accumulate demerit marks, hold office adequately, and accomplish affairs are all included within this; how can there be separate doubt?
translations.idiomatic: Those who accumulate demerit marks yet hold office adequately and get their work done are all covered by these rules—there is no room for separate doubt.

sentences.zh: 所雲通考者，據總多年之言。

translations.literal: What is called unified examination refers to language summing many years.
translations.idiomatic: What is meant by unified examination is a reckoning across many years.

sentences.zh: 至於黜陟之體，自依舊來年斷，何足復請。

translations.literal: As to the substance of promotion and demotion, it naturally follows the annual judgments of old; what need is there to request again?
translations.idiomatic: As for promotion and demotion, that still follows the annual judgments of former practice—there is no need to ask again.

sentences.zh: 其罰贖已決之殿，固非免限。

translations.literal: Demerit marks for fines and redemption already decided are certainly not within the exemption limit.
translations.idiomatic: Demerit marks for fines and commutations already settled are certainly not subject to exemption.

sentences.zh: 遇赦免罪，准其殿者除之。

translations.literal: When an amnesty remits the offense, demerit marks that may be struck are removed.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty pardons the offense, eligible demerit marks are struck off.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally appointed regular attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 時詔營明堂、國學，祚奏曰：「今雲羅西舉，開納岷、蜀；

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered the building of the Bright Hall and the Imperial Academy; Zuo memorialized, "Now clouds of banners advance west, opening Min and Shu to submission;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court ordered construction of the Bright Hall and the Imperial Academy. Zuo memorialized: "The banners now advance westward, bringing Min and Shu into the fold;

sentences.zh: 戎旗東指，鎮靖淮、荊；

translations.literal: military flags point east, pacifying Huai and Jing;
translations.idiomatic: military standards point east to pacify the Huai and Jing regions;

sentences.zh: 漢、沔之間，復須防捍。

translations.literal: between Han and Mian defense must again be maintained.
translations.idiomatic: between the Han and Mian rivers defense must again be maintained.

sentences.zh: 徵兵發眾，所在殷廣。

translations.literal: Recruiting soldiers and sending out masses—the places everywhere are heavily burdened.
translations.idiomatic: Recruitment is heavy everywhere.

sentences.zh: 邊郊多壘，烽驛未息，不可于師旅之際，興板築之功。

translations.literal: On the border ramparts many forts; beacon fires have not ceased—it is not possible amid armies to raise works of timber and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier fortresses are many and beacon fires have not ceased; we cannot launch major construction in the midst of military campaigns.

sentences.zh: 且獻歲雲暨，東作將始。

translations.literal: Moreover the offering year has come, and eastern labor is about to begin.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the new year has arrived and spring planting is about to begin.

sentences.zh: 臣愚量謂宜待豐靖之年，因數來之力，可不時而就。」

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly considers that we should wait for a year of abundance and, relying on the strength of several years, may complete it without delay.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly suggest waiting for a year of peace and plenty, when the labor of several good harvests can finish the work in good time.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 宣武末年，每引祚入東宮，密受賞賚，多至百餘萬，雜以錦繡。

translations.literal: In the last years of Emperor Xuanwu he often summoned Zuo into the Eastern Palace and secretly bestowed rewards, often reaching more than a million, mixed with brocades.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xuanwu's last years he often summoned Zuo to the Eastern Palace and secretly rewarded him, sometimes with more than a million in cash along with brocades.

sentences.zh: 又特賜以劍杖，恩寵甚深。

translations.literal: He was also specially granted sword and staff—favor and grace were very deep.
translations.idiomatic: He was also specially granted the sword and staff of honor, tokens of exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 遷左僕射。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left vice director of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 先是，梁將康絢遏淮，將灌揚、徐。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Liang general Kang Xuan blocked the Huai and was about to inundate Yang and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Liang general Kang Xuan had blocked the Huai River and was about to flood Yang and Xu.

sentences.zh: 祚表曰：「蕭衍狂狡，擅斷川瀆，役苦人勞，危亡已兆。

translations.literal: Zuo memorialized, "Xiao Yan is mad and crafty, arrogantly cutting off rivers and channels; the people labor in bitterness, and signs of peril and ruin already appear.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo submitted a memorial: "Xiao Yan is reckless and deceitful, arrogantly diverting rivers; the people labor in misery and the signs of collapse are already plain.

sentences.zh: 宜敕揚州選一猛將，遣當州之兵，令赴浮山，表裹夾攻。」

translations.literal: We should order Yangzhou to select a fierce general and send troops of that province to rush to Fushan for a pincer attack inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: The court should order Yangzhou to choose a fierce general and dispatch that province's troops to Fushan for a coordinated attack from both sides.

sentences.zh: 朝議從之。

translations.literal: Court discussion followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his plan.

sentences.zh: 除使持節、散騎常侍、都督、雍州刺史、征西將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commissioner with Imperial Staff, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander, Governor of Yongzhou, and General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commissioner bearing the imperial staff, regular attendant-in-ordinary, commander, governor of Yongzhou, and general who pacifies the west.

sentences.zh: 太和以前，朝法尤峻，貴臣蹉跌，便致誅夷。

translations.literal: Before the Taihe era court law was especially severe; if eminent ministers stumbled they were at once executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Taihe era court law was especially harsh: when eminent ministers stumbled they were immediately put to death.

sentences.zh: 李沖之用事也，欽祚識幹，薦為左丞，又兼黃門，意便滿足。

translations.literal: When Li Chong wielded power he admired Zuo's knowledge and competence, recommended him as left assistant director, and also as Yellow Gate; Zuo was then content.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chong held power he admired Zuo's ability, recommended him as left assistant director and also to the yellow gate, and Zuo was satisfied.

sentences.zh: 每以孤門，往經崔氏之禍，常慮危亡，苦自陳挹，辭色懇然，發於誠至。

translations.literal: Because he was a lone household that had passed through the calamity of the Cui clan, he always feared ruin and painfully humbled himself; his words and bearing were earnest, arising from sincere feeling.
translations.idiomatic: As the lone survivor of a family that had suffered the Cui clan disaster, he constantly feared destruction and humbled himself earnestly, his words and manner born of genuine feeling.

sentences.zh: 沖謂之曰：「人生有運，非可避也。

translations.literal: Chong said to him, "Life has fortune; it cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Chong told him, "Fortune has its turns; they cannot be evaded.

sentences.zh: 但當明白當官，何所顧畏。」

translations.literal: Only hold office with clarity—what is there to fear?
translations.idiomatic: Only serve in office with integrity—what is there to dread?

sentences.zh: 自是積十數年，位秩隆重，而進趣之心，更復不息。

translations.literal: From this for more than ten years his rank and position were weighty, yet his heart's drive for advancement never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years after that his rank grew weighty, yet his ambition for advancement never slackened.

sentences.zh: 又以東宮師傅之資，列辭尚書，志在封侯之賞，儀同之位。

translations.literal: Moreover, with the qualification of tutor of the Eastern Palace, he repeatedly declined the Ministry, his aim the reward of enfeoffment and the rank of Palace Equal to Three Lords.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on his post as tutor of the Eastern Palace, he repeatedly petitioned to leave the ministry, aiming at enfeoffment and the rank of palace equal to the three lords.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、任城王澄為之奏聞。

translations.literal: The Minister, the Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, memorialized this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works and Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, submitted the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 及為征西、雍州，雖喜外撫，尚以府號不優，心望加大。

translations.literal: When he became General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yongzhou, though pleased with external command, he still thought the title of his headquarters inferior and inwardly hoped for something greater.
translations.idiomatic: When he became general who pacifies the west and governor of Yongzhou, though glad of field command, he still found his headquarters title inadequate and inwardly hoped for greater honors.

sentences.zh: 執政者頗怪之。

translations.literal: Those in power were rather displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power were displeased.

sentences.zh: 于時領軍於忠恃寵驕恣，崔光之徒，曲躬承接。

translations.literal: At that time the Commander-in-Chief Yu Zhong relied on favor and was arrogant and unrestrained; Cui Guang and his sort bowed and received him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Commander-in-Chief Yu Zhong, relying on imperial favor, was arrogant and overbearing, while Cui Guang and others bowed and flattered him.

sentences.zh: 祚心惡之，乃遣子太尉從事中郎景尚說高陽王雍，令出忠為州。

translations.literal: Zuo hated this in his heart and sent his son Jingshang, attendant of the Grand Commandant, to persuade the Prince of Gaoyang, Yong, to have Zhong sent out as governor of a province.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo detested this and sent his son Jingshang, an attendant of the grand commandant, to persuade the Prince of Gaoyang, Yong, to have Zhong posted out as provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 忠聞而大怒，矯詔殺祚。

translations.literal: Zhong heard of it and was greatly enraged; he forged an edict and killed Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong learned of it he was furious and forged an edict to have Zuo executed.

sentences.zh: 祚達於政事。

translations.literal: Zuo was adept at government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo was skilled in administration.

sentences.zh: 凡所經履，咸為稱職，每有斷決，多為故事。

translations.literal: Whatever posts he passed through he fully answered to his duties; whenever he made a decision it often became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held he performed competently, and many of his decisions became precedents.

sentences.zh: 名器既重，時望亦深，一朝非罪見害，遠近莫不惋惜。

translations.literal: His name and vessels were already weighty and contemporary expectation was also deep; one morning he was harmed without crime, and near and far alike mourned.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation and rank were already great and public expectation ran high; when he was killed without cause in a single morning, men near and far alike grieved.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，遣使吊慰，追復伯爵。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court she sent envoys to offer condolences and posthumously restored his countly rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling assumed regency she sent envoys to mourn him and posthumously restored his countly title.

sentences.zh: 正光中，贈使持節、車騎將軍、儀同三司、雍州刺史，諡文貞公。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era he was posthumously granted Commissioner with Imperial Staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Palace Equal to Three Lords, and Governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous title Duke Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengguang era he was posthumously granted commissioner with the imperial staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry, palace equal to the three lords, and governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous title Duke Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 初，孝文之置中正，從容謂祚曰：「并州中正，卿家故應推王瓊也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Xiaowen established the Rectifiers, he said at leisure to Zuo, "For Rectifier of Bingzhou, your family ought naturally to recommend Wang Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Xiaowen established the rectifier system, he remarked to Zuo at leisure, "For rectifier of Bingzhou your family ought to recommend Wang Qiong.

sentences.zh: 祚退謂寮友曰：「瓊真偽今自未辨，我家何為減之？

translations.literal: Zuo withdrew and told his colleagues, "Whether Qiong is genuine or false is not yet distinguished—why should my family be reduced? Yet the sovereign simply believes Li Chong's boasting.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo withdrew and told his colleagues, "Whether Qiong is truly worthy is still unclear—why should my family be demoted? The emperor simply believes Li Chong's flattery.

sentences.zh: 然主上直信李沖吹噓之說耳。」

translations.literal: Yet the sovereign simply believed Li Chong's boasting.
translations.idiomatic: In truth the emperor simply trusted Li Chong's self-promotion."

sentences.zh: 祚死後三歲而於忠死，見祚為祟。

translations.literal: Three years after Zuo's death Yu Zhong died, seeing Zuo as a malign spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Three years after Zuo's death Yu Zhong died, claiming he was haunted by Zuo's spirit.

sentences.zh: 祚子景尚，字思和。

translations.literal: Zuo's son Jingshang, styled Sihe.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo's son Jingshang, whose style name was Sihe.

sentences.zh: 涉曆書傳，曉星曆占候，言事頗驗。

translations.literal: He ranged through books and records, understood star calendars and divination, and his predictions of affairs were often verified.
translations.idiomatic: He studied books and histories, understood astronomy and divination, and his predictions often proved correct.

sentences.zh: 初為彭城王中軍府參軍，遷員外郎、司徒主簿、太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: At first he was an aide in the Prince of Pengcheng's central army headquarters, promoted to outer court gentleman, chief clerk of the Ministry, and attendant of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as an aide in the Prince of Pengcheng's central army headquarters, then was promoted to outer court gentleman, chief clerk of the ministry, and attendant of the grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 公強當世，善事權寵，世號曰郭尖。

translations.literal: He was overbearing in his generation, good at courting power and favor, and the age called him Guo the Sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Overbearing in his day and skilled at courting power, his contemporaries called him Guo the Sharp.

sentences.zh: 位中書侍郎，未拜而卒。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Gentleman of the Secretariat but died before assuming office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to gentleman of the Secretariat but died before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 景尚弟慶禮，位通直郎。

translations.literal: Jingshang's younger brother Qingli held the post of Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshang's younger brother Qingli served as direct attendant.

sentences.zh: 慶禮子元貞，武定末，定州驃騎府長史。

translations.literal: Qingli's son Yuanzhen, at the end of the Wuding era, was chief clerk of the Rapid Cavalry Headquarters of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qingli's son Yuanzhen, at the end of the Wuding era, was chief clerk of the rapid cavalry headquarters of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 張彝，字慶賓，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, styled Qingbin, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, whose style name was Qingbin, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 曾祖幸，慕容超東牟太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xing was Governor of Dongmou under Murong Chao.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xing had been governor of Dongmou under Murong Chao.

sentences.zh: 歸魏，賜爵平陸侯，位青州刺史。

translations.literal: He submitted to Wei and was granted the title Marquis of Pinglu, holding the post of Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted to Wei and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pinglu and appointed governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖准之襲，又為東青州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhun inherited, and again served as Governor of Eastern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhun inherited the title and also served as governor of Eastern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父靈真，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Lingzhen died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingzhen died young.

sentences.zh: 彝性公強有風氣，曆覽經史，襲祖侯爵。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was upright and forceful with spirit; he ranged through the classics and histories and inherited his grandfather's marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was upright and forceful by nature, steeped himself in the classics and histories, and inherited his grandfather's marquisate.

sentences.zh: 與盧陽烏、李安人等結為親友，往來朝會，常相追隨。

translations.literal: He formed close friendship with Lu Yangwu, Li Anren, and others; at court assemblies they often followed one another.
translations.idiomatic: He formed close friendships with Lu Yangwu, Li Anren, and others and at court assemblies they were often seen together.

sentences.zh: 陽烏為主客令，安人與彝並散令。

translations.literal: Yangwu was Director of Guests; Anren and Yi were both outer court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yangwu was director of guests; Anren and Yi were both outer court gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 彝少而豪放，出入殿庭，步眄高上，無所顧忌。

translations.literal: Yi in youth was bold and unrestrained; entering and leaving the palace halls he walked with raised gaze and high step, without regard for anything.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yi was bold and unrestrained; entering and leaving the palace halls he walked with head high and gaze proud, heedless of all restraint.

sentences.zh: 文明太后雅尚恭謹，因會次見其如此，遂召集百寮督責之，令其修悔，而猶無悛改。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming valued respectful caution; at a gathering she saw him thus, then summoned the hundred officials and reproved him, ordering him to reform, yet he still did not repent.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming prized respectful conduct; seeing him behave so at an assembly, she summoned the officials and rebuked him, ordering him to reform, yet he still would not change.

sentences.zh: 善於督察，每有所巡檢，彝常充其選，清慎嚴猛，所至人皆畏伏，儔燈亦以此高之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at inspection; whenever there was a tour of inspection Yi was often chosen; pure, cautious, and stern, wherever he went people all feared and submitted, and his peers for this also held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at inspection and was often chosen for tours of investigation; pure, cautious, and stern, he inspired fear wherever he went, and his peers respected him for it.

sentences.zh: 遷主客令，例降侯為伯，轉太中大夫，仍行主客曹事，尋為黃門。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of Guests; by precedent the marquisate was reduced to a count, he was made Grand Master of the Palace, still administered the Bureau of Guests, and soon became Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of guests; by precedent his marquisate was reduced to a count, he was made grand master of the palace, continued to administer the bureau of guests, and soon entered the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 後從駕南征，母憂解任。

translations.literal: Later he followed the southern campaign; on his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accompanied the southern campaign; when his mother died he resigned.

sentences.zh: 彝居喪過禮，送葬自平城達家，千里步從，不乘車馬，顏貌瘦瘠，當世稱之。

translations.literal: Yi's mourning exceeded the rites; escorting the funeral from Pingcheng to his home, a thousand li on foot without riding horse or carriage, his face haggard—the age praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His mourning observances exceeded the prescribed rites; he walked a thousand li escorting the coffin from Pingcheng home without riding, his face gaunt, and contemporaries praised him.

sentences.zh: 孝文幸冀州，遣使吊慰，詔以驍騎將軍起之，還復本位。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen visited Jizhou, sent envoys to offer condolences, and ordered him raised as General of Valiant Cavalry and restored to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen visited Jizhou, sent envoys to condole with him, and ordered him recalled as general of valiant cavalry and restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 以參定遷都之勳，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: For his merit in settling the transfer of the capital he was advanced in enfeoffment to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: For his contribution to establishing the capital transfer he was advanced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 轉太常少卿，遷散騎常侍，兼侍中，持節巡察陝東河南十二州，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Palace Attendant, and with imperial staff inspected the twelve provinces east of Shan and south of the River, winning great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices, then regular attendant-in-ordinary and concurrent palace attendant, and with imperial staff inspected twelve provinces east of Shan and south of the River, winning great renown.

sentences.zh: 使還，以從征之勤，遷尚書。

translations.literal: On his return, for merit on the campaign he was promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to minister for his campaign service.

sentences.zh: 坐舉元昭為兼郎中，黜為守尚書。

translations.literal: He sat in office for recommending Yuan Zhao as concurrent Bureau Director and was demoted to Acting Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was penalized for recommending Yuan Zhao as concurrent bureau director and was demoted to acting minister.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，除正尚書，兼侍中，尋正侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu he was made regular Minister and concurrently Palace Attendant, and soon regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made regular minister and concurrent palace attendant, and soon regular palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 宣武親政，罷六輔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu personally took power he dismissed the Six Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu assumed personal rule he dismissed the six assistants.

sentences.zh: 彝與兼尚書邢巒聞處分非常，懼，出京奔走。

translations.literal: Yi and Concurrent Minister Xing Luan heard the disposition was extraordinary and, in fear, fled the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and concurrent minister Xing Luan heard that the measures were extraordinary and fled the capital in fear.

sentences.zh: 為御史中尉甄琛所彈，云「非武非兕，率彼曠野。」

translations.literal: They were impeached by Imperial Censor Zhong Zhen, who said, "Neither bull nor rhinoceros—he leads them through the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial censor Zhen impeached them, quoting the ode: "Not bull, not rhinoceros—yet he drives them through the wild.

sentences.zh: 詔書切責之。

translations.literal: An edict sternly reproved them.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict sternly rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 尋除安西將軍、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed general who pacifies the west and governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 彝務尚典式，考訪故事，及臨隴右，彌加討習。

translations.literal: Yi devoted himself to canonical forms, investigated and sought out precedents, and on reaching Longyou he applied himself even more to study.
translations.idiomatic: Yi devoted himself to ritual forms, researched precedents, and on reaching Longyou applied himself even more to study.

sentences.zh: 於是出入直衛，方伯羽儀，赫然可觀。

translations.literal: Thereupon his coming and going with straight guards and the feathered insignia of regional lords were splendid to behold.
translations.idiomatic: His retinue of guards and the feathered banners of a regional lord made a splendid display.

sentences.zh: 羌、夏畏伏，憚其威整；

translations.literal: The Qiang and Xia feared and submitted, dreading his stern discipline;
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang and Xia submitted in awe of his stern discipline;

sentences.zh: 一方肅靜，號為良牧。

translations.literal: the whole region was quieted and he was called a good governor.
translations.idiomatic: the whole region was pacified and he was hailed as an excellent governor.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，太極初就，彝與郭祚等俱以勤舊被征。

translations.literal: That winter, when the Hall of Supreme Ultimate was first completed, Yi together with Guo Zuo and others were all summoned for long service.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the Hall of Supreme Ultimate was first completed, Yi was summoned to court with Guo Zuo and others as veterans of long service.

sentences.zh: 及還州，進號撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: On returning to his province his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to his province his title was advanced to general who pacifies the army.

sentences.zh: 彝表解州任，詔不許。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized to resign his provincial post; the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi petitioned to resign his provincial post; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 彝敷政隴右，多所制立，宣佈新風，革其舊俗，人庶愛仰之。

translations.literal: Yi spread government in Longyou and established many regulations, proclaiming new customs and reforming old ways; the people loved and looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi governed Longyou extensively, establishing many regulations, proclaiming new customs and reforming old ways; the people admired him.

sentences.zh: 為國造佛寺，名曰興皇，諸有罪咎者，隨其輕重，謫為土木之功，無復鞭杖之罰。

translations.literal: For the state he built a Buddhist temple called Xinghuang; those guilty of offenses, according to severity, were sentenced to labor in earth and timber, and the punishment of staff and whip was no more.
translations.idiomatic: He built a Buddhist temple for the state called Xinghuang; offenders were sentenced according to severity to labor on the building instead of corporal punishment.

sentences.zh: 時陳留公主寡居，彝意願尚主，主亦許之。

translations.literal: At that time the Princess of Chenliu was a widow; Yi wished to marry her and the princess also consented.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Princess of Chenliu was widowed; Yi wished to marry her and she agreed.

sentences.zh: 僕射高肇亦望尚主，主意不可。

translations.literal: Vice Director Gao Zhao also hoped to marry the princess; the princess's intent could not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Gao Zhao also sought to marry her, but the princess would not change her mind.

sentences.zh: 肇怒，譖彝擅立刑法，勞役百姓，詔遣直後萬貳興馳驛檢察。

translations.literal: Zhao was enraged and slandered Yi for arrogantly establishing penal law and overworking the people; an edict sent Direct Attendant Wan Erxing post-haste to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was furious and accused Yi of arrogantly imposing penal laws and overworking the people; the emperor sent Direct Attendant Wan Erxing post-haste to investigate.

sentences.zh: 貳興，肇所親愛，必欲致彝深罪。

translations.literal: Erxing was beloved of Zhao and was certain to bring Yi to deep guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Erxing was Zhao's favorite and was determined to convict Yi of serious crimes.

sentences.zh: 彝清身奉法，求其愆過，遂無所得。

translations.literal: Yi maintained himself in purity and observed the law; seeking his faults, in the end nothing was found.
translations.idiomatic: Yi conducted himself with integrity and obeyed the law; though they searched for faults, they found none.

sentences.zh: 見代還洛，猶停廢數年。

translations.literal: When he was replaced and returned to Luoyang he was still suspended for several years.
translations.idiomatic: When he was recalled to Luoyang he remained in suspension for several years.

sentences.zh: 因得偏風，手腳不便；

translations.literal: He then suffered hemiplegia and his hands and feet were inconvenient;
translations.idiomatic: He then suffered a paralytic stroke that left his hands and feet impaired;

sentences.zh: 然志性不移，善自將攝，稍能朝拜。

translations.literal: yet his will and nature did not change; he was good at caring for himself and gradually could attend court.
translations.idiomatic: yet his spirit did not change; he cared for himself diligently and gradually resumed court attendance.

sentences.zh: 久之，除光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed grand master for splendid happiness with the golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 彝愛好知己，輕忽下流，非其意者，視之蔑爾。

translations.literal: Yi loved and valued those who knew him; he lightly regarded those below him, and those not to his liking he looked upon with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: He cherished his friends and looked down on social inferiors; those he disliked he treated with open contempt.

sentences.zh: 雖疹疾家庭，而志氣彌高。

translations.literal: Although illness afflicted his household, his spirit grew ever higher.
translations.idiomatic: Though illness troubled his household, his spirit only grew more exalted.

sentences.zh: 上《曆帝圖》五卷，起元庖犧，終於晉末，凡十六代，一百二十八帝，曆三千二百七十年，雜事五百八十九。

translations.literal: He submitted the Record of Imperial Calendars in five scrolls, from the primal sovereign Paoxi down to the end of Jin—altogether sixteen dynasties, one hundred twenty-eight emperors, spanning three thousand two hundred seventy years, with five hundred eighty-nine miscellaneous entries.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the Record of Imperial Calendars in five scrolls, from the primal sovereign Paoxi down to the end of Jin—sixteen dynasties, one hundred twenty-eight emperors, three thousand two hundred seventy years, and five hundred eighty-nine supplementary entries.

sentences.zh: 宣武善之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu approved the work.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，侍中崔光表：「彝及李韶，朝列之中，唯此二人，出身官次，本在臣右，器能幹世，又並為多。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, Palace Attendant Cui Guang memorialized, "Yi and Li Shao, among the court ranks, only these two men—in birth, office, and seniority—were originally above your servant; in talent and ability to govern the age they likewise excel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Ming's reign, Palace Attendant Cui Guang submitted a memorial: "Among the court, Zhang Yi and Li Shao alone, in birth, seniority, and original rank, stood above me; both are capable men who can govern their age.

sentences.zh: 而近來參差，便成替後。

translations.literal: Yet recently the order has been disturbed and they have been placed behind.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately the order of precedence has been upset and they have been ranked behind others.

sentences.zh: 計其階途，雖應遷陟，然恐班秩，猶未賜等。

translations.literal: Considering their career stages, though they ought to be promoted, I fear their grades and ranks have not yet been granted equally.
translations.idiomatic: By their careers they deserve promotion, yet I fear their grades and ranks have not been made equal.

sentences.zh: 昔衛之公叔，引下同舉；

translations.literal: Formerly in Wei, Gongsun of Wei drew those below him up to share advancement;
translations.idiomatic: In ancient Wei, Gongsun drew his inferiors up to share in advancement;

sentences.zh: 晉之士丐，推長伯游。

translations.literal: in Jin, Shi Gai pushed the elder Bo You forward.
translations.idiomatic: in Jin, Shi Gai yielded precedence to the elder Bo You.

sentences.zh: 古人所高，當時見許。

translations.literal: What the ancients honored was praised in their own day.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients honored such conduct, and their contemporaries praised it.

sentences.zh: 敢緣斯義，乞降臣位一階，授彼泛級。」

translations.literal: I dare, following this principle, beg to lower my own rank one step and grant them a corresponding grade.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to follow that principle and ask to lower my own rank one step and grant them a matching grade.

sentences.zh: 詔加征西將軍、冀州大中正。

translations.literal: An edict additionally appointed him General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Rectifier of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict additionally appointed him general who pacifies the west and grand rectifier of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 雖年向六十，加之風疹，而自強人事，孜孜無怠。

translations.literal: Though he was nearing sixty and moreover afflicted with wind paralysis, he yet forced himself in human affairs, diligent and never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Though nearly sixty and afflicted with paralysis, he still drove himself in public affairs, diligent and tireless.

sentences.zh: 公私法集，衣冠從事，延請道俗，修營齋講。

translations.literal: Public and private legal collections, gentry and clerks in attendance, he extended invitations to clergy and laity and arranged Buddhist lectures.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered legal texts public and private, invited gentry and clerks, monks and laymen, and held Buddhist lectures.

sentences.zh: 好善欽賢，愛獎人物，南北親舊，莫不多之。

translations.literal: He loved goodness and admired the worthy, cherished and rewarded men of talent; kinsmen north and south, none did not think well of him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved virtue and honored talent, encouraging and rewarding able men; relatives north and south all spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 大起第宅，微號華侈。

translations.literal: He raised mansions on a grand scale, and his reputation was slightly luxurious.
translations.idiomatic: He built mansions on a grand scale, earning a reputation for slight extravagance.

sentences.zh: 頗侮其疏宗舊戚，不甚存紀，時有怨憾焉。

translations.literal: He rather slighted his distant clansmen and old kin, not greatly maintaining ties, and at times there was resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He slighted distant kinsmen and old connections, keeping little contact with them, which at times bred resentment.

sentences.zh: 榮宦之間，未能止足，屢表在秦州豫有開援漢中之勳，希加賞報，積年不已，朝廷患之。

translations.literal: Amid honors and offices he could not stop; repeatedly he memorialized that while in Qinzhou and Yu he had merit in opening support for Hanzhong and hoped for reward and recompense, year after year without cease—the court was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: He could not rest content with his honors; again and again he claimed merit from Qinzhou and Yu in opening the route to Hanzhong and begged for rewards until the court grew weary of it.

sentences.zh: 第二子仲瑀上封事，求銓別選格，排抑武人，不使預在清品。

translations.literal: His second son Zhongyu submitted a sealed memorial seeking to distinguish selection standards and suppress military men, not allowing them into the pure grades.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Zhongyu submitted a sealed memorial demanding revised selection standards to exclude military men from the pure grades.

sentences.zh: 由是眾口喧喧，謗讟盈路，立榜大巷，克期會集，屠害其家。

translations.literal: Thereupon popular clamor arose, slander filled the roads, placards were posted in the great lanes, and a date was set for assembly to slaughter his household.
translations.idiomatic: Popular outrage erupted; slander filled the streets; notices were posted in the main thoroughfares fixing a date to massacre his family.

sentences.zh: 彝殊無畏避之意，父子安然。

translations.literal: Yi was wholly without fear or avoidance; father and sons remained calm.
translations.idiomatic: Yi showed no fear; father and sons remained calm.

sentences.zh: 神龜二年二月，羽林武賁將幾千人，相率至尚書省詬罵，求其長子尚書郎始均不獲，以瓦石擊打公門。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Shengui, several thousand guardsmen of the Feathered Forest came in a body to the Ministry to revile and abuse, seeking his eldest son Shangjun, gentleman of the Ministry, and when they did not obtain him they pelted the public gate with tiles and stones.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Shengui year 2, several thousand guardsmen of the Feathered Forest stormed the ministry to abuse the family, seeking Yi's eldest son Shangjun; failing to find him, they hurled tiles and stones at the gates.

sentences.zh: 上下懾懼，莫敢討抑。

translations.literal: High and low were terrified and none dared suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Officials high and low were terrified and none dared restrain them.

sentences.zh: 遂持火虜掠道中薪蒿，以杖石為兵器，直造其第，曳彝堂下，捶撻極意，唱呼焚其屋宇。

translations.literal: They then took fire, plundered fuel and reeds along the road, used staves and stones as weapons, went straight to his residence, dragged Yi beneath the hall, beat him with utmost cruelty, shouting to burn his houses.
translations.idiomatic: They seized fire, looted fuel along the roads, armed themselves with staves and stones, marched straight to his house, dragged Yi into the courtyard, beat him savagely, and shouted to burn his buildings.

sentences.zh: 始均、仲瑀當時逾北垣而走。

translations.literal: Shangjun and Zhongyu at the time leaped the north wall and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjun and Zhongyu leaped the north wall and fled.

sentences.zh: 始均回救其父，拜伏群小，以請父命。

translations.literal: Shangjun turned back to rescue his father, bowing prostrate among the mob to beg for his father's life.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjun turned back to save his father, prostrating himself among the mob to beg for his life.

sentences.zh: 羽林等就加毆擊，生投之於煙火中，及得屍骸，不復可識，唯以髻中小釵為驗。

translations.literal: The guardsmen then added blows and cast him alive into the flames; when the corpse was obtained it could no longer be recognized—only a small hairpin in the topknot served as identification.
translations.idiomatic: The guardsmen beat him further and threw him alive into the fire; when the body was recovered it was unrecognizable—only a small hairpin in the hair knot identified it.

sentences.zh: 仲瑀走免。

translations.literal: Zhongyu fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyu escaped.

sentences.zh: 彝僅有餘命，沙門寺與其比鄰，輿致於寺。

translations.literal: Yi had but a breath of life left; a Buddhist monastery neighbored him and they carried him there in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: Yi clung to life; a neighboring monastery took him in on a litter.

sentences.zh: 遠近聞見，莫不惋駭。

translations.literal: Those who heard and saw from near and far were all struck with horror and grief.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard or saw, near and far, were horrified and grieved.

sentences.zh: 乃卒。

translations.literal: He then died.
translations.idiomatic: He died shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 官為收掩羽林凶強者八人斬之。

translations.literal: The government arrested and executed eight of the violent guardsmen.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities arrested and beheaded eight of the ringleaders among the guardsmen.

sentences.zh: 不能窮誅群豎，即為大赦，以安眾心，有識者知國紀之將墜矣。

translations.literal: Unable to pursue and exterminate the whole mob, they at once proclaimed a general amnesty to calm popular hearts; men of insight knew that the norms of the state were about to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to punish the whole mob, the court proclaimed a general amnesty to calm the people; perceptive men saw that state discipline was collapsing.

sentences.zh: 喪還所焚宅，與始均東西分斂於小屋。

translations.literal: The funeral returned to the burned residence; with Shangjun they were buried separately east and west in a small house.
translations.idiomatic: The funeral was held at the burned house; Yi and Shangjun were buried separately in small chambers east and west.

sentences.zh: 仲瑀遂以創重，避居滎陽。

translations.literal: Zhongyu then, because of his wounds, avoided living in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded, Zhongyu withdrew to Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 至五月得漸瘳，始奔父喪，詔賜以布帛。

translations.literal: By the fifth month he gradually recovered and at last rushed to his father's funeral; an edict granted him cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifth month he had recovered enough to attend his father's funeral; the court granted him cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 靈太后以其累朝大臣，特垂矜惻，數月猶追言泣下，謂諸侍臣曰：「吾為張彝飲食不禦，乃至首發微有虧落。」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling, because he was a minister of many reigns, showed special pity; for months afterward she still spoke of him with tears, telling the attendant officials, "For Zhang Yi I could not eat or drink, until even my hair thinned slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling, honoring him as a minister of many reigns, mourned him deeply; months later she still wept when she spoke of him, telling attendants, "For Zhang Yi I lost my appetite until my hair even thinned a little.

sentences.zh: 悲痛之若此。

translations.literal: Her grief was to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of her grief.

sentences.zh: 初，彝曾祖幸所招引河東人為州，裁千餘家。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yi's great-grandfather Xing had recruited people of Hedong as provincials, only a little more than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yi's great-grandfather Xing had settled just over a thousand households of Hedong people in the province.

sentences.zh: 後相依合，旋罷入冀州。

translations.literal: Later they joined together in succession and were soon transferred into Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later they were gradually merged into Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 積三十年，析別有數萬戶。

translations.literal: Over thirty years the branches separated into tens of thousands of households.
translations.idiomatic: Over thirty years the population grew to tens of thousands of households.

sentences.zh: 故孝文比校天下人戶，最為大州。

translations.literal: Therefore when Emperor Xiaowen compared household registers throughout the realm, [Jizhou] was the largest province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen compared household registers empire-wide, Jizhou ranked largest.

sentences.zh: 彝為黃門，每侍坐，以為言。

translations.literal: When Yi was at the Yellow Gate, each time he attended seated he spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: While Yi served at the yellow gate he raised the matter whenever he attended the emperor.

sentences.zh: 孝文謂之曰：「終當以卿為刺史，酬先世誠效。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said to him, "In the end I shall make you a provincial governor to repay your forebears' loyal service.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen told him, "In time I shall appoint you governor to reward your family's loyal service.

sentences.zh: 彝追孝文往旨，累乞本州，朝議未許。

translations.literal: Yi recalled the emperor's former intent and repeatedly begged for his native province; court discussion did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi recalled that promise and repeatedly petitioned for his home province, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 彝亡後，靈太后云：「彝屢乞冀州，吾欲用之，有人違我此意。

translations.literal: After Yi's death Empress Dowager Ling said, "Yi repeatedly begged for Jizhou; I wished to grant it, but someone opposed my wish.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi's death Empress Dowager Ling said, "Yi begged repeatedly for Jizhou; I meant to grant it, but someone opposed me.

sentences.zh: 若從其請，或不至是，悔之無及。」

translations.literal: Had I followed his request, perhaps it would not have come to this; regret is endless.
translations.idiomatic: Had I granted his request, perhaps this would not have happened—regret is endless.

sentences.zh: 乃贈使持節、衛將軍、冀州刺史，諡文侯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Commissioner with Imperial Staff, General of the Guard, and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted commissioner with the imperial staff, general of the guard, and governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Wen.

sentences.zh: 始均字子衡，端潔好學，才幹有美于父。

translations.literal: Shangjun, styled Ziheng, was upright and fond of learning; in talent and competence he surpassed his father.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjun, styled Ziheng, was upright and studious; in ability he surpassed his father.

sentences.zh: 改陳壽《魏書》為編年之體，廣益異聞為三十卷。

translations.literal: He changed Chen Shou's Book of Wei into annalistic form and broadened it with additional material into thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He recast Chen Shou's Book of Wei into annalistic form, adding new material in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 又著《冠帶錄》及諸詩賦數十篇，並亡失。

translations.literal: He also composed the Record of Caps and Girdles and several dozen poems and rhapsodies, all now lost.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the Record of Caps and Girdles and dozens of poems and rhapsodies, all now lost.

sentences.zh: 初，大乘賊起于冀、瀛之間，遣都督元遙討平之，多所殺戮，積屍數萬。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Mahayana bandits rose between Ji and Ying; the commander Yuan Yao was sent to pacify them and killed many, piling corpses in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Mahayana rebels rose in Ji and Ying; Commander Yuan Yao suppressed them and killed tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 始均以郎中為行台，忿軍士以首級為功，令檢集人首數千，一時焚爇，至於灰燼，用息僥倖，見者莫不傷心。

translations.literal: Shangjun, as a bureau director on the mobile secretariat, resented that the soldiers took heads for merit; he ordered the collection of several thousand human heads and burned them at once to ashes, to end opportunism—those who saw it were all grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjun, serving on the mobile secretariat, detested the soldiers' head-counting; he gathered thousands of heads and burned them to ash to end such opportunism, to the grief of onlookers.

sentences.zh: 及始均之死也，始末在煙炭之間，有焦爛之痛，論者或亦推咎焉。
