translations.literal: When Shangjun himself died, from beginning to end he was amid smoke and flame; with the pain of scorching, some in discussion also attributed blame to this.
translations.idiomatic: When Shangjun died amid fire himself, some said he reaped what he had sown.

sentences.zh: 贈樂陵太守，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Governor of Leling, with the posthumous title Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made governor of Leling with the posthumous title Xiao.

sentences.zh: 子皓之，襲祖爵。

translations.literal: His son Haozhi inherited the grandfather's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Haozhi inherited the grandfather's title.

sentences.zh: 武定中，開府主簿，齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was chief clerk of an opening government; when Qi received the mandate the enfeoffment was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was chief clerk of an opening government; when Qi received the mandate his title was reduced by precedent.

sentences.zh: 皓之弟晏之。

translations.literal: Haozhi's younger brother Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Haozhi's younger brother was Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 晏之字熙德幼孤，有至性，為母鄭氏教誨，動依禮典。

translations.literal: Yanzhi, styled Xide, was orphaned young and had utmost filial nature; his mother Lady Zheng taught him, and in conduct he followed the ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi, styled Xide, lost his father young but showed deep filial devotion; his mother Lady Zheng raised him strictly according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 從爾硃榮平元顥，賜爵武城子。

translations.literal: He followed Erzhu Rong in pacifying Yuan Hao and was granted the title Viscount of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Erzhu Rong in pacifying Yuan Hao and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書二千石郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Bureau Director of the Two Thousand Bushel Rank in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to bureau director of the two-thousand-bushel rank in the ministry.

sentences.zh: 高嶽征潁川，復以為都督中兵參軍，兼記室。

translations.literal: When Gao Yue campaigned against Yingchuan he again made him commander of central army staff and concurrently recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yue campaigned in Yingchuan he again made him central army staff commander and recorder.

sentences.zh: 晏之文士，兼有武幹。

translations.literal: Yanzhi was a literary man who also had martial ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi was a scholar who also possessed military talent.

sentences.zh: 每與嶽帷帳之謀，又嘗以短兵接刃，親獲首級，深為嶽所嗟賞。

translations.literal: Each time he joined Yue in planning within the command tent; he also once fought at close quarters with short weapons and personally took heads, deeply winning Yue's admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He often advised Gao Yue in the command tent and once fought hand to hand, taking heads himself, which won Gao Yue's deep admiration.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，文宣為高陽王納晏之女為妃，令赴晉陽成禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao in Northern Qi, Emperor Wenxuan married Yanzhi's daughter to the Prince of Gaoyang and ordered Yanzhi to go to Jinyang to complete the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Northern Qi's Tianbao era, Emperor Wenxuan married Yanzhi's daughter to the Prince of Gaoyang and summoned Yanzhi to Jinyang for the wedding.

sentences.zh: 晏之後園陪宴，坐客皆賦詩。

translations.literal: Afterward in the rear garden Yanzhi accompanied the banquet; the seated guests all composed poems.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a rear-garden banquet Yanzhi joined the guests in composing poems.

sentences.zh: 晏之詩云：「天下有道，主明臣直；

translations.literal: Yanzhi's poem said, "When the realm has the Way, the ruler is enlightened and the ministers upright;
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi's poem read: "When the realm has the Way, the ruler is enlightened and ministers upright;

sentences.zh: 雖休勿休，永貽世則。」

translations.literal: though there is rest, do not rest—forever leave a model for the age.
translations.idiomatic: though there is peace, do not slacken—leave an everlasting model for the age.

sentences.zh: 文宣笑曰：「得卿箴諷，深以慰懷。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan laughed and said, "Receiving your admonition in verse deeply comforts my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan laughed and said, "Your verse of counsel comforts me deeply."

sentences.zh: 後行北徐州事，尋即真，為吏人所愛。

translations.literal: Later he administered Northern Xuzhou affairs, soon made regular [governor], and was loved by officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Northern Xuzhou, soon as full governor, and was beloved by officials and people.

sentences.zh: 御史崔子武督察州郡，至北徐，無所案劾，唯得百姓制《清德頌》數篇，乃歎曰：「本求罪狀，遂聞頌聲。」

translations.literal: Imperial Censor Cui Ziwu inspected the provinces and prefectures; arriving at Northern Xu he found no cases to impeach, only several pieces of the people's "Ode to Pure Virtue," and sighed, "I came seeking crimes yet found songs of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial censor Cui Ziwu inspected the provinces; at Northern Xu he found no offenses to impeach, only the people's "Ode to Pure Virtue," and sighed, "I sought faults yet found praise.

sentences.zh: 遷兗州刺史，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Governor of Yanzhou but died before assuming office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Yanzhou but died before taking office.

sentences.zh: 贈齊州刺史、太常卿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Governor of Qizhou and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted governor of Qizhou and director of the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 子乾威。

translations.literal: His son Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 乾威字元敬，性聰敏。

translations.literal: Qianwei, styled Yuanjing, was clever by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Qianwei, styled Yuanjing, was clever by nature.

sentences.zh: 涉獵群書，其世父皓謂人曰：「吾家千里駒也。」

translations.literal: He ranged through many books; his father's elder cousin Haozhi told people, "A thousand-li colt of our house.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely; his cousin Haozhi called him "our family's thousand-li colt.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，位太常丞。

translations.literal: He served Qi, holding the post of Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He served Qi as assistant director of the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 仕周，為宣納中士。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as Attendant for Proclamation Reception of the Middle Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he was attendant for proclamation reception of the middle rank.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，累遷晉王屬。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui's Kaihuang era he rose to attendant of the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 王甚美其才，與河內張衡俱見禮重，晉邸稱為二張焉。

translations.literal: The prince greatly admired his talent; together with Zhang Heng of Henei he was treated with ritual honor, and the prince's household called them the Two Zhangs.
translations.idiomatic: The prince greatly admired his talent; with Zhang Heng of Henei he was honored, and the prince's household called them the Two Zhangs.

sentences.zh: 及王為太子，遷員外散騎侍郎、太子內舍人。

translations.literal: When the prince became heir apparent he was promoted to Outer Attendant-in-Ordinary and Attendant within the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became heir apparent he was made outer attendant-in-ordinary and attendant within the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，授內史舍人、儀同三司，又以籓邸之舊，加開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded he was appointed Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, Palace Equal to Three Lords, and because of old ties from the princely residence was additionally granted an opening government.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang acceded he was appointed attendant of the palace secretariat and palace equal to the three lords, and because of old ties from the prince's household was granted an opening government.

sentences.zh: 尋拜謁者大夫，從幸江都，以本官攝江都贊務，稱為幹理。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Master for Protocol and followed the emperor to Jiangdu, holding his original office concurrently as assistant for Jiangdu affairs, and was called capable in administration.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made grand master for protocol, followed the emperor to Jiangdu as assistant for Jiangdu affairs, and was praised as an able administrator.

sentences.zh: 乾威嘗在塗，見一遺囊，恐其主求失，因令左右負之而行。

translations.literal: Qianwei once on the road saw a lost purse; fearing its owner would suffer loss from seeking it, he had his attendants carry it as they walked.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road Qianwei found a lost purse; fearing the owner would suffer from the loss, he had his attendants carry it along.

sentences.zh: 後數日，物主來認，悉以付之。

translations.literal: Several days later the owner came to claim it and he returned it all.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the owner came to claim it and he returned everything.

sentences.zh: 淮南太守楊綝嘗與十餘人同來謁見，帝問乾威曰：「其首立者為誰？」

translations.literal: Governor of Huainan Yang Shen once came with more than ten men for an audience; the emperor asked Qianwei, "Who is the one standing at the head?
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Huainan Yang Shen came with more than ten men for an audience; the emperor asked Qianwei, "Who stands at the head?

sentences.zh: 乾威下殿就視而答曰：「淮南太守楊綝。」

translations.literal: Qianwei went down from the hall to look and answered, "Governor of Huainan Yang Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Qianwei went down to look and answered, "Governor of Huainan Yang Shen."

sentences.zh: 帝謂乾威曰：「卿為謁者大夫，而乃不識參見人，何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Qianwei, "You are Grand Master for Protocol, yet do not know those who come to audience—why?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are grand master for protocol yet do not know those who attend audience—why?"

sentences.zh: 乾威對曰：「臣非不識楊綝，但慮不審，所以不敢輕對。

translations.literal: Qianwei replied, "Your servant is not ignorant of Yang Shen, but feared I might be wrong and therefore dared not answer lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Qianwei replied, "I am not ignorant of Yang Shen, but feared I might be mistaken and dared not answer rashly.

sentences.zh: 石建數馬足，蓋慎之至。」

translations.literal: Shi Jian counted horses' hooves—such is the utmost of caution.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian counted horses' hooves—that is the height of caution.

sentences.zh: 其廉慎皆此類也。

translations.literal: His integrity and caution were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity and caution were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 于時帝數巡幸，百姓疲弊，乾威因上封事以諫，帝不悅，自此見疏。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor frequently toured and the people were worn out; Qianwei therefore submitted a sealed memorial to remonstrate, and the emperor was displeased—from this he was estranged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor toured frequently and the people were exhausted; Qianwei submitted a sealed remonstrance, displeasing the emperor, and from then on fell from favor.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒官。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office.

sentences.zh: 有子爽。

translations.literal: He had a son Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Shuang.

sentences.zh: 仕至蘭陵令。

translations.literal: He served up to Magistrate of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang rose to magistrate of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 乾威弟乾雄，亦有才器。

translations.literal: Qianwei's younger brother Qianxiong also had talent and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Qianwei's younger brother Qianxiong also had talent.

sentences.zh: 秦孝王俊為秦州總管，選為法曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Jun of Qin was commander of Qinzhou he selected him as legal bureau aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jun of Qin was commander of Qinzhou he chose Qianxiong as legal bureau aide.

sentences.zh: 王嘗親案囚徒，乾雄誤不持狀，口對百餘人，皆盡事情，同輩莫不歎能。

translations.literal: The prince once personally tried prisoners; Qianxiong by mistake did not hold the dossier yet answered more than a hundred men orally, all matching the facts—his colleagues all sighed at his ability.
translations.idiomatic: The prince once tried prisoners in person; Qianxiong forgot the dossier yet answered for more than a hundred men from memory, all correctly, to his colleagues' amazement.

sentences.zh: 後曆壽春、陽城二縣令，俱有政績。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as magistrate of Shouchun and Yangcheng, both with political achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as magistrate of Shouchun and Yangcheng, both with distinction.

sentences.zh: 邢巒，字洪賓，河間鄚人，魏太常貞之後也。

translations.literal: Xing Luan, styled Hongbin, was a native of Mo in Hejian and a descendant of Zhenzhi, Grand Director of Imperial Sacrifices of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan, styled Hongbin, came from Mo in Hejian and was descended from Zhenzhi, grand director of imperial sacrifices under Wei.

sentences.zh: 族五世祖嘏，石勒頻徵不至。

translations.literal: In the fifth generation of the clan his ancestor Gu was repeatedly summoned by Shi Le but would not come.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations back his ancestor Gu was repeatedly summoned by Shi Le but refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 嘏無子，巒高祖蓋自旁宗入後。

translations.literal: Gu had no son; Luan's great-grandfather Gai entered the lineage from a collateral branch as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Gu had no sons; Luan's great-grandfather Gai was adopted from a collateral branch.

sentences.zh: 蓋孫穎，字宗敬，以才學知名。

translations.literal: Gai's grandson Ying, styled Zongjing, was known for his talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Gai's grandson Ying, whose style name was Zongjing, won renown for talent and scholarship.

sentences.zh: 太武時，與范陽盧玄等同征。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Taiwu, he went on campaign together with Lu Xuan of Fanyang and others.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Taiwu, he joined campaigns alongside Lu Xuan of Fanyang and others.

sentences.zh: 後拜中書侍郎，改通直常侍、平城子使宋。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, then changed to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and made Marquis of Pingcheng as envoy to Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made vice director of the Secretariat, then transferred to regular attendant-in-ordinary and enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingcheng to serve as envoy to Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 還，以病歸鄉。

translations.literal: Upon his return, he went home to his native place because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After returning, he retired to his home district on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝曰：「往憶邢穎長者，有學義，宜侍講東宮，今安在？」

translations.literal: After some time, the emperor said, "I recall in the past the elder Xing Ying, who had learning and integrity and was fit to lecture in the Eastern Palace—where is he now?
translations.idiomatic: Some time later the emperor said, "I remember the elder Xing Ying of old—a man of learning and principle who ought to have lectured in the Eastern Palace. Where is he now?

sentences.zh: 司徒崔浩曰：「穎臥病在家。」

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Cui Hao said, "Ying lies ill at home."
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Cui Hao replied, "Ying is bedridden at home."

sentences.zh: 帝遣太醫馳驛就療。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the imperial physician post-haste by relay to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched the court physician by urgent relay to treat him.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈定州刺史，諡曰康，子修年，即巒父也，位州主簿。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously honored as Governor of Dingzhou with the posthumous title Kang; his son Xiunian, who was Luan's father, held the post of chief clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as governor of Dingzhou with the posthumous title Kang. His son Xiunian—Luan's father—served as chief clerk of the province.

sentences.zh: 巒少好學，負帙尋師，守貧厲節，遂博覽書傳，有文才幹略。

translations.literal: Luan from youth loved learning, shouldered his books to seek teachers, kept poverty and upheld integrity, and so came to read widely in books and records, possessing literary talent and strategic ability.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Luan loved study. He carried his books from teacher to teacher, embraced poverty and held fast to integrity, and in time ranged widely through books and records, showing both literary gifts and strategic judgment.

sentences.zh: 美須髯，姿貌甚偉。

translations.literal: He had a fine beard and moustache, and his appearance was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a handsome beard and moustache, and his bearing was strikingly grand.

sentences.zh: 累遷兼員外散騎常侍，使齊。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Concurrent Supernumerary Regular Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary and sent as envoy to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to concurrent supernumerary regular cavalry attendant-in-ordinary and was dispatched as envoy to Southern Qi.

sentences.zh: 還，再遷中書侍郎，甚見顧遇，常參坐席。

translations.literal: After his return he was promoted again to Vice Director of the Secretariat and received great favor and attention, regularly taking part in seated discussions.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted again to vice director of the Secretariat, enjoyed marked favor, and was regularly included in the emperor's seated councils.

sentences.zh: 孝文因行藥至司空府南，見巒宅，謂巒曰：「朝行藥至此，見卿宅乃住。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, while out taking medicine, came as far as the south of the Ministry of Works' office, saw Luan's residence, and said to Luan, "On my way to take medicine I came here and stopped when I saw your house.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, passing south of the Ministry of Works while out for his medicinal regimen, caught sight of Luan's house and said to him, "I was on my way for medicine and halted when I saw your dwelling.

sentences.zh: 東望德館，情有依然。」

translations.literal: Looking east toward the hall of virtue, my feelings remain as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing east toward your hall of virtue, I feel the old affection anew.

sentences.zh: 巒對曰：「陛下移構中京，方建無窮之業。

translations.literal: Luan replied, "Your Majesty is shifting the capital to the central metropolis and is just now building an enterprise without end.
translations.idiomatic: Luan answered, "Your Majesty is moving the capital to the central metropolis and raising an enterprise without end.

sentences.zh: 臣意在與魏升降，甯容不務永年之宅。」

translations.literal: Your servant's intent is to rise and fall with Wei; how could he be content not to seek a dwelling for long years?
translations.idiomatic: This servant's wish is to rise and fall with Wei. How could he be content to build a house meant to last forever?

sentences.zh: 帝謂司空穆亮、僕射李沖曰：「巒之此言，其意不小。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the Minister of Works Mu Liang and the Director of the Department Li Chong, "In this remark of Luan's, his intent is no small thing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Minister of Works Mu Liang and Director of the Department Li Chong, "In these words of Luan's, his ambition is no small matter."

sentences.zh: 有司奏策秀、孝，詔曰：「秀、孝殊問，經、權異策，邢巒才清，可令策秀。」

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized on the policy and filial-piety examinations, and an edict said, "The policy and filial-piety questions differ, and the canonical and expedient examinations are not the same. Xing Luan's talent is pure—let him be examined on policy."
translations.idiomatic: When the offices reported on the policy and filial-piety examinations, an edict declared, "Policy and filial piety are different fields, and canonical versus expedient questioning requires different tests. Xing Luan's talent is clear—let him sit for the policy examination."

sentences.zh: 後兼黃門郎，從征流北。

translations.literal: Later he concurrently served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and followed the campaign north of the Liu.
translations.idiomatic: He later served concurrently as gentleman of the yellow gate and joined the campaign north of the Liu River.

sentences.zh: 巒在新野，後至。

translations.literal: Luan was at Xinye and arrived later.
translations.idiomatic: Luan was at Xinye and arrived after the main force.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「伯玉天迷其心，鬼惑其慮，守危邦，固逆主。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Boyu has heaven-bewitched his heart and ghosts deluded his plans; he holds a perilous state and clings to a rebellious lord.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Boyu's heart has been bewitched by heaven and his plans led astray by ghosts. He holds a doomed state and serves a rebellious master.

sentences.zh: 至此以來，雖未禽滅，城隍已崩，想在不遠。

translations.literal: From the time we reached here, though he has not yet been captured and destroyed, his walls and moats have already collapsed; I think that will not be far off.
translations.idiomatic: Since we arrived, he has not yet been taken and destroyed, but his walls and moats have already crumbled. I think the end cannot be far off.

sentences.zh: 所以緩攻者，正待中書為露布耳。」

translations.literal: The reason I have slowed the attack is precisely to wait for the Secretariat to write the victory proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I have eased the assault is simply to wait for the Secretariat to draft the victory proclamation.

sentences.zh: 尋除正黃門，兼御史中尉、瀛州大中正，遷散騎常侍，兼尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Regular Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Senior Rectifier of Yingzhou, then promoted to Regular Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary and Concurrent Director of the Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made regular gentleman of the yellow gate, concurrently censor-in-chief and senior rectifier of Yingzhou, then promoted to regular cavalry attendant-in-ordinary with concurrent appointment as director of the department.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，巒奏曰：「先皇深觀古今，去諸奢侈，服御尚質，不貴雕鏤，所珍在素，不務奇彩，至乃紙絹為帳扆，銅鐵為轡勒，訓朝廷以節儉，示百姓以憂矜。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuanwu, Luan memorialized, saying, "The former emperor deeply observed past and present, removed all extravagance, kept dress and equipage plain, did not value carving and inlay, prized simplicity, and did not pursue strange colors. He even made screens of paper and silk and bridle ornaments of copper and iron, instructing the court in thrift and showing the people compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu, Luan submitted a memorial: "The late emperor surveyed past and present, stripped away luxury, kept dress and equipage plain, and disdained carving and inlay. He valued simplicity, not gaudy color—even making screens of paper and silk and bridle fittings of copper and iron, teaching thrift to the court and showing the people his care.

sentences.zh: 逮景明之初，承升平之業，四疆清晏，遠近來同。

translations.literal: When the Jingming era began, he inherited an age of rising peace; the four borders were clear and quiet, and near and far alike came into alignment.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jingming era he inherited an age of peace. The four frontiers lay calm, and near and far alike fell into harmony.

sentences.zh: 於是蕃貢繼路，商估交入，諸所獻貿，倍多於常。

translations.literal: Thereupon tribute from the frontier states followed one after another on the roads, merchants and traders entered in succession, and the goods presented in tribute were many times the usual amount.
translations.idiomatic: Then tribute from the border peoples streamed in along the roads, merchants and traders crossed the borders in succession, and the goods offered in tribute far exceeded the ordinary measure.

sentences.zh: 雖加以節約，猶歲損萬計，珍貨常有餘，國用恆不足。

translations.literal: Even with added economy, there was still an annual loss of tens of thousands, rare goods were constantly in surplus, and state revenue was always insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Even with added frugality, the state still lost tens of thousands each year. Precious goods piled up while revenue perpetually fell short.

sentences.zh: 若不裁其分限，便恐無以支歲。

translations.literal: If their allotment is not cut back, I fear there will be no means to support the year's expenses.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not cut these allotments, I fear we will have no way to meet the year's expenses.

sentences.zh: 自今非為要須者，請皆不受。」

translations.literal: From now on, for all items that are not truly necessary, please accept none of them.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, for everything that is not truly necessary, I ask that nothing be accepted.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋正尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made regular director of the department.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed regular director of the department.

sentences.zh: 梁、溱二州行事夏侯道遷以漢中內附，詔加巒使持節、都督征梁、漢諸軍事，進退征攝，得以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Xiahou Daqian, who handled affairs in Liang and Qin provinces, brought Hanzhong over to allegiance from within; an edict added to Luan's commission the staff of authority as commissioner, with command over all military affairs for the campaign against Liang and Han, with power to advance, retreat, levy troops, and act as expedient required.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Daqian, administrator of Liang and Qin provinces, surrendered Hanzhong to the dynasty from within. An edict added to Luan's commission the staff of authority as commissioner with command over all forces campaigning against Liang and Han, empowering him to advance, retreat, levy troops, and act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 巒至漢中，遣兵討之，賊畢款附，乘勝追奔至關城之下。

translations.literal: When Luan reached Hanzhong, he sent troops to attack; the bandits all submitted in good faith, and pursuing the victory in flight he pressed on to below Guan City.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan reached Hanzhong, he sent troops against them. The rebels all submitted in good faith, and pressing the pursuit he drove them to the foot of Guan City.

sentences.zh: 詔拜巒使持節、梁、秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Luan Commissioner with Staff of Authority and Governor of Liang and Qin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Luan commissioner with staff of authority and governor of Liang and Qin provinces.

sentences.zh: 於是開地定境，東西七百，南北千里，獲郡十四。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened territory and fixed the borders—seven hundred li east to west and a thousand li north to south—and captured fourteen commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He then opened territory and fixed the borders—seven hundred li from east to west and a thousand li from north to south—and took fourteen commanderies.

sentences.zh: 二部護軍及諸縣戍，遂逼涪城。

translations.literal: The two frontier protectors and the garrisons of the various counties then pressed on Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: The two frontier protectors and the garrison posts of the various counties then pressed toward Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 巒表曰：「揚州、成都，相去萬里。

translations.literal: Luan memorialized, saying, "Yangzhou and Chengdu are ten thousand li apart.
translations.idiomatic: Luan memorialized: "Yangzhou and Chengdu lie ten thousand li apart.

sentences.zh: 陸途既絕，唯資水路。

translations.literal: The land route is already cut off; only the water route can be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: The land route is already severed; only the water route remains.

sentences.zh: 水軍西上，非周年不達。

translations.literal: If the navy goes upstream, it will not arrive in less than a full year.
translations.idiomatic: A fleet sailing upstream would need nearly a full year to arrive.

sentences.zh: 外無軍援，一可圖也。

translations.literal: With no military aid from outside, this is the first reason it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: With no army to relieve them from outside, that is the first reason the region can be taken.

sentences.zh: 益州頃經劉季連反叛，鄧元起攻圍，倉庫空竭，無復固守之意，二可圖也。

translations.literal: Yizhou had recently undergone the rebellion of Liu Jilian and the siege by Deng Yuanqi; the storehouses were emptied and there was no longer any will to hold firm—this is the second reason it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou had lately suffered Liu Jilian's rebellion and Deng Yuanqi's siege. The storehouses were empty and the will to hold out was gone—the second reason it can be taken.

sentences.zh: 蕭深藻是裙屐少年，未洽政務；

translations.literal: Xiao Shenzao is a slipper-and-clogs youth who has not yet mastered governance;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Shenzao is a youth of slippers and clogs who has not yet mastered governance;

sentences.zh: 今之所任並非宿將重名，皆是左右少年而已，三可圖也。

translations.literal: those now appointed are none of the old generals of great name—they are all mere young men at the ruler's side—this is the third reason it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: those now in command are none of the seasoned generals of great name—they are all young favorites at court—the third reason it can be taken.

sentences.zh: 蜀之所恃，惟阻劍閣。

translations.literal: What Shu relies upon is only the barrier of Jianmen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: What Shu relies on is only the barrier of Jianmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 今既克南安，已奪其險，據彼界內，三分已一。

translations.literal: Now that Nan'an has been taken, its peril has already been seized; within that territory, one third is already ours.
translations.idiomatic: Nan'an is already taken and its strongpoint lost. Within that territory a third is already ours.

sentences.zh: 從南安向涪，方軌任意，前軍累破，後眾喪魂，四可圖也。

translations.literal: From Nan'an toward Fu, the road lies open as we choose; the vanguard has repeatedly broken the enemy and the rear ranks have lost heart—this is the fourth reason it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: From Nan'an toward Fu the road lies open at our choosing. The vanguard has broken the enemy again and again while the rear ranks have lost heart—the fourth reason it can be taken.

sentences.zh: 深藻是蕭衍兄子，骨肉至親，若其逃亡，當無死理。

translations.literal: Shenzao is the nephew of Xiao Yan and a kinsman of the closest blood; if he flees, he surely cannot escape death.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzao is Xiao Yan's nephew and closest kin. If he flees, he can hardly hope to live.

sentences.zh: 脫軍走涪城，深藻何肯城中坐而受困？

translations.literal: If the army retreats to Fucheng, how could Shenzao sit in the city and accept encirclement?
translations.idiomatic: If our army presses on to Fucheng, how could Shenzao sit in the city and accept siege?

sentences.zh: 五可圖也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth reason it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fifth reason it can be taken.

sentences.zh: 臣聞乘機而動，武之善經，未有舍幹戚而康時，不征伐而統一。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that to move by opportunity is the excellent constant of warfare; never yet has anyone secured the age without weapons of war, or achieved unity without campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that seizing the moment is the supreme constant of war. Never yet has an age been secured without arms, or unity achieved without campaigning.

sentences.zh: 臣以不才，屬當戎寄，上憑國威，頻有薄捷，瞻望涪、益，旦夕可屠，正以兵少糧匱，未宜前出。

translations.literal: Your servant, lacking talent, has been entrusted with military command; relying on the state's prestige, he has had repeated small victories. Looking toward Fu and Yizhou, they could be taken within days. It is only because troops are few and grain scarce that it is not yet fitting to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Lacking talent, I have been entrusted with military command. Relying on the dynasty's prestige I have won repeated minor victories. Fu and Yizhou seem ready to fall within days—yet with too few troops and too little grain, advance is still unwise.

sentences.zh: 今若不取，後圖便難。

translations.literal: If it is not taken now, later plans will be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not take them now, later plans will be far harder.

sentences.zh: 輒率愚管，必將殄克。

translations.literal: I rashly offer this humble opinion and will surely destroy and conquer.
translations.idiomatic: I offer this humble counsel in all confidence that we can destroy and conquer them.

sentences.zh: 如其無功，分受憲坐。

translations.literal: If there is no success, I shall share in the punishment according to my portion.
translations.idiomatic: If I fail, let me bear my share of punishment.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷未欲經略，臣便為無事，乞歸侍養，微展烏鳥。」

translations.literal: If the court does not yet wish to undertake grand strategy, then let your servant be dismissed as idle and permitted to return home to serve his parents and briefly fulfill the duty of the crow and the bird."
translations.idiomatic: If the court is not yet ready for grand strategy, then dismiss me as useless and let me go home to care for my parents and briefly discharge the filial debt owed the crow and the nestling."

sentences.zh: 巒又表曰：「昔鄧艾、鐘會率十八萬眾，傾中國資給，裁得平蜀。

translations.literal: Luan also memorialized, saying, "In the past Deng Ai and Zhong Hui led one hundred eighty thousand men and exhausted the resources of the central state before they barely pacified Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Luan memorialized again: "In the past Deng Ai and Zhong Hui led one hundred eighty thousand men and drained the central state's resources before they barely pacified Shu.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，鬥實力也。

translations.literal: The reason it was so was that they matched strength in battle.
translations.idiomatic: They succeeded only because they matched strength against strength.

sentences.zh: 況臣才絕古人，何宜請二萬之眾而希平蜀？

translations.literal: How much less should your servant, whose talent falls short of the men of old, ask for twenty thousand troops and hope to pacify Shu?
translations.idiomatic: How much less should I, whose talent falls far short of those men of old, ask for a mere twenty thousand troops and expect to pacify Shu?

sentences.zh: 所以敢者，正以據得要險，士庶慕義。

translations.literal: The reason I dare is precisely that we hold the vital passes and the gentry and common people incline to righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: I dare only because we hold the vital passes and the gentry and common people incline toward us.

sentences.zh: 此往則易，彼來則難，任力而行，理有可克。

translations.literal: Going thither is easy; coming hither is hard. Acting according to strength, reason holds that it can be conquered.
translations.idiomatic: To go there is easy; to come here is hard. Acting with the force at hand, conquest is reasonable.

sentences.zh: 今王足前進，已逼涪城。

translations.literal: Now Wang Zu is advancing and has already pressed on Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zu is already advancing and has pressed on Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 脫得涪城，則益州便是成禽之物。

translations.literal: If Fucheng is taken, then Yizhou will be something already in the hunter's bag.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fucheng falls, Yizhou will be game already in the bag.

sentences.zh: 臣誠知征戎危事，未易可為，自軍度劍閣以來，鬚髮中白。

translations.literal: Your servant truly knows that campaigning is a perilous affair and not easily done; since the army crossed Jianmen Pass, the hair amid my beard and temples has turned white.
translations.idiomatic: I know well that war is perilous and not easily done. Since the army crossed Jianmen Pass, the hair at my temples has turned white.

sentences.zh: 所以勉強者，既到此地而自退不守，恐孤先皇之恩遇，負陛下之爵祿。

translations.literal: The reason I force myself on is that, having come this far, to withdraw and not hold would fear betraying the late emperor's grace and failing Your Majesty's rank and salary.
translations.idiomatic: I press on because, having come this far, to withdraw and abandon the field would betray the late emperor's grace and fail the rank and stipend Your Majesty gave me.

sentences.zh: 是以孜孜，頻有陳請。」

translations.literal: Therefore I have been diligent and repeatedly submitted memorials.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I have toiled on and memorialized again and again.

sentences.zh: 宣武不從。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu did not consent.

sentences.zh: 又王足於涪城輒還，遂不定蜀。

translations.literal: Moreover, Wang Zu withdrew on his own at Fucheng, and so Shu was not pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zu then withdrew from Fucheng on his own initiative, and Shu was never pacified.

sentences.zh: 巒既克巴西，遣軍主李仲遷守之。

translations.literal: After Luan had taken Ba West, he sent the army commander Li Zhongqian to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: After Luan took Ba West, he sent the army commander Li Zhongqian to hold it.

sentences.zh: 仲遷得梁將張法養女，有美色，甚惑之。

translations.literal: Zhongqian obtained the daughter of the Liang general Zhang Fayang; she was of beautiful appearance, and he was greatly infatuated with her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqian took the daughter of the Liang general Zhang Fayang—a woman of striking beauty—and became deeply infatuated with her.

sentences.zh: 散費兵儲，專心酒色，公事諮承，無能見者。

translations.literal: He squandered military stores, devoted himself to wine and women, and when official business was referred to him, none could gain audience.
translations.idiomatic: He squandered military stores, gave himself over to wine and women, and when official business was brought to him, no one could gain an audience.

sentences.zh: 巒忿之切齒。

translations.literal: Luan gnashed his teeth in anger at this.
translations.idiomatic: Luan gnashed his teeth in fury.

sentences.zh: 仲遷懼，謀叛。

translations.literal: Zhongqian grew afraid and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment, Zhongqian plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 城人斬其首以降梁將譙希遠，巴西遂沒。

translations.literal: The people of the city cut off his head and surrendered to the Liang general Qiao Xiyuan, and Ba West was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople cut off his head and surrendered to the Liang general Qiao Xiyuan, and Ba West was lost.

sentences.zh: 武興氐楊集起等反，巒遣統軍傅豎眼討平之。

translations.literal: Yang Jiqing of the Wuxing Di and others rebelled; Luan sent the commanding general Fu Shuyan to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiqing of the Wuxing Di and others rose in rebellion. Luan sent the commanding general Fu Shuyan to attack and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 巒之初至漢中，從容風雅，接豪右以禮，撫從庶以惠。

translations.literal: When Luan first reached Hanzhong, he was easy and refined in manner, received the great families with courtesy, and comforted the common people with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan first reached Hanzhong, he was easy and refined in manner, received the great families with courtesy, and comforted the common people with kindness.

sentences.zh: 歲餘之後，頗因其去就，誅滅百姓，籍為奴婢者二百餘口，兼商販聚斂，清論鄙之。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he frequently executed common people according to whether they stayed or left, registering more than two hundred mouths as slaves, and also engaged in trade and amassed wealth—men of upright judgment despised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he began executing common people according to whether they stayed or left, registering more than two hundred persons as slaves, and also traded and amassed wealth—men of upright judgment despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 征授度支尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Director of the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed director of the department of revenue.

sentences.zh: 時梁人侵軼徐、兗，朝廷乃以巒為使持節、都督東討諸軍事、安東將軍，尚書如故。

translations.literal: At that time the people of Liang raided Xu and Yan provinces, and the court therefore made Luan Commissioner with Staff of Authority, Commander of All Forces for the Eastern Campaign, and General Who Pacifies the East, while retaining his post as director.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang forces raided Xu and Yan provinces, the court appointed Luan commissioner with staff of authority, commander of all forces for the eastern campaign, and general who pacifies the east, while retaining his directorship.

sentences.zh: 宣武勞遺巒於東堂曰：「知將軍旋京未久，膝下難違；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu saw Luan off with words of encouragement in the Eastern Hall, saying, "I know the general has not long returned to the capital and that it is hard to leave your parents;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu saw Luan off with encouragement in the Eastern Hall: "I know you have not long been back in the capital and that it is hard to leave your parents;

sentences.zh: 然東南之寄，非將軍莫可。

translations.literal: yet the trust of the southeast cannot be placed in anyone but the general.
translations.idiomatic: yet the southeast cannot be entrusted to anyone but you.

sentences.zh: 自古忠臣亦非無孝也。」

translations.literal: From antiquity, loyal ministers have not been without filial piety either.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers, after all, have never been wholly without filial piety.

sentences.zh: 巒曰：「願陛下勿以東南為慮。」

translations.literal: Luan said, "I wish that Your Majesty would not worry about the southeast."
translations.idiomatic: Luan said, "I ask that Your Majesty not worry about the southeast."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「漢祖有云：'金吾擊郾，吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Han Zu once said, 'When Jin Wu strikes Yan, I have no worries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Han Zu once said, 'When Jin Wu strikes Yan, I have no worries.

sentences.zh: '今將軍董戎，朕何慮哉！」

translations.literal: Now that the general oversees the army, what should I worry about!'
translations.idiomatic: Now that you oversee the army, what have I to worry about!'

sentences.zh: 巒至，乃分遣將帥致討，兗州悉平；

translations.literal: When Luan arrived, he dispatched generals in separate columns to attack; Yan province was entirely pacified;
translations.idiomatic: When Luan arrived, he dispatched generals in separate columns to attack, and Yan province was entirely pacified;

sentences.zh: 進圍宿豫，平之。

translations.literal: he advanced and besieged Suyu, and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: then advanced to besiege Suyu and took it.

sentences.zh: 帝賜巒璽書慰勉之。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed on Luan an imperial letter of seal-script to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed on Luan an imperial letter in seal script to comfort and encourage him.

sentences.zh: 及梁城賊走，中山王英乘勝攻鐘離，又詔巒率眾會之。

translations.literal: When the bandits fled from Liang city, Prince of Zhongshan Ying pursued the victory to attack Zhongli, and another edict ordered Luan to lead his forces to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels fled from Liang city, the Prince of Zhongshan Ying pursued the victory to attack Zhongli, and another edict ordered Luan to lead his forces to join him.

sentences.zh: 巒以為鐘離天險，朝貴所具，若有內應，則所不知，如其無也，必無克狀。

translations.literal: Luan considered that Zhongli was a heaven-sent stronghold and that the court nobles were equipped for it; if there were collaborators within, that was unknown to him, but if there were none, there would surely be no prospect of capture.
translations.idiomatic: Luan judged Zhongli a heaven-sent stronghold that the court nobles had prepared for; if there were collaborators within, he could not know, but if there were none, capture seemed impossible.

sentences.zh: 且俗語云「耕則問田奴，絹則問織婢」，臣既謂難，何容強遣。

translations.literal: Moreover, as the common saying goes, 'When plowing, ask the field slave; when weaving silk, ask the weaving maid'—since your servant holds it difficult, how can he be forced to go?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, as the proverb says, 'Ask the field slave about plowing and the weaving maid about silk.' Since I hold the task difficult, how can I be forced to go?"

sentences.zh: 巒既累表求還，帝許之。

translations.literal: Luan repeatedly memorialized asking to return, and the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Luan repeatedly memorialized asking to return, and the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 英果敗退，時人伏其識略。

translations.literal: Ying indeed suffered defeat and retreated; men of the time admired Luan's foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Ying indeed suffered defeat and withdrew; men of the time admired Luan's foresight.

sentences.zh: 初，侍中盧昶與巒不平，昶與元暉俱為宣武所寵，御史中尉崔亮，昶之黨也，昶、暉令亮糾巒，事成，許言于宣武，以亮為侍中。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Chang had been on bad terms with Luan. Chang and Yuan Hui were both favored by Emperor Xuanwu; Cui Liang, censor-in-chief and Chang's partisan, together with Hui had Liang impeach Luan. If the affair succeeded, they promised to speak to Emperor Xuanwu and make Liang an attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the attendant-in-ordinary Lu Chang had been on bad terms with Luan. Chang and Yuan Hui both enjoyed Emperor Xuanwu's favor. Cui Liang, censor-in-chief and Chang's partisan, together with Hui had Liang impeach Luan, promising that if the case succeeded they would speak to the emperor and make Liang an attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 亮奏巒在漢中掠良人為婢。

translations.literal: Liang memorialized that in Hanzhong Luan had seized common people and made them maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: Liang memorialized that in Hanzhong Luan had seized common people and made them maidservants.

sentences.zh: 巒懼，乃以漢中所得巴西太守龐景仁女化生等二十餘口與暉。

translations.literal: Luan grew afraid and therefore gave to Hui more than twenty persons taken in Hanzhong, including the daughter of Pang Jingren, governor of Ba West, named Huasheng.
translations.idiomatic: Luan grew afraid and gave Hui more than twenty persons taken in Hanzhong, including Huasheng, daughter of Pang Jingren, governor of Ba West.

sentences.zh: 化生等數人，奇色也。

translations.literal: Huasheng and several others were of extraordinary beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Huasheng and several others were of extraordinary beauty.

sentences.zh: 暉大悅，乃背昶為巒言，雲巒新有大功，已經赦宥，不宜方為此獄，帝納之。

translations.literal: Hui was greatly pleased and thereupon turned against Chang to speak for Luan, saying Luan had lately achieved great merit and had already been pardoned—he ought not now to be put through this prosecution; the emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was greatly pleased and turned against Chang to speak for Luan, saying he had lately won great merit and had already been pardoned and ought not now face this prosecution. The emperor accepted the argument.

sentences.zh: 高肇以巒有克敵效而為昶等所排，助巒申釋，故得不坐。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao, because Luan had the achievement of conquering the enemy yet was pushed aside by Chang and the others, helped Luan plead for release, and so he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, seeing that Luan had conquered the enemy yet was pushed aside by Chang and his faction, helped plead for his release, and so he escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 豫州城人白早生殺刺史司馬悅，以城南入梁，遣其將齊苟仁率眾入據縣瓠。

translations.literal: Bai Zaosheng, a man of Yuzhou city, killed the governor Sima Yue, opened the south of the city to Liang, and sent his general Qi Gouren to lead troops in and occupy Xianhu.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zaosheng, a townsman of Yuzhou, killed Governor Sima Yue, opened the south gate to Liang, and sent his general Qi Gouren to lead troops in and occupy Xianhu.

sentences.zh: 詔巒持節率羽林精騎討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Luan, holding the staff of authority, to lead picked cavalry of the imperial guard to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Luan, bearing the staff of authority, to lead picked cavalry of the imperial guard against him.

sentences.zh: 封平舒縣伯，賞宿豫之功也。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingshu—a reward for the achievement at Suyu.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingshu, a reward for the victory at Suyu.

sentences.zh: 宣武臨東堂勞遣巒曰：「早生走也？

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu, seeing Luan off at the Eastern Hall, asked, "Will Zaoshang flee?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu saw Luan off at the Eastern Hall and asked, "Will Zaoshang flee?

sentences.zh: 守也？

translations.literal: Or hold out?
translations.idiomatic: Or hold the city?

sentences.zh: 何時平？」

translations.literal: When will it be pacified?
translations.idiomatic: When will it be pacified?

sentences.zh: 巒曰：「今王師若臨，士人必翻然歸順，圍之窮城，奔走路絕，不度此年，必傳首京師。

translations.literal: Luan said, "If the royal army now arrives, the gentry and people will surely turn about and submit. Besieging them in a trapped city with the road of flight cut off, before this year is out their heads will surely be sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Luan said, "When the royal army arrives, the gentry and people will surely turn and submit. Besieged in a trapped city with no road of escape, before the year is out their heads will reach the capital.

sentences.zh: 願陛下不足為慮。」

translations.literal: I wish that Your Majesty need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty need not worry.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「卿言何其壯哉！

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "Your words are truly bold!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "Your words are bold indeed!

sentences.zh: 知卿親老，頻勞於外，然忠孝不俱，不得辭也。」

translations.literal: I know your parents are old and that you have repeatedly toiled abroad, yet loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fully kept—you cannot decline.
translations.idiomatic: I know your parents are old and that you have toiled repeatedly abroad, yet loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fully kept—you cannot refuse.

sentences.zh: 於是巒率騎八百，倍道兼行。

translations.literal: Thereupon Luan led eight hundred cavalry, traveling day and night at double speed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Luan led eight hundred cavalry, traveling day and night at forced march.

sentences.zh: 五日于鮑口，擊賊大將胡孝智，乘勝至縣瓠，因即度汝。

translations.literal: On the fifth day at Baokou he struck the bandits' great general Hu Xiaozhi, pursued the victory to Xianhu, and thereupon crossed the Ru.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day at Baokou he struck the rebels' great general Hu Xiaozhi, pursued the victory to Xianhu, and crossed the Ru River.

sentences.zh: 既而大兵繼至，遂長圍圍之。

translations.literal: Soon the main army followed, and they thereupon laid a long siege around the city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the main army arrived, and they laid a long siege around the city.

sentences.zh: 詔巒使持節、假鎮南將軍，都督南討諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict made Luan Commissioner with Staff of Authority and Acting General Who Pacifies the South, Commander of All Forces for the Southern Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Luan commissioner with staff of authority and acting general who pacifies the south, commander of all forces for the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 中山王英南討三關，亦次縣瓠，以後軍未至，前寇稍多，憚不敢進。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhongshan Ying also campaigned south against the Three Passes and likewise halted at Xianhu; because the rear army had not arrived and the enemy in front were somewhat numerous, he feared and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhongshan Ying also campaigned south against the Three Passes and halted at Xianhu. Because the rear army had not arrived and the enemy ahead were numerous, he feared to advance.

sentences.zh: 乃與巒分兵，將掎角攻之。

translations.literal: He then divided forces with Luan and planned a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: He then divided forces with Luan and planned a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 梁將齊苟仁等二十一人開門出降，即斬早生等同惡數十人，豫州平。

translations.literal: The Liang generals Qi Gouren and twenty others opened the gate and came out to surrender; they immediately beheaded Zaoshang and several dozen fellow evildoers, and Yuzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang generals Qi Gouren and twenty others opened the gate and surrendered. Zaoshang and several dozen fellow evildoers were immediately beheaded, and Yuzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 巒振旅還京師，宣武臨東堂勞之。

translations.literal: Luan returned his army in order to the capital, and Emperor Xuanwu received him with encouragement in the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Luan returned his army in good order to the capital, and Emperor Xuanwu received him with encouragement in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 巒曰：「此陛下聖略威靈，英等將士之力，臣何功之有？」

translations.literal: Luan said, "This is Your Majesty's sage strategy and august prestige, and the strength of Ying and the officers and soldiers—what merit does your servant have?
translations.idiomatic: Luan said, "This is Your Majesty's sage strategy and august prestige, and the strength of Ying and the officers and soldiers—what merit have I?

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「卿匪直一月三捷，所足稱奇。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "You are not merely achieving three victories in one month, which alone would be worth calling remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "It is not merely that you won three victories in one month, remarkable as that would be.

sentences.zh: 乃存士伯，讓功而弗處。」

translations.literal: You also preserved the dignity of a gentleman, yielding merit and not keeping it for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: You also preserved the dignity of a gentleman, yielding merit and refusing to claim it."

sentences.zh: 巒自宿豫大捷及平縣瓠，志行修正，不復以財賄為懷，戎資軍實，絲毫無犯。

translations.literal: From the great victory at Suyu and the pacification of Xianhu onward, Luan corrected his will and conduct and no longer harbored bribery in his heart; military funds and stores he did not violate in the slightest.
translations.idiomatic: From the great victory at Suyu and the pacification of Xianhu onward, Luan corrected his conduct and no longer coveted bribes; he did not touch military funds or stores in the slightest.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中尚書，加撫軍將軍，卒于官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Department and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Army, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the palace department and given the additional title general who pacifies the army, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 巒才兼文武，朝野瞻望，上下悼惜之。

translations.literal: Luan combined civil and military talent; court and countryside looked up to him, and high and low mourned and regretted his loss.
translations.idiomatic: Luan united civil and military gifts. Court and countryside looked up to him, and all ranks mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎大將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as grand general of chariots and cavalry and governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，帝欲贈冀州，黃門甄琛以巒前曾劾己，乃云：「瀛州巒之本郡，人情所俗。」

translations.literal: At first the emperor wished to posthumously honor him with Jizhou, but Zhen Chen of the Yellow Gate, because Luan had once impeached him, said, "Yingzhou is Luan's native commandery—the place to which popular feeling turns.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor wished to honor him with Jizhou, but Zhen Chen of the yellow gate—because Luan had once impeached him—said, "Yingzhou is Luan's native commandery, the place to which popular feeling turns.

sentences.zh: 乃從之。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon agreed.

sentences.zh: 及琛為詔，乃雲優贈車騎將軍、瀛州刺史，議者笑琛淺薄。

translations.literal: When Chen drafted the edict, he wrote that he was graciously posthumously honored as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Yingzhou; commentators laughed at Chen's pettiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen drafted the edict, he wrote only that Luan was graciously posthumously honored as general of chariots and cavalry and governor of Yingzhou—commentators laughed at Chen's pettiness.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文定。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wendi.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Wendi.

sentences.zh: 子遜。

translations.literal: His son was Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xun.

sentences.zh: 遜字子言，貌雖陋短，頗有風氣。

translations.literal: Xun, styled Ziyan, though ugly and short in appearance, had quite a force of character.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, styled Ziyan, was ugly and short in appearance yet possessed a force of character.

sentences.zh: 襲爵後，遷國子博士、本州中正。

translations.literal: After inheriting the title, he was transferred to Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Senior Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: After inheriting the title he was made erudite of the imperial academy and senior rectifier of his native province.

sentences.zh: 因謁靈太后，自陳功名之子，久抱沈屈：「臣父屢為大將，而臣身無軍國階級。

translations.literal: On paying a visit to Empress Dowager Ling, he declared himself the son of a man of achievement and long bore hidden grievance: "My father repeatedly served as a great general, yet I myself have no military or civil rank.
translations.idiomatic: On visiting Empress Dowager Ling he declared himself the son of a man of achievement and long nursed hidden grievance: "My father repeatedly served as a great general, yet I myself hold no military or civil rank.

sentences.zh: 臣父唯為忠臣，不為慈父」。

translations.literal: My father was only a loyal minister, not a loving father."
translations.idiomatic: My father was a loyal minister only—not a loving father."

sentences.zh: 靈太后慨然，以遜為長兼吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling was moved and made Xun Senior Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling was moved and appointed Xun senior concurrent director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 後位大司農卿，與少卿元慶哲至相糾訟。

translations.literal: Later he held the post of Director of the Grand Granary and, with the Vice Director Yuan Qingzhe, came to mutual impeachment and litigation.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as director of the grand granary and came to mutual impeachment and litigation with Vice Director Yuan Qingzhe.

sentences.zh: 遜銳於財利，議者鄙之。

translations.literal: Xun was sharp in pursuit of profit; commentators despised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was sharp in pursuit of profit, and commentators despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈光祿勳、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously honored as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as grand master for splendid happiness and governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 子祖征，開府祭酒。

translations.literal: His son Zuzheng was libationer of the grand marshal's staff.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuzheng was libationer of the grand marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 父喪未終，謀反，伏法。

translations.literal: Before his father's mourning was finished, he plotted rebellion and was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: Before his father's mourning period was finished, he plotted rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 祖征弟祖效，貌寢，有風尚。

translations.literal: Zuzheng's younger brother Zuxiao was plain in appearance but had refinement and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Zuzheng's younger brother Zuxiao was plain in appearance but possessed refinement and integrity.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，卒于尚書郎。

translations.literal: He served Qi and died while holding the post of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served Qi and died while holding the post of director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 祖效弟祖俊，開府行參軍。

translations.literal: Zuxiao's younger brother Zujun was a staff adjutant of the grand marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: Zuxiao's younger brother Zujun was a staff adjutant of the grand marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，位尚書都官郎中。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he held the post of Director of the Ministry of Justice in the Department.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era he held the post of director of the ministry of justice in the department.

sentences.zh: 巒弟偉，尚書郎中。

translations.literal: Luan's younger brother Wei was a Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Luan's younger brother Wei was a director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 偉子昕。

translations.literal: Wei's son was Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's son was Xin.

sentences.zh: 昕字子明，幼孤，見愛于祖母李氏。

translations.literal: Xin, styled Ziming, was orphaned in youth and was beloved by his grandmother, Lady Li.
translations.idiomatic: Xin, styled Ziming, was orphaned in youth and was beloved by his grandmother, Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 好學，早有才情，解褐蕩寇將軍，累遷太尉記室參軍。

translations.literal: He loved learning, showed literary talent early, entered office as General Who Represses Bandits, and was repeatedly promoted to Secretary of the Grand Marshal's Staff.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, showed literary talent early, entered office as general who represses bandits, and rose repeatedly to secretary of the grand marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚收李神俊奏昕修起居注。

translations.literal: Li Shenjun, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, memorialized that Xin should compile the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun, director of the ministry of personnel, memorialized that Xin should compile the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，除中書侍郎，加平東將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taichang era he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, with the additional titles General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taichang era he was appointed vice director of the secretariat, with the additional titles general who pacifies the east and grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 時言冒竊官級，為中尉所劾，免官，乃為《述躬賦》。

translations.literal: At the time it was said he had falsely seized official rank and was impeached by the censor-in-chief; he was dismissed from office and thereupon wrote "Fu on Restraining the Body."
translations.idiomatic: At the time it was said he had falsely seized official rank and was impeached by the censor-in-chief. Dismissed from office, he wrote the "Fu on Restraining the Body."

sentences.zh: 未幾，受詔與秘書監常景典儀注事。

translations.literal: Before long he received an edict, together with Chang Jing, Director of the Secretariat, to codify ritual and protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he received an edict to codify ritual and protocol together with Chang Jing, director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武帝行釋奠禮，昕與校書郎裴伯茂等俱為錄義。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu performed the libation sacrifice, Xin together with the collating secretary Pei Bamao and others all served as recorders of meaning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu performed the libation sacrifice, Xin together with the collating secretary Pei Bamao and others served as recorders of meaning.

sentences.zh: 永熙末，昕入為侍讀，與溫子升、魏收參掌文詔。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongxi era Xin entered service as lecturer-in-attendance and, together with Wen Zisheng and Wei Shou, jointly managed literary edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongxi era Xin entered service as lecturer-in-attendance and, together with Wen Zisheng and Wei Shou, jointly managed literary edicts.

sentences.zh: 遷鄴，乃歸河間。

translations.literal: He moved to Ye and then returned to Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Ye and then returned to Hejian.

sentences.zh: 天平初，與侍中從叔子才、魏季景、魏收同征赴都，尋還鄉里，既而復征。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianping era he went with his cousin-by-marriage Zicai, Wei Jijing, and Wei Shou on campaign to the capital, soon returned to his home district, and was summoned again not long after.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianping era he joined his cousin-by-marriage Zicai, Wei Jijing, and Wei Shou on campaign to the capital, soon returned home, and was summoned again not long after.

sentences.zh: 時梁使兼散騎常侍劉孝儀等來聘，詔昕兼正員郎，迎於境上。

translations.literal: At that time the Liang envoy, Concurrent Regular Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Xiaoyi and others, came on a friendly visit; an edict made Xin concurrent regular director and sent him to welcome them at the border.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang envoy, concurrent regular cavalry attendant-in-ordinary Liu Xiaoyi and others, came on a friendly visit, an edict made Xin concurrent regular director and sent him to welcome them at the border.

sentences.zh: 司徒孫騰引為中郎。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Sun Teng brought him in as a gentleman of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Sun Teng brought him in as a gentleman of the palace.

sentences.zh: 尋除通直常侍，加中軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, with the additional title General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed regular attendant-in-ordinary, with the additional title general of the central army.

sentences.zh: 既有才藻，兼長几案。

translations.literal: He had both literary talent and was also skilled at desk work.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed literary talent and was also skilled at desk work.

sentences.zh: 自孝昌之後，天下多務，世人競以吏工取達，文學大衰。

translations.literal: From the Xiaochang era onward the realm had many affairs, and men of the age competed to rise through clerical craft; literature greatly declined.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xiaochang era onward the realm was beset with affairs, and men competed to rise through clerical craft while literature greatly declined.

sentences.zh: 司州中從事宋遊道以公斷見知，時與昕嘲謔，昕謂之曰：「世事同知文學外。」

translations.literal: Song Youdao, aide of the central province, was known for fair judgment; at the time he and Xin exchanged banter, and Xin said to him, "In worldly affairs we are alike—outside literature.
translations.idiomatic: Song Youdao, aide of the central province, was known for fair judgment. When he and Xin exchanged banter, Xin told him, "In worldly affairs we are alike—outside literature.

sentences.zh: 遊道有慚色。

translations.literal: Youdao showed a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 興和中，以本官副李象使于梁。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era he served in his original post as deputy to Li Xiang on a mission to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xinghe era he served in his original post as deputy to Li Xiang on a mission to Liang.

sentences.zh: 昕好忤物，人謂之牛。

translations.literal: Xin liked to give offense to others; men called him the Ox.
translations.idiomatic: Xin liked to give offense to others, and men called him the Ox.

sentences.zh: 是行也，談者謂之牛象鬥於江南。

translations.literal: On this mission, commentators called it the ox and the elephant fighting south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: On this mission commentators called it the ox and the elephant fighting south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄王攝選，擬昕為司徒右長史，未奏，遇疾卒，士友悲之。

translations.literal: Prince Wenxiang of Qi, acting in selection, intended Xin for Right Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works; before the appointment was submitted, he fell ill and died, and scholars and friends mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang of Qi, acting in selection, intended Xin for right chief clerk of the ministry of works. Before the appointment was submitted he fell ill and died, and scholars and friends mourned him.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎將軍、都官尚書、冀州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Director of the Ministry of Justice, and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as grand general of chariots and cavalry, director of the ministry of justice, and governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 所著文章自有集錄。

translations.literal: The essays he wrote were collected in his own compiled works.
translations.idiomatic: The essays he wrote were collected in his own compiled works.

sentences.zh: 偉弟晏，字幼平。

translations.literal: Wei's younger brother Yan, styled Youping.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's younger brother Yan, styled Youping.

sentences.zh: 美風儀，博涉經史，善談釋老，雅好文詠。

translations.literal: He had fine bearing and deportment, ranged widely through the classics and histories, was skilled in discussing Buddhism and Daoism, and elegantly loved literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He had fine bearing and deportment, ranged widely through the classics and histories, was skilled in discussing Buddhism and Daoism, and loved literary composition.

sentences.zh: 位滄州刺史，為政清靜，吏人安之。

translations.literal: He held the post of Governor of Cangzhou; his governance was pure and quiet, and officials and people were at ease under him.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Cangzhou. His governance was pure and quiet, and officials and people were at ease under him.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書左僕射、瀛州刺史，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously honored as Left Director of the Department and Governor of Yingzhou, with the posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as left director of the department and governor of Yingzhou, with the posthumous title Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 晏篤于義讓，初為南兗州，例得一子解褐，乃啟其孤弟子子慎為朝請。

translations.literal: Yan was deeply devoted to righteousness and yielding; when he first served in Southern Yanzhou, by precedent he could obtain one son's entry into office, yet he petitioned that his orphaned nephew Zishen be made court gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was deeply devoted to righteousness and yielding. When he first served in Southern Yanzhou, by precedent he could obtain office for one son, yet he petitioned that his orphaned nephew Zishen be made court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 子慎年甫十二，而其子已弱冠矣。

translations.literal: Zishen was only twelve years old, while his own son was already past twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Zishen was only twelve, while his own son was already past twenty.

sentences.zh: 後為滄州，復啟孤兄子昕為府主簿，而其子並未從宦，世人以此多之。

translations.literal: Later, when he served in Cangzhou, he again petitioned that his orphaned elder brother's son Xin be made chief clerk of the prefecture, while his own sons had none yet entered office; men of the age for this reason greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as governor of Cangzhou, he again petitioned that his orphaned elder brother's son Xin be made chief clerk of the prefecture while his own sons had not yet entered office. Men of the age greatly praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 子亢，字子高，頗有文學。

translations.literal: His son Kang, styled Zigao, had considerable literary accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang, styled Zigao, had considerable literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 位兼通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He held the post of Concurrent Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of concurrent regular attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 使于梁，時年二十八。

translations.literal: He was sent as envoy to Liang at the age of twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent as envoy to Liang at the age of twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 後為中外府屬，坐事死于晉陽。

translations.literal: Later he served as staff member of the central and outer offices and, on account of an offense, died at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served on the staff of the central and outer offices and, on account of an offense, died at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 巒叔祖祐，字宗祐。

translations.literal: Luan's granduncle You, styled Zongyou.
translations.idiomatic: Luan's granduncle You, styled Zongyou.

sentences.zh: 少有學尚，知名于時。

translations.literal: In youth he had learning and integrity and was known in his time.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he possessed learning and integrity and was known in his time.

sentences.zh: 假員外散騎常侍，使于宋。

translations.literal: He served as Acting Supernumerary Regular Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary and was sent as envoy to Song.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting supernumerary regular cavalry attendant-in-ordinary and was sent as envoy to Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 以將命之勤，除建威將軍、平原太守、賜爵城平男。

translations.literal: Because of diligence in carrying out his commission, he was appointed General Who Establishes Might, Governor of Pingyuan, and enfeoffed as Baron of Chengpu.
translations.idiomatic: For diligence in carrying out his commission he was appointed general who establishes might, governor of Pingyuan, and enfeoffed as baron of Chengpu.

sentences.zh: 政清刑肅，百姓安之。

translations.literal: His governance was pure and his punishments stern; the common people were at ease under him.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was pure and his punishments stern, and the common people were at ease under him.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子產，字神寶。

translations.literal: His son Chan, styled Shenbao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chan, styled Shenbao.

sentences.zh: 好學善屬文，少時作《孤蓬賦》，為進所稱。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at composing prose; in youth he wrote "Fu on the Solitary Thistle," which contemporaries praised.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and was skilled at prose. In youth he wrote the "Fu on the Solitary Thistle," which contemporaries praised.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，除著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Presented as a xiucai, he was appointed Assistant Editor in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Presented as a provincial graduate, he was appointed assistant editor in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 假常侍、鄚縣子，使于齊。

translations.literal: Acting as Regular Attendant, he was made Viscount of Mo and sent as envoy to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Acting as regular attendant, he was made viscount of Mo and sent as envoy to Qi.

sentences.zh: 產仍世將命，時人美之。

translations.literal: The Chan family for generations carried out commissions abroad, and men of the time admired this.
translations.idiomatic: The Chan family for generations carried out commissions abroad, and men of the time admired them for it.

sentences.zh: 曆中書侍郎、太子中庶子，卒，朝廷嗟惜焉。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Vice Director of the Eastern Palace, and at his death the court sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as vice director of the secretariat and vice director of the eastern palace, and at his death the court sighed in regret.

sentences.zh: 贈平州刺史、樂城子，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Governor of Pingzhou and Viscount of Lecheng, with the posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as governor of Pingzhou and viscount of Lecheng, with the posthumous title Ding.

sentences.zh: 祐從子虯，字神彪。

translations.literal: You's clansman Qiu, styled Shenbiao.
translations.idiomatic: You's clansman Qiu, styled Shenbiao.

sentences.zh: 著作郎敏之子也。

translations.literal: He was the son of Min, Editor in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Min, editor in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 少為《三禮》鄭氏學，明經有文思。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Zheng school of the Three Rites, understood the classics, and had literary thought.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied the Zheng school of the Three Rites, mastered the classics, and possessed literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才上第，為中書議郎、尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: Presented as a xiucai and placed in the upper rank, he became Policy Adviser of the Secretariat and Director in the Palace Department of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Presented as a provincial graduate and placed in the upper rank, he became policy adviser of the secretariat and director in the palace department of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 孝文因公事與語，問朝觀宴饗禮，虯以經對，大合上旨。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, on official business, conversed with him and asked about the rites of court audience and banquets; Qiu answered according to the classics, greatly matching the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, on official business, conversed with him and asked about the rites of court audience and banquets. Qiu answered from the classics, greatly matching the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，尚書令王肅多用新儀，虯往往折以《五經》正禮。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Wang Su, Director of the Department, frequently used new rites, and Qiu often refuted them with the orthodox rites of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Wang Su, director of the department, frequently used new rites, and Qiu often refuted them with the orthodox rites of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 為尚書左丞，多所糾正，台閣肅然。

translations.literal: He became Left Assistant Director of the Department, corrected many matters, and the offices became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He became left assistant director of the department, corrected many matters, and the offices became orderly.

sentences.zh: 時雁門人有害母者，八坐奏轅之而瀦其室，宥其二子。

translations.literal: At that time a man of Yanmen had killed his mother; the Eight Ministers memorialized that he be executed by cart and his house confiscated, pardoning his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a man of Yanmen had killed his mother. The Eight Ministers memorialized that he be executed by cart and his house confiscated, pardoning his two sons.

sentences.zh: 虯駁奏云：「君親無將，將而必誅。

translations.literal: Qiu rebutted the memorial, saying, "Between ruler and parent there is no allowance for rebellion; if one rebels, he must be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu rebutted the memorial: "Between ruler and parent there is no allowance for rebellion; if one rebels, he must be put to death.

sentences.zh: 謀逆者戳及期親，害親者令不及子，既逆甚梟鏡，禽獸之不若，而使禋祀不絕，遺育承傳，非所以勸忠孝之道，存三綱之義。

translations.literal: For plotting rebellion the punishment reaches relatives within one year of mourning; for harming a parent the command does not extend to the sons. Yet this crime exceeds the owl and the mirror—he is not even as good as a beast—and to let the ancestral sacrifices continue and leave descendants to carry on is not the way to encourage loyalty and filial piety or preserve the meaning of the Three Bonds.
translations.idiomatic: For plotting rebellion punishment reaches relatives within one year of mourning; for harming a parent the command does not extend to sons. Yet this crime exceeds the owl and the mirror—he is worse than a beast—and to let ancestral sacrifices continue and leave descendants to carry on is not the way to encourage loyalty and filial piety or preserve the Three Bonds.

sentences.zh: 若聖教含容，不加孥戮，使父子罪不相及，惡止於其身者，則宜投之四裔，敕所在不聽配匹。

translations.literal: If the sage teaching is to be tolerant and not extend punishment to wives and children, so that the crimes of father and son do not reach each other and evil stops with the person himself, then they should be cast to the four borderlands with orders that where they are, marriage shall not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: If the sage teaching is to be tolerant and not extend punishment to wives and children, so that the crimes of father and son do not reach each other and evil stops with the person himself, then they should be cast to the four borderlands with orders that where they are, marriage shall not be permitted.

sentences.zh: 《盤庚》言無令易種新邑，漢法五月食梟羹，皆欲絕其類也。」

translations.literal: The Pan Geng says, 'Do not let them change the seed in the new city'; the law of Han in the fifth month served owl broth—all wished to cut off their kind."
translations.idiomatic: The Pan Geng says, 'Do not let them change the seed in the new city'; Han law in the fifth month served owl broth—all wished to cut off their kind."

sentences.zh: 奏入，宣武從之。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Emperor Xuanwu followed it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial entered, Emperor Xuanwu accepted it.

sentences.zh: 後為光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Later he served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 母在鄉遇患，請假歸。
