translations.literal: His mother fell ill in his home district; he requested leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: His mother fell ill in his home district, and he requested leave to return.

sentences.zh: 遇秋水暴長，河梁破絕，虯得一小船而度。

translations.literal: When autumn waters rose violently, the river bridge was broken and cut off; Qiu obtained a small boat and crossed.
translations.idiomatic: When autumn floods rose violently and the river bridge was broken, Qiu obtained a small boat and crossed.

sentences.zh: 船漏滿不沒，時人異之。

translations.literal: The boat leaked and filled yet did not sink; men of the time regarded this as strange.
translations.idiomatic: The boat leaked and filled yet did not sink; men of the time regarded it as strange.

sentences.zh: 母喪，哀毀過禮，為時所稱。

translations.literal: During his mother's mourning he grieved beyond the rites and was praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: During his mother's mourning he grieved beyond the rites and was praised by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州刺史，諡曰威。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously honored as Governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous title Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous title Wei.

sentences.zh: 虯善與人交，清河崔亮、頓丘李平並與親善。

translations.literal: Qiu was good at friendship; Cui Liang of Qinghe and Li Ping of Dunqiu were both close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was good at friendship; Cui Liang of Qinghe and Li Ping of Dunqiu were both close to him.

sentences.zh: 所作碑頌雜筆三十餘篇。

translations.literal: The stele inscriptions, eulogies, and miscellaneous writings he composed numbered more than thirty pieces.
translations.idiomatic: The stele inscriptions, eulogies, and miscellaneous writings he composed numbered more than thirty pieces.

sentences.zh: 長子臧。

translations.literal: His eldest son was Zang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Zang.

sentences.zh: 臧字子良，幼孤，早立操尚，博學有藻思。

translations.literal: Zang, styled Ziliang, was orphaned in youth, established integrity early, and was broadly learned with literary thought.
translations.idiomatic: Zang, styled Ziliang, was orphaned in youth, established integrity early, and was broadly learned with literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 年二十一，神龜中舉秀才，考上第，為太學博士。

translations.literal: At the age of twenty-one, in the Shengui era he was presented as a xiucai, placed in the upper rank, and became Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-one, in the Shengui era he was presented as a provincial graduate, placed in the upper rank, and became erudite of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 正光中，議立明堂，臧為裴頠一室之議。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era, when the Bright Hall was discussed for establishment, Zang upheld Pei Yi's single-chamber proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengguang era, when establishment of the Bright Hall was debated, Zang upheld Pei Yi's single-chamber proposal.

sentences.zh: 事雖不行，當時稱其理博。

translations.literal: Though the matter was not carried out, men of the time praised the breadth of his reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Though the matter was not carried out, men of the time praised the breadth of his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 出為本州中從事，雅為鄉情所附。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Aide of his native province and was deeply attached to by local sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as aide of his native province and was deeply attached to by local sentiment.

sentences.zh: 永安初，徵為金部郎中，以疾不赴。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yong'an era he was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Revenue but, on account of illness, did not go.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yong'an era he was summoned as director in the ministry of revenue but, on account of illness, did not go.

sentences.zh: 轉除東牟太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed Governor of Dongmou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred and appointed governor of Dongmou.

sentences.zh: 時天下多事，在職少能廉白，臧獨清慎奉法，吏人愛之。

translations.literal: At the time the realm had many affairs, and incumbents rarely could remain pure and upright; Zang alone was pure, cautious, and upheld the law, and officials and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the realm had many affairs, and incumbents rarely remained pure and upright. Zang alone was pure, cautious, and upheld the law, and officials and people loved him.

sentences.zh: 隴西李延寔，莊帝之舅，乙太傅出除青州，啟臧為屬。

translations.literal: Li Yanshi of Longxi, maternal uncle of Emperor Zhuang, when Grand Tutor Yi went out to Qingzhou, petitioned that Zang serve on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanshi of Longxi, maternal uncle of Emperor Zhuang, when Grand Tutor Yi went out to Qingzhou, petitioned that Zang serve on his staff.

sentences.zh: 領樂安內史，有惠政。

translations.literal: He concurrently administered Le'an as inner governor and had benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently administered Le'an as inner governor and governed with benevolence.

sentences.zh: 後除濮陽太守，尋加安東將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Puyang and soon given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed governor of Puyang and soon given the additional title general who pacifies the east.

sentences.zh: 臧和雅信厚，有長者之風，為時人所愛敬。

translations.literal: Zang was harmonious, elegant, faithful, and generous, with the air of an elder; men of the time loved and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Zang was harmonious, elegant, faithful, and generous, with the air of an elder; men of the time loved and respected him.

sentences.zh: 為特進甄琛行狀，世稱其工。

translations.literal: He wrote the conduct report for Special Advance Zhen Chen, and the age praised its craftsmanship.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the conduct report for Special Advance Zhen Chen, and the age praised its craftsmanship.

sentences.zh: 與裴敬憲、盧觀兄弟並結友，曾共讀《回文集》，臧獨先通之。

translations.literal: He formed friendships with Pei Jingxian and the brothers Lu Guan, once together reading the Collected Palindrome Texts; Zang alone mastered it first.
translations.idiomatic: He formed friendships with Pei Jingxian and the brothers Lu Guan, once reading together the Collected Palindrome Texts; Zang alone mastered it first.

sentences.zh: 撰古來文章並敘作者氏族，號曰《文譜》，未就，病卒，時賢悼惜之。

translations.literal: He compiled ancient writings and also recorded the clans of the authors, calling it the Literary Genealogies; before it was finished he died of illness, and worthy men of the time mourned and regretted this.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled ancient writings and recorded the clans of the authors, calling it the Literary Genealogies. Before it was finished he died of illness, and worthy men of the time mourned him.

sentences.zh: 其文筆凡百餘篇。

translations.literal: His literary writings numbered more than one hundred pieces in all.
translations.idiomatic: His literary writings numbered more than one hundred pieces in all.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮北將軍、定州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Dingzhou, with the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as general who pacifies the north and governor of Dingzhou, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 子恕，涉學有識悟。

translations.literal: His son Shu had broad learning and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu had broad learning and discernment.

sentences.zh: 齊武平末，尚書屯田郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wuping era of Qi he was Director of Tuntian in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuping era of Qi he was director of tuntian in the ministry.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，尚書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was Vice Director of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was vice director of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 卒于沂州長史。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Chief Clerk of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as chief clerk of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 臧弟邵，字子才，小字吉。

translations.literal: Zang's younger brother Shao, styled Zicai, with the childhood name Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zang's younger brother Shao, styled Zicai, with the childhood name Ji.

sentences.zh: 少時有避，遂不行名。

translations.literal: In youth he had a taboo and therefore did not use his formal name.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had a taboo and therefore did not use his formal name.

sentences.zh: 年五歲，魏吏部郎清河崔亮見而奇之曰：「此子後當大成，位望通顯。」

translations.literal: At the age of five, Cui Liang, Director of the Ministry of Personnel of Qinghe, saw him and marveled, saying, "This child will later achieve great things and reach eminent rank and renown.
translations.idiomatic: At five, Cui Liang, director of the ministry of personnel of Qinghe, saw him and marveled: "This child will later achieve great things and reach eminent rank and renown.

sentences.zh: 十歲便能屬文，雅有才思，聰明強記，日誦萬餘言。

translations.literal: At ten he could already compose prose, had elegant literary thought, was clever with a strong memory, and recited more than ten thousand words each day.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he could already compose prose, possessed elegant literary gifts, was clever with a strong memory, and recited more than ten thousand words each day.

sentences.zh: 族兄巒有人倫鑒，謂子弟曰：「宗室中有此兒，非常人也。」

translations.literal: His clansman Luan had judgment of human character and told his sons and nephews, "In the imperial clan there is this boy—he is no ordinary person.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Luan had judgment of human character and told his sons and nephews, "In our clan there is this boy—he is no ordinary person.

sentences.zh: 少在洛陽，會天下無事，與時名勝，專以山水遊宴為娛，不暇勤業。

translations.literal: In youth in Luoyang, when the realm was at peace, together with famous men of the age he devoted himself solely to roaming mountains and waters and feasting for pleasure, with no leisure for diligent study.
translations.idiomatic: In youth in Luoyang, when the realm was at peace, he joined famous men of the age in devoting himself solely to roaming mountains and waters and feasting for pleasure, with no leisure for diligent study.

sentences.zh: 嘗霖雨，乃讀《漢書》，五日略能遍之，後因飲謔倦，方廣尋經史，五行俱下，一覽便無所遺。

translations.literal: Once during prolonged rain he read the Book of Han; in five days he could roughly go through it all. Later, because of drinking and banter he grew weary, he then broadly sought out the classics and histories; with five lines at once beneath his eyes, one reading left nothing forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Once during prolonged rain he read the Book of Han and in five days could roughly go through it all. Later, weary of drinking and banter, he broadly sought out the classics and histories; with five lines at once beneath his eyes, one reading left nothing forgotten.

sentences.zh: 文章典麗，既贍且速。

translations.literal: His essays were classical and beautiful, both ample and swift.
translations.idiomatic: His essays were classical and beautiful, both ample and swift.

sentences.zh: 年未二十，名動衣冠。

translations.literal: Before he was twenty, his name shook the gentry and officials.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was twenty, his name shook the gentry and officials.

sentences.zh: 嘗與右北平陽固、河東裴伯茂、從兄罘、河南陸道暉等至北海王昕舍宿飲，相與賦詩，凡數十首，皆在主人奴處。

translations.literal: Once together with Yang Gu of Youbeiping, Pei Bamao of Hedong, his clansman Fei, Lu Daohui of Henan, and others he went to the house of the Prince of Beihai, Xin, to lodge and drink; together they composed poems, several dozen in all, all left with the host's slave.
translations.idiomatic: Once together with Yang Gu of Youbeiping, Pei Bamao of Hedong, his clansman Fei, Lu Daohui of Henan, and others he lodged and drank at the house of Prince Xin of Beihai. Together they composed several dozen poems, all left with the host's slave.

sentences.zh: 旦日奴行，諸人求詩不得，邵皆為誦之。

translations.literal: The next day the slave went out; the others sought the poems and could not obtain them, but Shao recited them all for them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the slave went out. The others sought the poems and could not obtain them, but Shao recited them all.

sentences.zh: 諸人有不認詩者，奴還得本，不誤一字。

translations.literal: Among the others there were some who did not recognize their own poems; when the slave returned with the originals, not a single character was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Some among them did not recognize their own poems. When the slave returned with the originals, not a single character was wrong.

sentences.zh: 諸人方之王粲。

translations.literal: The others then compared him to Wang Can.
translations.idiomatic: The others then compared him to Wang Can.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書隴西李神俊大相欽重，引為忘年之交。

translations.literal: Li Shenjun, Director of the Ministry of Personnel of Longxi, greatly admired and honored him and brought him into friendship despite the difference in age.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun, director of the ministry of personnel of Longxi, greatly admired and honored him and brought him into friendship despite the difference in age.

sentences.zh: 釋巾為魏宣武挽郎。

translations.literal: He left the towel and served as mourning officer for Emperor Xuanwu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He left the towel and served as mourning officer for Emperor Xuanwu of Wei.

sentences.zh: 除奉朝請，遷著作佐郎，深為領軍元叉所禮。

translations.literal: He was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance and transferred to Assistant Editor in the Secretariat, deeply treated with courtesy by Yuan Cha, Director of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed court gentleman for attendance and transferred to assistant editor in the secretariat, deeply treated with courtesy by Yuan Cha, director of the army.

sentences.zh: 叉新除遷尚書令，神俊與陳郡袁翻在席，叉令邵作謝表，須臾便就，以示諸賓。

translations.literal: When Cha was newly appointed and transferred to Director of the Department, Shenjun and Yuan Fan of Chen Commandery were at the banquet; Cha ordered Shao to compose a letter of thanks, and in a moment it was done and shown to the guests.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha was newly appointed director of the department, Shenjun and Yuan Fan of Chen commandery were at the banquet. Cha ordered Shao to compose a letter of thanks; in a moment it was done and shown to the guests.

sentences.zh: 神俊曰：「邢邵此表，足使袁公變色。」

translations.literal: Shenjun said, "This letter of Xing Shao's is enough to make Master Yuan change color.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjun said, "This letter of Xing Shao's is enough to make Master Yuan change color.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，與黃門侍郎李琰之對典朝議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xiaochang era he, together with Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Li Yanzhi, jointly managed court deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiaochang era he, together with Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Li Yanzhi, jointly managed court deliberations.

sentences.zh: 自孝明之後，文雅大盛。

translations.literal: From the time of Emperor Ming onward, elegant writing greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: From the time of Emperor Ming onward, elegant writing greatly flourished.

sentences.zh: 邵雕蟲之美，獨步當時，每一文初出，京師為之紙貴，讀誦俄遍遠近。

translations.literal: Shao's ornamental beauty in composition stood alone in his age; whenever a new piece first appeared, the capital made paper costly for it, and within a short time it was read and recited near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's ornamental beauty in composition stood alone in his age. Whenever a new piece first appeared, the capital made paper costly for it, and within a short time it was read and recited near and far.

sentences.zh: 于時袁翻與范陽祖瑩位望通顯，文筆之美，見稱先達；

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Fan and Zu Ying of Fanyang both held eminent rank and renown, and the beauty of their writing was praised by earlier generations;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Fan and Zu Ying of Fanyang both held eminent rank and renown, and the beauty of their writing was praised by earlier generations;

sentences.zh: 以邵藻思華贍，深共嫉之。

translations.literal: because Shao's literary thought was rich and splendid, they deeply envied him together.
translations.idiomatic: because Shao's literary thought was rich and splendid, they deeply envied him together.

sentences.zh: 每洛中貴人拜職，多憑邵為謝章表。

translations.literal: Whenever eminent men of Luoyang received appointment, most relied on Shao to write their letters of thanks and memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever eminent men of Luoyang received appointment, most relied on Shao to write their letters of thanks and memorials.

sentences.zh: 嘗有一貴勝初授官，大事賓食，翻與邵俱在坐，翻意主人托其為讓表。

translations.literal: Once a noble newly received appointment and gave a great banquet for guests; Fan and Shao were both seated, and Fan expected the host to commission him to write the letter of declination.
translations.idiomatic: Once a noble newly received appointment and gave a great banquet for guests. Fan and Shao were both seated, and Fan expected the host to commission him to write the letter of declination.

sentences.zh: 遂命邵作之，翻甚不悅。

translations.literal: The host thereupon ordered Shao to compose it; Fan was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The host thereupon ordered Shao to compose it; Fan was very displeased.

sentences.zh: 每告人云：「邢家小兒常客作章表，自買黃紙，寫而送之。」

translations.literal: He often told people, "The boy of the Xing family constantly writes memorials for guests, buying yellow paper himself, copying and sending them.
translations.idiomatic: He often told people, "The boy of the Xing family constantly writes memorials for guests, buying yellow paper himself, copying and sending them.

sentences.zh: 邵恐為翻所害，乃辭以疾。

translations.literal: Shao feared being harmed by Fan and therefore pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shao feared being harmed by Fan and therefore pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 屬尚書令元羅出鎮青州，啟為府司馬，遂在青土，終日酣賞，盡山泉之致。

translations.literal: When Director of the Department Yuan Luo went out to govern Qingzhou, he petitioned that Shao serve as staff marshal, and so he was in the land of Qing, drinking and admiring all day, exhausting the pleasures of mountains and streams.
translations.idiomatic: When Director of the Department Yuan Luo went out to govern Qingzhou, he petitioned that Shao serve as staff marshal. Shao remained in Qing province, drinking and admiring all day, exhausting the pleasures of mountains and streams.

sentences.zh: 永安初，累遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yong'an era he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yong'an era he was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 所作詔文體宏麗。

translations.literal: The edicts he composed were grand and beautiful in style.
translations.idiomatic: The edicts he composed were grand and beautiful in style.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃兆入洛，京師擾亂。

translations.literal: When Er Zhujiu entered Luoyang, the capital was thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Er Zhujiu entered Luoyang, the capital was thrown into disorder.

sentences.zh: 邵與弘農楊愔避地嵩高山。

translations.literal: Shao together with Yang Yin of Hongnong took refuge on Songgao Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Shao together with Yang Yin of Hongnong took refuge on Songgao Mountain.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，兼給事黃門侍郎，尋為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Putai era he concurrently served as Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate and soon became Regular Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the Putai era he concurrently served as supervising secretary of the yellow gate and soon became regular cavalry attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，敕令恆直內省，給御史，令覆案尚書門下事，凡除大官，先問其可不，然後施行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taichang era an edict ordered him constantly on duty within the inner palace, given the censorate, and charged to review cases of the Secretariat and Chancellery; for all major appointments, the court first asked whether he approved, and only then carried them out.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taichang era an edict ordered him constantly on duty within the inner palace, given the censorate, and charged to review cases of the secretariat and chancellery. For all major appointments, the court first asked whether he approved, and only then carried them out.

sentences.zh: 除衛將軍、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Guard and Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general of the guard and director of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 以親老還鄉，詔所在特給兵力五人，並令歲一入朝，以備顧問。

translations.literal: Because his parents were old he returned home; an edict ordered that where he was should specially grant him five soldiers, and also ordered him to enter court once a year to be available for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Because his parents were old he returned home. An edict ordered that where he was should specially grant him five soldiers, and also ordered him to enter court once a year to be available for consultation.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: During his mother's mourning he grieved beyond the rites.
translations.idiomatic: During his mother's mourning he grieved beyond the rites.

sentences.zh: 後楊愔與魏元叉及邵請置學，奏曰：

translations.literal: Later Yang Yin, together with Wei Yuancha and Shao, petitioned to establish schools, memorializing as follows:
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Yin, together with Wei Yuancha and Shao, petitioned to establish schools, memorializing as follows:

sentences.zh: 二黌兩學，盛自虞、殷。

translations.literal: The two halls and two academies flourished from the time of Yu and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The two halls and two academies flourished from the time of Yu and Yin.

sentences.zh: 所以宗配上帝，以著莫大之嚴；

translations.literal: By them the ancestral temple was joined to the Lord on High in sacrifice, to display the greatest solemnity;
translations.idiomatic: Through them the ancestral temple joined the Lord on High in sacrifice, displaying the greatest solemnity;

sentences.zh: 宣佈下土，以彰則天之軌。

translations.literal: and edicts were proclaimed to the lower realm, to manifest the track of Heaven's standard.
translations.idiomatic: and edicts were proclaimed to the lower realm, to manifest the track of Heaven's standard.

sentences.zh: 養黃髮以詢哲言，育青衿而敷典教。

translations.literal: The white-haired were nourished to consult wise words; the green-collared were reared to spread canonical teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The white-haired were nourished to consult wise words; the green-collared were reared to spread canonical teaching.

sentences.zh: 用能享國長久，風徽萬祀者也。

translations.literal: Thus states could enjoy long endurance and leave a fine legacy for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Thus states could enjoy long endurance and leave a fine legacy for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 爰暨亡秦，改革其道，坑儒滅學，以蔽黔黎。

translations.literal: When it reached the fallen Qin, it reformed their Way, buried the ru and destroyed learning, to blind the common people.
translations.idiomatic: When it reached fallen Qin, it reformed their Way, buried the ru and destroyed learning, to blind the common people.

sentences.zh: 故九服分崩，祚終二代。

translations.literal: Therefore the nine domains split apart and the throne ended after two generations.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the nine domains split apart and the throne ended after two generations.

sentences.zh: 炎漢勃興，更修儒術。

translations.literal: The blazing Han rose vigorously and again restored Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: The blazing Han rose vigorously and again restored Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 故西京有六學之義，東都有三本之盛。

translations.literal: Therefore the Western Capital had the meaning of the Six Schools, and the Eastern Capital had the splendor of the Three Foundations.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Western Capital had the meaning of the Six Schools, and the Eastern Capital had the splendor of the Three Foundations.

sentences.zh: 逮自魏、晉，撥亂相因，兵革之中，學校不絕，仰惟高祖孝文皇帝，稟聖自天，道鏡今古，列教序於鄉黨，敦詩書于郡國。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, disorder followed in succession; amid arms and armor, schools did not cease. Looking up to the High Ancestor Emperor Xiaowen, he received sagehood from Heaven, and his Way mirrors present and past; he arrayed teaching and order in the districts and villages and nurtured the Odes and Documents in the commanderies and states.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward, disorder followed in succession; amid arms and armor, schools did not cease. Looking up to the High Ancestor Emperor Xiaowen, he received sagehood from Heaven, and his Way mirrors present and past; he arrayed teaching and order in the districts and villages and nurtured the Odes and Documents in the commanderies and states.

sentences.zh: 但經始事殷，戎軒屢駕，未遑多就，弓劍弗追。

translations.literal: But the beginning of the enterprise was vast, and the military carriage repeatedly set out; there was no leisure for much completion, and bow and sword could not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: But the beginning of the enterprise was vast, and the military carriage repeatedly set out; there was no leisure for much completion, and bow and sword could not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 世宗統曆，聿遵先緒，永平之中，大興板築。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong inherited the calendar and followed the former thread; in the Yongping period he greatly raised board and earthworks.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong inherited the calendar and followed the former thread; in the Yongping period he greatly raised board and earthworks.

sentences.zh: 續以水旱，戎馬生郊，雖逮為山，還停一簣。

translations.literal: Then came flood and drought, and war-horses were born in the suburbs; though it reached the building of a mountain, it still stopped one basket short.
translations.idiomatic: Then came flood and drought, and war-horses were born in the suburbs; though it reached the building of a mountain, it still stopped one basket short.

sentences.zh: 而明堂禮樂之本，乃郁荊棘之林；

translations.literal: Yet the root of the Bright Hall and ritual music became a thicket of brambles and thorns;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the root of the Bright Hall and ritual music became a thicket of brambles and thorns;

sentences.zh: 膠序德義之基，空盈牧豎之跡。

translations.literal: the foundation of the school of virtue and righteousness stood empty, filled only with the tracks of herd boys.
translations.idiomatic: the foundation of the school of virtue and righteousness stood empty, filled only with the tracks of herd boys.

sentences.zh: 城隍嚴固之重，闕磚石之工；

translations.literal: The weight of the city walls and strong fortifications lacked the work of brick and stone;
translations.idiomatic: The weight of the city walls and strong fortifications lacked the work of brick and stone;

sentences.zh: 墉構顯望之要，少樓榭之飾。

translations.literal: the essential points of wall and structure and conspicuous expectation had little adornment of towers and pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: the essential points of wall and structure and conspicuous expectation had little adornment of towers and pavilions.

sentences.zh: 加以風雨稍侵，漸致虧墜，非所謂追隆堂構，儀刑萬國者也。

translations.literal: Added to this, wind and rain gradually encroached, and it progressively came to ruin and collapse—it is not what is called pursuing the loftiness of the hall's structure and taking the rites as model for the ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: Added to this, wind and rain gradually encroached, and it progressively came to ruin and collapse—it is not what is called pursuing the loftiness of the hall's structure and taking the rites as model for the ten thousand states.

sentences.zh: 伏聞朝議以高祖大造區夏，道侔姬文，擬祀明堂，式配上帝。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that court deliberation, because the High Ancestor greatly created the realm within the Four Seas and his Way equals King Wen of Zhou, proposes to sacrifice at the Bright Hall and join the Lord on High in sacrifice in the prescribed manner.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that the court deliberates that, because the High Ancestor greatly created the realm within the Four Seas and his Way equals King Wen of Zhou, it proposes to sacrifice at the Bright Hall and join the Lord on High in sacrifice in the prescribed manner.

sentences.zh: 今若基宇不修，仍同丘畎，即使高皇神享，闕于國陽，宗事之典，有聲無實。

translations.literal: If the foundations and structures are not repaired and it remains like a field mound, then even if the high emperor's spirit enjoys sacrifice, it will be lacking at the national altar; the canonical rites of ancestral service will have sound without substance.
translations.idiomatic: If the foundations and structures are not repaired and it remains like a field mound, then even if the high emperor's spirit enjoys sacrifice, it will be lacking at the national altar; the canonical rites of ancestral service will have sound without substance.

sentences.zh: 此臣子所以匪甯，億兆所以佇望也。

translations.literal: For this reason ministers and sons cannot be at ease, and the hundred millions stand waiting in hope.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason ministers and sons cannot be at ease, and the hundred millions stand waiting in hope.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞官方授能，所以任事，既任事矣，酬之以祿。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that the official realm assigns ability in order to entrust affairs; once affairs are entrusted, salary rewards the service.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has also heard that the official realm assigns ability in order to entrust affairs; once affairs are entrusted, salary rewards the service.

sentences.zh: 如此則上無曠官之議，下絕屍素之謗。

translations.literal: In this way, above there will be no criticism of vacant offices, and below the slander of corpse-like idleness will be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In this way, above there will be no criticism of vacant offices, and below the slander of corpse-like idleness will be cut off.

sentences.zh: 今國子雖有學官之名，而無教授之實，何異免絲燕麥，南箕北哉。

translations.literal: Now the Imperial Academy, though it has the name of a school office, has no reality of instruction—how is it different from dodder mistaken for silk, oats of the south, or the Winnowing Basket and the Dipper of the north?
translations.idiomatic: Now the Imperial Academy bears the name of a school yet has no reality of instruction—how is it different from dodder passed off as silk, southern oats, or the Winnowing Basket and the Dipper: names without substance?

sentences.zh: 昔劉向有言寔：者宜興辟雍、陳禮樂以風天下。

translations.literal: In the past Liu Xiang had words, saying: one should establish the Pi Yong and display ritual music to transform the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Liu Xiang had words, saying: one should establish the Pi Yong and display ritual music to transform the realm.

sentences.zh: 夫禮樂所以養人，刑法所以殺人。

translations.literal: For ritual and music are what nourish men; penal law is what kills men.
translations.idiomatic: For ritual and music are what nourish men; penal law is what kills men.

sentences.zh: 而有司勤勤，請定刑法，至於禮樂，則曰未敢。

translations.literal: Yet the responsible officials are diligent in requesting the fixing of criminal law, while concerning rites and music they say they dare not yet.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the responsible officials press diligently for the codification of criminal law, while on rites and music they say they still dare not act.

sentences.zh: 是敢於殺人，不敢於養人也。

translations.literal: This is daring to kill people but not daring to nurture people.
translations.idiomatic: They are bold enough to punish with death, yet lack the courage to cultivate the people.

sentences.zh: 臣以為當今四海清平，九服甯晏，經國要重，理應先營，脫復稽延，則劉向之言征矣。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that at present the four seas are clear and peaceful, the nine domains tranquil and secure, and the essentials of governing the state ought first to be established; if this is again delayed, then Liu Xiang's words will prove true.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that now, with the realm at peace and the nine domains secure, the foundations of statecraft ought to be laid first; further delay will make Liu Xiang's warning come true.

sentences.zh: 但事不兩興，須有進退。

translations.literal: But two undertakings cannot be launched at once; there must be advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet two great projects cannot be pursued at once—priorities must be chosen.

sentences.zh: 以臣愚量，宜罷尚方雕靡之作，頗省永寧土木之功，並減瑤光材瓦之力，兼分石窟鐫琢之勞，及諸事役非世急者，三時農隙，修比數條。

translations.literal: By your subject's dull reckoning, the ornate work of the Palace Workshops should be stopped, the earth-and-wood labor at Yongning considerably reduced, the timber and tile effort at Yaoguang cut back as well, and the toil of carving at the stone grottoes divided up, together with all corvée tasks not urgently needed by the age; in the three farming seasons' intervals, these several items should be repaired.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, the court should halt the Palace Workshops' ornamental projects, pare back Yongning's earthworks, reduce Yaoguang's timber and tile consumption, lighten the stone-grotto carving, and suspend every non-urgent levy—then, in the slack seasons between harvests, devote labor to the measures I propose.

sentences.zh: 使辟雍之禮，蔚爾而復興；

translations.literal: Then the rites of the Biyong would luxuriantly revive again;
translations.idiomatic: The rites of the Biyong would flourish once more;

sentences.zh: 諷誦之音，煥然而更作。

translations.literal: The sounds of recitation and chanting would brilliantly be performed anew.
translations.idiomatic: The voices of recitation and chant would ring out again.

sentences.zh: 美榭高墉，嚴壯於外；

translations.literal: Fine terraces and high walls would be stern and grand without;
translations.idiomatic: Elegant halls and towering ramparts would stand imposing without;

sentences.zh: 槐宮棘寺，顯麗於中。

translations.literal: The locust palace and thorn court would be conspicuous and splendid within.
translations.idiomatic: Within, the academies and law courts would shine with dignity and beauty.

sentences.zh: 更明古今，重遵鄉飲，敦進郡學，精課經業。

translations.literal: Make clearer the ancient and modern, again observe the district drinking ceremony, earnestly advance district schools, and strictly examine classical studies.
translations.idiomatic: Clarify learning across past and present, restore the district drinking rite, promote district schools, and rigorously test students in the classics.

sentences.zh: 如此則元、凱可得之於上序，游、夏可致之于下國，豈不休歟。

translations.literal: If so, then Yuan and Kai could be obtained in the upper ranks, and You and Xia could be brought forth in the lower states—would this not be glorious?
translations.idiomatic: Then men like Yuan and Kai would rise through the highest halls of learning, and disciples like You and Xia would emerge from the provinces—is that not a splendid prospect?

sentences.zh: 靈太后令曰：「配饗大禮，為國之本，比以戎馬在郊，未遑修繕，今四表晏寧，當束有司，別議經始。」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: 'The great rite of joint sacrifice is the foundation of the state. Recently, with war-horses abroad, there was no leisure to repair and build; now the four quarters are tranquil and secure, and the responsible officials should be assembled to discuss separately the beginning of the work.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling decreed: 'The great rite of joint sacrifice is the foundation of the state. While armies were in the field we could not attend to construction; now that the realm is at peace, the responsible officials should be convened to plan the undertaking.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書令，加侍中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing and additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Director of the Masters of Writing with the additional title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 于時與梁和，妙簡聘使，邵與魏收及從子子明被征入朝。

translations.literal: At that time, when peace was made with Liang, envoys were carefully chosen; Shao, together with Wei Shou and his nephew Ziming, was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was concluded with Liang and envoys were carefully selected, Shao was summoned to court along with Wei Shou and his nephew Ziming.

sentences.zh: 當時文人，皆邵之下，但以不持威儀，名高難副，朝廷不令出境。

translations.literal: Among the literati of the time, all were below Shao; yet because he did not maintain dignified bearing and his fame was hard to match, the court did not allow him to go abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary men of letters all ranked below him, but because he cared nothing for decorum and his reputation was too lofty to suit the role, the court would not let him serve as envoy.

sentences.zh: 南人曾問賓司：「邢子才故應是北間第一才士，何為不作聘使？」

translations.literal: Southerners once asked the host of guests: 'Xing Zicai ought surely to be the foremost man of talent in the North—why is he not made an envoy?
translations.idiomatic: Southerners once asked the reception official: 'Xing Zicai should be the North's foremost man of letters—why is he not sent as envoy?

sentences.zh: 答云：「子才文辭實無所愧，但官位已高，恐非復行限。」

translations.literal: The reply was: 'Zicai's literary skill truly has nothing to be ashamed of, but his official rank is already high, and I fear he no longer fits the age limit for travel.'
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: 'Zicai's literary gifts are beyond reproach, but his rank is already too high—he likely no longer meets the age limit for such missions.'

sentences.zh: 南人曰：「鄭伯猷，護軍猶得將命，國子祭酒何為不可？」

translations.literal: The southerners said: 'Zheng Boyou, though only a Defender-in-Chief, was still able to carry imperial orders—why should a Director of the National University not be allowed?'
translations.idiomatic: The southerners replied: 'Zheng Boyou served as envoy though he was only Defender-in-Chief—why not a Director of the National University?'

sentences.zh: 邵既不行，復請還故郡。

translations.literal: Shao, unable to go, again requested return to his former commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao was not sent, he again asked to return to his former prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武帝在京輔政，征之，在第為賓客。

translations.literal: The Emperor Wu was regent in the capital region and summoned him; he received guests at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, then governing from the capital region, summoned him and kept him at home to receive guests.

sentences.zh: 除給事黃門侍郎，與溫子升對為侍讀。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and paired with Wen Zisheng as lecturing attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and paired with Wen Zisheng as imperial lecturing attendants.

sentences.zh: 宣武富於春秋，初總朝政，崔暹每勸禮接名賢，詢訪得失，以邵宿有名望，故請征焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu, rich in youth and first holding court power, was often urged by Cui Xuan to treat renowned worthies with courtesy and inquire into gains and losses; because Shao had long enjoyed reputation, he was therefore requested for summons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu, still young when he first took power, was repeatedly urged by Cui Xuan to receive eminent men courteously and seek their counsel; because Shao's name was long established, Xuan was the one who recommended summoning him.

sentences.zh: 宣武甚親重之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu was very intimate with and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu treated him with great intimacy and esteem.

sentences.zh: 多別引見。

translations.literal: He was often summoned for separate audiences.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor frequently received him in private audience.

sentences.zh: 邵舊鄙崔暹無學術，言論之際，遂雲暹無所知解。

translations.literal: Shao had always looked down on Cui Xuan for lacking learning; in the course of conversation he then said Xuan understood nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had always despised Cui Xuan as a man without scholarship, and in conversation declared that Xuan knew nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 宣武還以邵言告暹，並道「此漢不可親近。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu in turn told Shao's words to Xuan, and also said, 'This Han cannot be approached closely.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu repeated Shao's remarks to Xuan, adding, 'This northerner is not someone to get close to.

sentences.zh: 暹頗銜之。

translations.literal: Xuan harbored considerable resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan took deep offense.

sentences.zh: 邵奏魏帝，發敕用妻兄李伯倫為司徒祭酒。

translations.literal: Shao memorialized the Wei emperor, issuing an edict to appoint his wife's elder brother Li Bolun Director of Sacrificial Affairs at the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Shao petitioned the Wei emperor and had an edict issued appointing his wife's elder brother Li Bolun Director of Sacrificial Affairs at the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 詔書已出，暹即啟宣武，執其專擅，伯倫官事便寢。

translations.literal: After the edict had gone out, Xuan at once reported to Emperor Xuanwu, accusing him of acting on his own authority; Bolun's appointment was immediately halted.
translations.idiomatic: Once the edict was issued, Xuan immediately reported to Emperor Xuanwu and charged Shao with overstepping his authority; Bolun's appointment was at once cancelled.

sentences.zh: 邵由是被疏。

translations.literal: Because of this Shao came to be estranged.
translations.idiomatic: From this Shao fell from favor.

sentences.zh: 其後除驃騎、西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Afterward he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Western Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Western Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 在州有善政，桴鼓不鳴，吏人奸伏，守令長短，無不知之。

translations.literal: In the province his governance was good; the drum of complaint was never sounded, officials and people concealed their wrongdoing, and the strengths and failings of prefects and magistrates were all known to him.
translations.idiomatic: As governor he ruled well: no complaint drum was ever struck, wrongdoing among officials and commoners was quickly exposed, and he knew the merits and faults of every prefect and magistrate.

sentences.zh: 定陶縣去州五十里，縣令妻日暮取人鬥酒束脯，邵逼夜攝令，未明而去，責其取受，舉州不識其所以。

translations.literal: Dingtao County was fifty li from the provincial seat; the county magistrate's wife at dusk took a man's wine and a bundle of dried meat; Shao in the night summoned the magistrate, and before dawn departed, rebuking him for taking bribes—the whole province did not know how he had learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: Dingtao County lay fifty li from the provincial capital. One evening the magistrate's wife accepted wine and dried meat from a local man. Shao summoned the magistrate that same night and, before dawn, rebuked him for taking bribes—yet no one in the province knew how he had found out.

sentences.zh: 在任都不營生產，唯南兗糴粟，就濟陽食之。

translations.literal: Throughout his tenure he engaged in no private enterprise; he only bought grain in Southern Yan and ate it at Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: During his entire term he undertook no private business; he bought grain in Southern Yan and lived on it at Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 邵繕修觀宇，頗為壯麗；

translations.literal: Shao repaired and built halls and towers, making them quite grand and splendid;
translations.idiomatic: Shao restored halls and towers until they were notably grand;

sentences.zh: 皆為之名題，有清風觀、明月樓，而不擾公私，唯使兵力。

translations.literal: All were given names by him—the Clear Wind Pavilion and the Bright Moon Tower—and yet he disturbed neither public nor private interests, using only corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: He named them himself—the Clear Wind Pavilion and the Bright Moon Tower—yet he burdened neither public nor private resources, relying only on allotted labor.

sentences.zh: 吏民為立生祠，並勒碑頌德。

translations.literal: Officials and people erected living shrines for him and carved steles praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners built living shrines to him and carved steles in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 及代，吏人父老及媼嫗皆遠相攀追，號泣不絕。

translations.literal: When he was replaced, old officials and elders among the people, even old women, all pursued him from afar, weeping without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When he was relieved of office, elders among the officials and people—even old women—followed him from afar, weeping without end.

sentences.zh: 至都，除中書令。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the capital he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 舊格制：生兩男者，賞羊五口，不然則絹十匹。

translations.literal: The old regulation: those who bore two sons were rewarded with five sheep; otherwise ten bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: An old regulation rewarded households that produced two sons with five sheep, or otherwise with ten bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 僕射崔暹奏絕之。

translations.literal: Vice Director Cui Xuan memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Cui Xuan petitioned to abolish the practice.

sentences.zh: 邵云：「此格不宜輒斷。

translations.literal: Shao said: 'This regulation should not be abruptly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Shao said: 'This regulation ought not be abolished outright.

sentences.zh: 句踐以區區之越，賞法：生三男者給乳母。

translations.literal: Goujian, with his tiny state of Yue, made it law: those who bore three sons were given wet-nurses.
translations.idiomatic: Goujian, ruling tiny Yue, rewarded those who bore three sons with wet-nurses.

sentences.zh: 況以天下之大而絕此條！

translations.literal: How much more, with a realm as vast as this, to abolish this article!
translations.idiomatic: How much more should a realm as vast as ours keep such a provision!

sentences.zh: 舜藏金於山，不以為乏，今藏之於民，復何所損。」

translations.literal: Shun stored gold in the mountains and did not consider himself impoverished; now storing it among the people—what harm is there?
translations.idiomatic: Shun kept gold in the mountains and did not count himself poor; storing wealth among the people now—what would we lose?

sentences.zh: 又准舊皆訊囚取占，然後送付廷尉。

translations.literal: Again, by old practice all prisoners were interrogated and divination taken before they were sent to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: By older practice, too, prisoners were interrogated and divination performed before cases were sent to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 邵以為不可，乃立議曰：「設官分職，各有司存，丞相不問鬥人，虞官弓招不進。

translations.literal: Shao considered this unacceptable and therefore submitted an opinion: 'Establish offices and divide duties—each has its keeper; the chancellor does not inquire into brawlers, and the bow-master does not summon those who fail to deliver bows.
translations.idiomatic: Shao objected and submitted an opinion: 'Offices exist and duties are divided—each has its proper keeper. The chancellor does not meddle in brawls, and the bow-master does not chase down every missed delivery.

sentences.zh: 豈使屍祝兼刀匕之役，家長侵雞犬之功。」

translations.literal: How could one make the temple priest also perform the knife-and-spoon service, or let the head of the household usurp the work of chickens and dogs?
translations.idiomatic: Surely the temple priest should not also wield knife and ladle, nor the head of a household take over every petty chore.

sentences.zh: 詔並從之。

translations.literal: The edicts all followed his views.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted both proposals.

sentences.zh: 自除太常卿兼中書監，攝國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Director of Ceremonies while concurrently serving as Supervisor of the Secretariat and acting Director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was next appointed Director of Ceremonies, concurrently Supervisor of the Secretariat and acting Director of the National University.

sentences.zh: 是時朝臣多守一職，帶領二官甚少。

translations.literal: At that time many court officials held only one office; very few concurrently held two posts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time most court officials held a single post; few held two at once.

sentences.zh: 邵頓居三職，並是文學之首，當世榮之。

translations.literal: Shao suddenly held three offices, all foremost in literary affairs—the age honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao suddenly held three posts, each the summit of literary office—and his contemporaries regarded it as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 幸晉陽，路中頻有甘露之瑞，朝臣皆作《甘露頌》，尚書符令邵為之序。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Jinyang, sweet dew appeared repeatedly along the road; court officials all composed 'Sweet Dew Eulogies,' and the Secretariat ordered Shao to write the preface.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey to Jinyang, sweet dew appeared again and again along the route; court officials all wrote 'Sweet Dew Eulogies,' and the Secretariat commissioned Shao to compose the preface.

sentences.zh: 及文宣崩，凶禮多見訊訪，敕撰哀策。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan died, mourning rites were much consulted with him, and he was ordered to draft the lamentation text.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan died, he was frequently consulted on funeral rites and ordered to draft the lamentation text.

sentences.zh: 後授特進，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was granted Special Advance and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later granted the rank of Special Advance and died.

sentences.zh: 邵率情簡素，內行修謹，兄弟親姻之間，稱為雍睦。

translations.literal: Shao was straightforward and plain by nature, careful in private conduct; among brothers and affinal kin he was called harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was candid and unpretentious by nature, scrupulous in private life, and among brothers and in-laws was praised for harmony.

sentences.zh: 博覽墳籍，無不通曉。

translations.literal: He broadly read the classics and records and was thoroughly versed in them all.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and historical works and mastered them all.

sentences.zh: 晚年尤以《五經》章句為意，窮其指要。

translations.literal: In his later years he especially devoted himself to the chapter-and-commentary meaning of the Five Classics, exhausting their essential points.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he devoted himself above all to the chapter-and-commentary meaning of the Five Classics, probing their essentials to the end.

sentences.zh: 吉凶禮儀，公私諮稟，質疑去惑，為世指南。

translations.literal: On auspicious and inauspicious rites, public and private consultations were brought to him; he resolved doubts and removed confusion, serving as a guide for the age.
translations.idiomatic: On ritual matters, public and private, men came to him for guidance; he cleared doubts and became a standard for his generation.

sentences.zh: 每公卿會議，事關典故，邵援筆立成，證引該洽。

translations.literal: Whenever high ministers met in conference on matters touching precedent, Shao took brush and completed the text at once, citing proofs comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever ministers met on questions of precedent, Shao would take brush in hand and finish a draft on the spot, citing sources with full mastery.

sentences.zh: 帝命朝章，取定俄頃，詞致宏遠，獨步當時。

translations.literal: When the emperor ordered court documents, Shao settled them in a moment; his phrasing was broad and far-reaching, unmatched in his time.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne required court pronouncements, he settled the wording in moments—his style lofty and unmatched in his day.

sentences.zh: 與濟陰溫子升為文士之冠，世論謂之溫、刑。

translations.literal: With Wen Zisheng of Jiyin he stood at the crown of literary men; the age called them Wen and Xing.
translations.idiomatic: With Wen Zisheng of Jiyin he stood at the head of men of letters; contemporaries spoke of 'Wen and Xing.'

sentences.zh: 钜鹿魏收雖天才豔發，而年事在二人之後，故子升死後，方稱邢魏焉。

translations.literal: Julu's Wei Shou, though his talent blazed brilliantly, was younger than the two of them; therefore only after Zisheng's death was the pair called Xing and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou of Julu, for all his brilliant talent, was younger than both men; only after Zisheng's death did people speak of 'Xing and Wei.'

sentences.zh: 雖望實兼重，不以才位傲物。

translations.literal: Though his reputation and substance were both weighty, he did not treat others arrogantly because of talent or rank.
translations.idiomatic: For all his fame and substance, he never lorded talent or rank over others.

sentences.zh: 脫略簡易，不修威儀，車服器用，充事而已。

translations.literal: Careless and easygoing, he did not cultivate dignified bearing; carriages, robes, and utensils were merely sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: He was informal and unceremonious, caring nothing for dignified bearing; his carriage, dress, and furnishings were merely adequate.

sentences.zh: 有齋不居，坐臥恆在一小屋。

translations.literal: When fasting he did not occupy the main hall; sitting or lying down he always stayed in one small room.
translations.idiomatic: When observing fasts he did not use the main hall; whether sitting or lying down he kept to one small room.

sentences.zh: 果餌之屬，或置之梁上，賓至，下而共啖。

translations.literal: Fruit and sweets and the like he sometimes placed on the beam; when guests arrived he brought them down and they ate together.
translations.idiomatic: He sometimes stored fruit and sweets on a beam; when guests came he brought them down and shared them.

sentences.zh: 天姿質素，特安異同，士無賢愚，皆能傾接，對客或解衣覓虱，且與劇談。

translations.literal: Heaven-endowed and plain by nature, he was especially at ease with difference; whether the scholar was worthy or foolish, he could all receive them with open warmth; facing guests he sometimes undressed to pick lice, yet talked on with great animation.
translations.idiomatic: Plain by nature, he was entirely at ease with disagreement; worthy or dull, every scholar found a warm welcome. With guests he might unbutton his robe to hunt lice and talk on with abandon.

sentences.zh: 有書甚多，而不甚讎校。

translations.literal: He owned very many books but did not greatly collate them.
translations.idiomatic: He owned a great many books but rarely collated them.

sentences.zh: 見人校書，笑曰：「何愚之甚！

translations.literal: Seeing someone collating books, he laughed and said: 'How extremely foolish!
translations.idiomatic: Seeing someone proofreading a text, he laughed: 'How absurdly foolish!

sentences.zh: 天下書至死讀不可遍，焉能始復校此。

translations.literal: Books under heaven cannot all be read even unto death—how can one again begin collating this?
translations.idiomatic: There are more books under heaven than one could read in a lifetime—why bother collating this one?

sentences.zh: 日思誤書，更是一適。」

translations.literal: Pondering mistaken books is yet another pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on a misprinted book is its own kind of delight.

sentences.zh: 妻弟李季節，才學之士，謂子才曰：「世間人多不聰明，思誤書何由能得？」

translations.literal: His wife's younger brother Li Jijie, a man of talent and learning, said to Zicai: 'Most people in the world are not intelligent—how can pondering mistaken books lead to understanding?'
translations.idiomatic: His brother-in-law Li Jijie, a scholar in his own right, asked Zicai: 'Most people are not clever—how can misprints teach you anything?'

sentences.zh: 子才曰：「若思不能得，便不勞讀書。」

translations.literal: Zicai said: 'If by pondering one cannot obtain understanding, then there is no need to trouble oneself with reading books.'
translations.idiomatic: Zicai replied: 'If reflection cannot yield understanding, then there is no point in reading at all.'

sentences.zh: 與婦甚疏，未嘗內宿。

translations.literal: He was very distant from his wife and never spent the night within.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at a remove from his wife and never slept in the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 自雲嘗晝入內閣，為狗所吠，言畢便撫掌大笑。

translations.literal: He himself said that once he entered the inner chambers by day and was barked at by a dog; having said this he at once clapped his hands and laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He once said that he entered the inner chambers by day and was barked at by a dog—and finished the story with a great clap and peal of laughter.

sentences.zh: 性好談賞，又不能閑獨，公事歸休，恆須賓客自伴。

translations.literal: By nature he loved conversation and appreciation, yet could not bear solitude; when public business ended for the day he always needed guests to keep him company.
translations.idiomatic: He loved talk and fine company and could not abide being alone; when the day's business ended he always required guests at his side.

sentences.zh: 事寡嫂甚謹，養孤子恕慈愛特深。

translations.literal: He served his elder brother's widow with great respect and raised his orphaned nephew Shu with exceptional tenderness.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his elder brother's widow with great reverence and raised his orphaned nephew Shu with deep affection.

sentences.zh: 在兗州，有都信雲恕疾，便憂之廢寢食，顏色貶損。

translations.literal: In Yan Province there was a courier named Yun Shu who fell ill; Shao at once worried until he neglected sleep and food, and his complexion declined.
translations.idiomatic: In Yan Province a courier named Yun Shu fell ill; Shao worried so deeply that he neglected sleep and food and his face grew haggard.

sentences.zh: 及卒，人士為之傷心，痛悼雖甚，竟不再哭，賓客吊慰，抆淚而已。

translations.literal: When Shu died, men of standing grieved for him; though the pain of mourning was great, he never wept again—when guests came to condole he merely wiped away tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu died, scholars mourned him deeply; though Shao grieved intensely, he never wept again—when guests came to console him he only wiped his eyes.

sentences.zh: 其高情達識，開遣滯累，東門吳以還，所未有也。

translations.literal: His lofty feeling and penetrating insight, opening and releasing accumulated burdens—since Dongmen Wu there had been nothing like it.
translations.idiomatic: In lofty spirit and clear insight, in freeing himself from the weight of grief, none since Dongmen Wu had been his equal.

sentences.zh: 有集三十卷，見行於世。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in thirty juan, current in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works in thirty juan circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 邵世息大寶，有文情。

translations.literal: Shao's son by a proper wife was Dabao, who had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's legitimate son Dabao possessed literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 孽子大德、大道，略不識字焉。

translations.literal: His sons by concubines, Dade and Dadao, scarcely knew characters at all.
translations.idiomatic: His sons by concubines, Dade and Dadao, could barely read.

sentences.zh: 李崇，字繼長，小名繼伯，頓丘人也。

translations.literal: Li Chong, styled Jichang, with childhood name Jibo, was a man of Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, styled Jichang and known in youth as Jibo, came from Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 文成元皇后第二兄誕之子。

translations.literal: He was the son of Dan, second elder brother of Empress Yuan of Emperor Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Dan, younger brother of Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 年十四，召拜主文中散，襲爵陳留公，鎮西大將軍。

translations.literal: At fourteen he was summoned and appointed Master of Documents in Attendance, succeeded to the title Marquis of Chenliu, and was made General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he was summoned to court, appointed Master of Documents in Attendance, inherited the marquisate of Chenliu, and was made General Who Guards the West.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，為荊州刺史，鎮上洛，敕發秦、陝二州兵送崇至理。

translations.literal: Early in the reign of Emperor Xiaowen he was made Governor of Jing Province and stationed at Shangluo; an edict ordered troops from Qin and Shan Provinces to escort Chong to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was appointed Governor of Jing Province and posted to Shangluo; an edict ordered troops from Qin and Shan Provinces to escort him to office.

sentences.zh: 崇辭曰：「邊人失和，本怨刺史，奉詔代之，但須一宣詔旨而已。

translations.literal: Chong declined, saying: 'The border people have lost harmony, and their grievance is originally against the governor; obeying the edict to replace him, one need only proclaim the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Chong declined, saying: 'The border people are unsettled because they resent the governor. To replace him, the throne need only proclaim its intent.

sentences.zh: 不勞發兵自防，使人懷懼。」

translations.literal: There is no need to dispatch troops to guard oneself and make people harbor fear.
translations.idiomatic: There is no need to march troops in my defense and frighten the people.

sentences.zh: 孝文從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃輕將數十騎馳到上洛，宣詔綏慰，人即帖然。

translations.literal: He then rode lightly with several dozen horsemen to Shangluo, proclaimed the edict and soothed the people, and the people at once submitted peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: He rode swiftly to Shangluo with only a few dozen horsemen, proclaimed the edict, and reassured the people—and they at once submitted.

sentences.zh: 邊戍掠得齊人者，悉令還之。

translations.literal: Border garrisons who had captured men of Qi were all ordered to return them.
translations.idiomatic: Border garrisons holding captives from Qi were ordered to release them all.

sentences.zh: 南人感德，仍送荊州口二百許人。

translations.literal: Southerners, moved by his virtue, in turn sent back about two hundred people from Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his virtue, the southerners in turn returned some two hundred people from Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 兩境交和，無復烽燧之警。

translations.literal: The two borders were harmonious, and there were no further beacon-fire alarms.
translations.idiomatic: Peace held along both borders, and beacon alarms ceased.

sentences.zh: 在州四年，甚有稱績。

translations.literal: He was four years in the province and won considerable praise for his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in office his record won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 召還京師，賞賜隆厚。

translations.literal: Summoned back to the capital, he received lavish rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he was richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 除兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 兗土舊多劫盜，崇乃村置一樓，樓懸一鼓，盜發之處，雙槌亂擊，四面諸村，聞鼓皆守要路。

translations.literal: The land of Yan had long had many bandits and robbers; Chong therefore placed one tower in each village, hung one drum in each tower, and wherever thieves arose, double mallets beat wildly; in the surrounding villages, hearing the drum, all guarded the key roads.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Province had long been plagued by bandits. Chong placed a watchtower in every village, hung a drum in each tower, and whenever thieves struck, the drums were beaten frantically; villages for miles around, hearing them, blocked the key roads.

sentences.zh: 俄頃之間，聲布百里，其中險要，悉有伏人，盜竊始發，便爾禽送。

translations.literal: In a brief moment the sound spread a hundred li; in the dangerous places within, all had men lying in ambush; as soon as theft began, the culprits were at once captured and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: Within moments alarm spread a hundred li; every choke point had men in ambush, and thieves were seized the moment they struck.

sentences.zh: 諸州置樓縣鼓，自崇始也。

translations.literal: The placing of tower drums in the provinces began with Chong.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial system of tower drums began with Chong.

sentences.zh: 後例降為侯，改授安東將軍。

translations.literal: Later, by precedent his rank was reduced to marquis, and he was reassigned as General of Pacification of the East.
translations.idiomatic: Later his title was reduced by precedent to marquis, and he was reassigned as General of Pacification of the East.

sentences.zh: 車駕南征，詔崇副驃騎大將軍、咸陽王禧都督左翼諸軍事。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage marched south, an edict made Chong deputy to General of Agile Cavalry, Prince Xianyang of Xianyang, commanding the left wing.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south, Chong was ordered to serve as deputy to General of Agile Cavalry Prince Xianyang, commanding the left wing.

sentences.zh: 徐州降人郭陸聚黨作逆，人多應之。

translations.literal: Guo Lu of Xuzhou, a defector, gathered a faction and rebelled, and many people joined him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Lu of Xuzhou, a defector, raised a rebel band, and many rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 崇遣高平卜冀州詐稱犯罪，逃亡歸陸，陸納之，以為謀主。

translations.literal: Chong sent Bu Jizhou of Gaoping, who feigned guilt and fled as a criminal back to Lu; Lu received him and made him chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Chong sent Bu Jizhou of Gaoping, who pretended to be a fugitive criminal and joined Lu, who took him in as chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 數月，冀州斬陸送之，賊徒潰散。

translations.literal: After several months Jizhou beheaded Lu and sent the head; the band of rebels scattered and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: After several months Jizhou killed Lu and sent his head; the rebels collapsed.

sentences.zh: 入為河南尹。

translations.literal: He entered court as Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 後車駕南討漢陽，崇行梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage marched south to attack Hanyang, Chong acted as Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor marched south against Hanyang, Chong served as acting Governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 氐楊靈珍遣弟婆羅與子雙領步騎萬餘，襲破武興，與齊相結。

translations.literal: The Di chieftain Yang Lingzhen sent his younger brother Poluo and his son Shuang leading more than ten thousand foot and horse to strike and break Wuxing, and joined with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Yang Lingzhen sent his brother Poluo and his son Shuang with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to overrun Wuxing and ally with Qi.

sentences.zh: 詔崇為使持節、都督隴右諸軍事，率眾討之。

translations.literal: An edict made Chong Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the Longyou region, leading the host to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Chong Bearer of the Staff and Commander-in-Chief of the Longyou region to lead troops against him.

sentences.zh: 崇槎山分進，出其不意，表裹以襲，群氐皆棄靈珍散歸，靈珍眾減太半。

translations.literal: Chong advanced by rafts and mountains in divided columns, taking the enemy unawares; attacking inside and outside, all the Di abandoned Lingzhen and scattered home, and Lingzhen's force was reduced by more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Chong advanced in divided columns by mountain paths and raft crossings, catching the enemy unawares; attacked from within and without, the Di bands abandoned Lingzhen and fled home, and his force was cut by more than half.

sentences.zh: 崇進據赤土。

translations.literal: Chong advanced and occupied Chitu.
translations.idiomatic: Chong advanced and seized Chitu.

sentences.zh: 靈珍又遣從弟率五千人屯龍門，躬率精勇一萬據鷲硤。

translations.literal: Lingzhen again sent a younger cousin leading five thousand men to garrison Longmen, while he himself led ten thousand picked warriors to hold Jiuxia.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhen sent a younger cousin with five thousand men to hold Longmen while he personally led ten thousand elite troops to hold Jiuxia.

sentences.zh: 龍門之北數十里中，伐樹塞路。

translations.literal: Several tens of li north of Longmen, trees were felled to block the road.
translations.idiomatic: For several tens of li north of Longmen, trees were felled to block the roads.

sentences.zh: 鷲硤之口，積大木，聚礌石，臨崖下之，以拒官軍。

translations.literal: At the mouth of Jiuxia, great logs were piled and boulders gathered; from the cliff they were rolled down to resist the government army.
translations.idiomatic: At the mouth of Jiuxia they piled logs and stones and rolled them from the cliffs to block the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 崇乃命統軍慕容拒率眾五千，從他路夜襲龍門，破之。

translations.literal: Chong then ordered the commander Murong Ju to lead five thousand men by another route to attack Longmen by night and break it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong ordered Commander Murong Ju to take five thousand men by another route and storm Longmen by night.

sentences.zh: 崇自攻靈珍。

translations.literal: Chong himself attacked Lingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Chong himself attacked Lingzhen.

sentences.zh: 靈珍連戰敗走，俘其妻子。

translations.literal: Lingzhen fought repeatedly, was defeated, and fled; his wife and children were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhen was defeated in repeated battles and fled; his wife and children were captured.

sentences.zh: 崇多設疑兵，襲克武興。

translations.literal: Chong set up many feints and by surprise assault captured Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Chong deployed many decoys and took Wuxing by surprise.

sentences.zh: 齊梁州刺史陰廣宗遣參軍鄭猷、王思考率眾援靈珍。

translations.literal: Yin Guangzong, Governor of Liang Province under Qi, sent the staff officers Zheng You and Wang Sikao leading troops to aid Lingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Guangzong, Liang Governor under Qi, sent staff officers Zheng You and Wang Sikao with troops to relieve Lingzhen.

sentences.zh: 崇大破之，並斬婆羅首，殺千餘人，俘獲猷等。

translations.literal: Chong greatly defeated them, beheaded Poluo's head as well, killed more than a thousand men, and captured You and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Chong routed them, took Poluo's head, killed more than a thousand men, and captured You and his companions.

sentences.zh: 靈珍走奔漢中。

translations.literal: Lingzhen fled in flight to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhen fled to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 孝文在南陽，覽表大悅曰：「使朕無西顧之憂者，李崇功也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, at Nanyang, reading the report was greatly pleased and said: 'The one who lets Us have no worry to the west is Li Chong's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanyang, Emperor Xiaowen read the report with delight and said: 'Li Chong is the man who frees me from all worry in the west.

sentences.zh: 拜梁州刺史，手詔曰：「便可善思經略，去其可除，安其可育，公私所患，悉令芟夷。」

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Liang Province; the handwritten edict said: 'You should carefully consider strategy, remove what can be removed, settle what can be settled, and cut down entirely whatever harms public and private interest.'
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Liang Province with a handwritten edict: 'Plan carefully—eliminate what must go, secure what can be secured, and root out every ill that afflicts public and private life.'

sentences.zh: 及錄珍偷據白水，崇擊破之，靈珍遠遁。

translations.literal: When Lu Zhen stole and held Baishui, Chong struck and broke him, and Lingzhen fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Zhen seized Baishui, Chong defeated him and Lingzhen fled deep into the hills.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，徵為右衛將軍，兼七兵尚書，轉左衛將軍、相州大中正。

translations.literal: Early in the reign of Emperor Xuanwu he was summoned as General of the Right Guard, concurrently Minister of the Seven Arms, then transferred to General of the Left Guard and Grand Assessor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was recalled as General of the Right Guard and concurrent Minister of the Seven Arms, then transferred to General of the Left Guard and Grand Assessor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 魯陽蠻柳北喜、魯北燕等聚眾反叛，諸蠻悉應之，圍逼湖陽。

translations.literal: The barbarians of Luyang, Liu Beixi, Lu Beiyan, and others gathered crowds and rebelled; all the barbarians responded, surrounding and pressing Huyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Luyang barbarians Liu Beixi, Lu Beiyan, and others rose in rebellion; barbarian bands everywhere joined them and besieged Huyang.

sentences.zh: 遊擊將軍李暉光鎮北城，盡力捍禦。

translations.literal: Mobile Commander Li Huiguang guarded the north city and exerted all strength in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Commander Li Huiguang held the north city and fought with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 賊勢甚盛，詔以崇為使持節、都督征蠻諸軍事以討之。

translations.literal: The rebels' momentum was very strong; an edict made Chong Bearer of the Staff and Commander-in-Chief of the campaign against the barbarians to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' strength was overwhelming; Chong was appointed Bearer of the Staff and Commander-in-Chief of the barbarian campaign.

sentences.zh: 蠻眾數萬，屯據形要，以拒官軍。

translations.literal: The barbarian host numbered tens of thousands, encamped in strategic terrain to resist the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of barbarians held strategic ground against the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 崇累戰破之，斬北燕等，徙萬餘戶於幽、并諸州。

translations.literal: Chong repeatedly fought and broke them, beheaded Beiyan and the others, and relocated more than ten thousand households to You and Bing Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Chong defeated them in repeated battles, beheaded Beiyan and others, and relocated more than ten thousand households to You and Bing Provinces.

sentences.zh: 宣武追賞平氐之功，封魏昌縣伯。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu rewarded in retrospect the achievement of pacifying the Di and enfeoffed him as Baron of Weichang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu rewarded his pacification of the Di and enfeoffed him as Baron of Weichang.

sentences.zh: 東荊州蠻樊安聚眾于龍山，僭稱大號。

translations.literal: The barbarian Fan An of Eastern Jing Province gathered a crowd on Longshan and presumptuously proclaimed a reign title.
translations.idiomatic: Fan An, a barbarian leader of Eastern Jing Province, gathered followers on Longshan and proclaimed himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 梁武遣兵應之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang sent troops to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang sent troops to support him.

sentences.zh: 諸將擊不利，乃以崇為鎮南將軍、都督征蠻諸軍事，率步騎討之。

translations.literal: The generals' attacks did not succeed; Chong was therefore made General Who Guards the South and Commander-in-Chief of the campaign against the barbarians, leading foot and horse to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When other generals failed, Chong was made General Who Guards the South and Commander-in-Chief of the barbarian campaign, leading infantry and cavalry against Fan An.

sentences.zh: 崇分遣諸將，攻擊賊壘，連戰克捷，生禽樊安，進討西荊，諸蠻悉降。

translations.literal: Chong sent out his generals in separate columns to attack the rebel camps; in successive battles he won victories, captured Fan An alive, advanced to attack Western Jing, and all the barbarians submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Chong sent his generals against the rebel camps in separate columns, won successive victories, captured Fan An alive, advanced into Western Jing, and brought all the barbarians to submission.

sentences.zh: 尋兼侍中、東道大使，黜陟能否，著賞罰之稱。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally Palace Attendant and Grand Envoy of the Eastern Circuit, promoting and demoting men according to ability, and won a reputation for rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally appointed Palace Attendant and Grand Envoy of the Eastern Circuit, judging officials by merit and earning a reputation for fair reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 出除散騎常侍、征南將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out and was removed as Regular Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the South, and Governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He left court as Regular Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the South, and Governor of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「應敵制變，算非一途，救左擊右，疾雷均勢。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'Meeting the enemy and controlling change—plans are not of one path alone; saving the left by striking the right is like thunder equalizing force.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: 'To meet the enemy and adapt, no single stratagem suffices; to relieve one point by striking another is like thunder that balances force.

sentences.zh: 今朐山蟻寇，久結未殄，賊愆狡詐，或生詭劫，宜遣銳兵，備其不意。

translations.literal: Now the ant-like bandits at Qushan have long gathered and are not yet exterminated; the rebels' offenses are cunning and deceitful, and may produce sudden raids by trickery—sharp troops should be sent to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits at Qushan have long held out; cunning and treacherous, they may strike by surprise—send elite troops to guard against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 崇可都督淮南諸軍事，坐敦威重，遙運聲算。」

translations.literal: Chong may command the military affairs of the Huai region, sitting with weighty authority, operating strategy from afar.'
translations.idiomatic: Chong is hereby appointed Commander of the Huai region, to hold the line with grave authority and direct strategy from afar.'

sentences.zh: 延昌初，加侍中、車騎將軍、都督江西諸軍事。

translations.literal: Early in the Yan chang era he was additionally made Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yan chang era he was additionally made Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Commander-in-Chief west of the river.

sentences.zh: 先是，壽春縣人苟泰有子三歲，遇賊亡失，數年不知所在，後見在同縣趙奉伯家。

translations.literal: Previously, Gou Tai of Shouyang County had a three-year-old son who, encountering bandits, was lost; for several years no one knew where he was, until later he was seen in the household of Zhao Fengbo in the same county.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gou Tai of Shouyang County had lost his three-year-old son to bandits; for years no one knew where the boy was until he was found in the household of Zhao Fengbo in the same county.

sentences.zh: 泰以狀告，各言己子，並有鄰證，郡縣不能斷。

translations.literal: Tai reported according to the facts; each claimed the child as his own, and both had neighbor witnesses—the commandery and county could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Tai filed a report; each man claimed the boy as his son, neighbors testified for both sides, and the local authorities could not decide.

sentences.zh: 崇令二父與兒各在別處，禁經數旬，然後告之曰：「君兒遇患，向已暴死，可出奔哀也。」

translations.literal: Chong ordered the two fathers and the child each to stay in separate places, forbade contact for several ten-day periods, and then told them: 'Your son has met with illness and has just died suddenly—you may go forth to wail in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Chong separated the two fathers and the child for several weeks, then told them: 'Your son has fallen ill and died suddenly—you may go and mourn.

sentences.zh: 苟泰聞即號啕，悲不自勝；

translations.literal: Gou Tai, hearing this, at once wailed loudly, overcome by grief beyond bearing;
translations.idiomatic: Gou Tai burst into uncontrollable wailing;

sentences.zh: 奉伯咨嗟而已，殊無痛意。

translations.literal: Fengbo sighed and that was all, entirely without the air of pain.
translations.idiomatic: Fengbo sighed but showed no real anguish.

sentences.zh: 崇察知之，乃以兒還泰，詰奉伯詐狀。

translations.literal: Chong, having perceived this, then returned the child to Tai and interrogated Fengbo about the false claim.
translations.idiomatic: Chong saw through the deception, returned the boy to Tai, and interrogated Fengbo about the fraud.

sentences.zh: 奉伯款引，雲先亡一子，故妄認之。

translations.literal: Fengbo confessed fully, saying he had previously lost a son and therefore falsely claimed this one.
translations.idiomatic: Fengbo confessed that he had lost a son earlier and had falsely claimed this boy.

sentences.zh: 又定州流人解慶賓兄弟，坐事俱徙揚州。

translations.literal: Also, the exiled man Xie Qingbin and his younger brother of Ding Province, because of an offense, were both banished to Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Also, the exiles Xie Qingbin and his brother of Ding Province, convicted of a crime, were both sent to Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 弟思安背役亡歸。

translations.literal: The younger brother Sian deserted his corvée and fled home.
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother Sian abandoned his corvée and fled home.

sentences.zh: 慶賓懼後役追責，規絕名貫，乃認城外死屍，詐稱其弟為人所殺，迎歸殯葬。

translations.literal: Qingbin feared later corvée would pursue and assign blame; he plotted to sever his name from the register, therefore claimed a dead corpse outside the city, falsely saying his brother had been killed by others, and brought it back for burial.
