translations.idiomatic: Qingbin feared pursuit for the desertion and plotted to erase his brother from the rolls; he identified a corpse outside the city, claimed it was his murdered brother, and arranged a funeral.

sentences.zh: 頗類思安，見者莫辨。

translations.literal: It rather resembled Sian; those who saw it could not distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: The body resembled Sian closely enough that witnesses could not tell otherwise.

sentences.zh: 又有女巫陽氏自雲見鬼，說思安被害之苦，饑渴之意。

translations.literal: Also a witch named Yang declared she had seen a ghost, describing Sian's suffering when killed and his hunger and thirst.
translations.idiomatic: A witch named Yang claimed to have seen Sian's ghost and described his torment, hunger, and thirst.

sentences.zh: 慶賓又誣疑同軍兵蘇顯甫、李蓋等所殺，經州訟之。

translations.literal: Qingbin also falsely suspected fellow soldiers Su Xianfu and Li Gai of the killing and brought suit at the provincial level.
translations.idiomatic: Qingbin also accused fellow soldiers Su Xianfu and Li Gai of the murder and sued at the provincial level.

sentences.zh: 二人不勝楚毒，各自款引。

translations.literal: The two could not endure the torture and each confessed fully.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to endure torture, both men confessed.

sentences.zh: 獄將決竟，崇疑而停之。

translations.literal: The case was about to be decided when Chong, doubting, halted it.
translations.idiomatic: The case was nearly closed when Chong, suspicious, halted proceedings.

sentences.zh: 密遣二人非州內所識者，偽從外來，詣慶賓告曰：「僕住在北州，比有一人見過寄宿。

translations.literal: Secretly he sent two men unknown within the province, who feigned coming from outside, to go to Qingbin and report: 'Your servant lives in the northern province; recently a man came by and lodged with me.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly he sent two strangers from outside the province to Qingbin, saying: 'We come from the north. A man recently lodged with us.

sentences.zh: 夜中共語，疑其有異，便即詰問，乃雲是流兵背役，姓解字思安。

translations.literal: At night we talked together; suspecting he was unusual, I at once questioned him, and he then said he was a fugitive soldier who had deserted corvée, surnamed Xie with given name Sian.
translations.idiomatic: We spoke at night, found him suspicious, and questioned him. He said he was a fugitive corvée deserter named Xie Sian.

sentences.zh: 時欲送官，苦見求及，稱'有兄慶賓，今往揚州相國城內，嫂姓徐。

translations.literal: At the time I wanted to send him to the authorities, but he begged me hard and said: 'I have an elder brother Qingbin, now in Xiangguo City in Yang Province; my sister-in-law's surname is Xu.'
translations.idiomatic: We meant to turn him in, but he begged us hard, saying he had a brother Qingbin in Xiangguo City in Yang Province and a sister-in-law surnamed Xu.

sentences.zh: 君脫矜慜，為往告報，見申委曲，家兄聞此，必重相報。

translations.literal: If you would show pity and go report this for me, explaining the full circumstances—when my elder brother hears this he is sure to reward you heavily.
translations.idiomatic: If you would take pity and carry word to him, my brother will surely reward you handsomely.

sentences.zh: 今但見質，若往不獲，送官何晚？

translations.literal: Now I have only brought him as a hostage; if you go and do not obtain the reward, what harm in sending him to the authorities later?
translations.idiomatic: We have brought him as a hostage. If the errand fails, you can still hand him over later.

sentences.zh: '是故相造，指申此意。

translations.literal: For this reason I have come specially to explain this intent to you.
translations.idiomatic: That is why we have come to you.

sentences.zh: 君欲見雇幾何？

translations.literal: How much do you wish to be hired for?
translations.idiomatic: What fee do you want?

sentences.zh: 當放賢弟。

translations.literal: Then your worthy younger brother will be released.
translations.idiomatic: Pay it, and we will release your brother.

sentences.zh: 若其不信，可見隨看之。」

translations.literal: If you do not believe it, you may come along and see for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If you doubt us, come and see for yourself.

sentences.zh: 慶賓悵然失色，求其少停。

translations.literal: Qingbin, dismayed, turned pale and asked for a little delay.
translations.idiomatic: Qingbin turned pale with dismay and asked for time.

sentences.zh: 此人具以報崇，攝慶賓問之，伏引。

translations.literal: This man reported everything fully to Chong; Qingbin was summoned and questioned, and confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The agents reported to Chong; Qingbin was summoned, questioned, and confessed.

sentences.zh: 更問蓋等，乃雲自誣。

translations.literal: When Gai and the others were questioned again, they then said they had falsely incriminated themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Questioned again, Gai and the others admitted they had falsely confessed.

sentences.zh: 數日之間，思安亦為人縛送。

translations.literal: Within several days Sian was also bound and sent in by someone.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Sian was captured and sent in as well.

sentences.zh: 崇召女巫視之，鞭笞一百。

translations.literal: Chong summoned the witch to view the matter and had her flogged a hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Chong summoned the witch, exposed the fraud, and had her flogged a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 崇斷獄精審，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Chong's judgment of cases was precise and thorough—all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's adjudication was precise and thorough—cases like these were typical.

sentences.zh: 時有泉水湧於八公山頂，壽春城中有魚數從地湧出，野鴨群飛入城，與鵲爭巢。

translations.literal: At the time a spring gushed on the summit of Bagong Mountain, and in Shouyang city several fish repeatedly surged up from the ground; wild ducks in flocks flew into the city and contested nests with magpies.
translations.idiomatic: A spring burst forth on Bagong Mountain; fish repeatedly welled up from the ground in Shouyang; flocks of wild ducks flew into the city and fought magpies for nests.

sentences.zh: 五月，大霖雨十有三日，大水入城，屋宇皆沒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, great rains fell for thirteen days; floodwaters entered the city and houses were all submerged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month rain fell torrentially for thirteen days; floodwaters poured into the city and submerged every house.

sentences.zh: 崇與兵泊於城上，水增未已，乘船附於女牆，城不沒者二版而已。

translations.literal: Chong and his soldiers moored on the city wall; the water kept rising without cease; they boarded boats alongside the parapet—the city was not submerged by only two courses of wall.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and his soldiers took refuge on the walls; as the water kept rising they tied boats to the parapets—the city stood only two wall-courses above the flood.

sentences.zh: 州府勸崇棄州保北山。

translations.literal: The provincial office urged Chong to abandon the province and hold the north mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials urged Chong to abandon the city and retreat to the northern hills.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「吾受國重恩，忝守籓嶽，淮南萬里，系於吾身，一旦動腳，百姓瓦解，揚州之地，恐非國物。

translations.literal: Chong said: 'I have received the state's heavy grace and am disgracefully guarding this frontier command; the Huai region for ten thousand li depends on my person—once I move my foot, the people will collapse, and the land of Yang Province will likely no longer be the state's possession.
translations.idiomatic: Chong said: 'I owe the state a great debt and guard this frontier in its name. The whole Huai region hangs on me—if I stir, the people will break, and Yang Province may cease to be ours.

sentences.zh: 昔王尊慷慨，義感黃河，吾豈愛一軀，取愧千載。

translations.literal: In former times Wang Zun was impassioned; his righteousness moved the Yellow River—I, how could I cherish one body and bring shame for a thousand years?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zun once held the Yellow River with passionate resolve—how could I cling to my own life and disgrace myself for ages?

sentences.zh: 但憐茲士庶，無辜同死，可桴筏隨高，人規自脫。

translations.literal: Only pity these officials and people, innocent yet dying together—you may raft and follow the high ground, each planning his own escape.
translations.idiomatic: I pity only the innocent people doomed to die with me—let them raft to high ground and save themselves as they can.

sentences.zh: 吾必守死此城。」

translations.literal: I shall surely hold this city and die in it.
translations.idiomatic: I will hold this city unto death.

sentences.zh: 時州人裴絢等受梁假豫州刺史，因乘大水，謀欲為亂，崇皆擊滅之。

translations.literal: At the time Pei Xuan and others of the province received from Liang a false appointment as Governor of Yu Province; taking advantage of the great flood, they plotted rebellion, and Chong struck and destroyed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xuan and others, holding false Liang appointments as Governor of Yu Province, plotted rebellion amid the flood; Chong crushed them all.

sentences.zh: 又以洪水為災，請罪解任。

translations.literal: Also, because the flood was a disaster, he requested punishment and resignation from office.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested punishment and resignation because of the flood disaster.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夏雨氾濫，斯非人力，何得以此辭解。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'Summer rain overflowed—this is not within human power; how can you use this as grounds for resignation?
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: 'Summer floods are beyond human power—you cannot resign on that account.

sentences.zh: 今水涸路通，公私復業，便可繕甲積糧，修復城雉，勞恤士庶，務盡綏懷之略也。」

translations.literal: Now the water has receded and roads are open; public and private have returned to their occupations—you should repair armor, accumulate grain, restore walls and parapets, labor to comfort officials and people, and exhaust every measure of pacification and cherishing.
translations.idiomatic: The waters have fallen, roads are open, and life resumes—repair armor, stock grain, rebuild the walls, and comfort the people with every measure of relief.

sentences.zh: 崇又表解州，不聽。

translations.literal: Chong again memorialized to resign the province; the throne did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Chong again petitioned to resign the governorship; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 是時，非崇則淮南不守矣。

translations.literal: At that time, but for Chong, Huainan would not have been held.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, without Chong, Huainan would not have held.

sentences.zh: 崇沈深有將略，寬厚善禦眾。

translations.literal: Chong was deep and steady, with generalship; generous and good at controlling the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was deep, steady, and skilled in command—generous and adept at leading men.

sentences.zh: 在州凡十年，常養壯士數千人，寇賊侵邊，所向摧破，號曰：「臥彪」，賊甚憚之。

translations.literal: In the province for ten years in all, he constantly maintained several thousand stalwart warriors; when bandits invaded the border, wherever he went he crushed and broke them; he was called 'Crouching Tiger,' and bandits greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years as governor he kept several thousand picked warriors; wherever bandits struck he shattered them. They called him the Crouching Tiger, and enemies feared him greatly.

sentences.zh: 梁武惡其久在淮南，屢設反間，無所不至。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang hated his long stay in Huainan and repeatedly set up counterplots—there was nothing he did not attempt.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang resented his long hold on Huainan and tried every stratagem against him.

sentences.zh: 宣武雅相委重，梁無以措謀。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu greatly entrusted him in turn; Liang had no way to set schemes in motion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu trusted him completely, and Liang could gain no foothold.

sentences.zh: 乃授崇車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、萬戶郡公，諸子皆為縣侯，欲以構崇。

translations.literal: They therefore granted Chong General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of the State with equal ceremony to the Three Dukes, Duke of a Ten-Thousand-Household Commandery—all his sons were made county marquises—intending thereby to alienate Chong.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore heaped honors on him—General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of State with equal ceremony to the Three Dukes, Duke of a ten-thousand-household commandery, all his sons made county marquises—hoping to turn him against the throne.

sentences.zh: 崇表言其狀。

translations.literal: Chong memorialized stating the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Chong memorialized explaining the situation.

sentences.zh: 宣武屢賜璽書慰勉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu repeatedly bestowed sealed letters to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu repeatedly sent sealed letters of comfort and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 賞賜珍異，歲至五三，親待無與為比。

translations.literal: Rewards of rare treasures came five or three times a year; personal favor was unmatched by any.
translations.idiomatic: Rare gifts arrived several times each year; no one enjoyed such personal favor.

sentences.zh: 梁武每歎息，服宣武之能任崇也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang each time sighed and acknowledged Emperor Xuanwu's ability to employ Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang sighed each time, acknowledging Emperor Xuanwu's skill in keeping Chong loyal.

sentences.zh: 孝明踐阼，褒賜衣馬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaoming ascended the throne, he rewarded him with robes and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaoming took the throne, he rewarded Chong with robes and horses.

sentences.zh: 及梁遣其遊擊將軍趙祖悅襲據西硤石，更築外城，逼徙緣淮之人於城內。

translations.literal: When Liang sent its Mobile Commander Zhao Zuyue to strike and seize Western Xiashi, rebuilding the outer wall, forcing the people along the Huai to move within the city—
translations.idiomatic: When Liang sent Mobile Commander Zhao Zuyue to seize Western Xiashi, rebuild its outer wall, and drive the people along the Huai inside the fortifications—

sentences.zh: 又遣二將昌義之、王神念率水軍溯淮而上，規取壽春，田道龍寇邊城，路長平寇五門，胡興茂寇開、霍。

translations.literal: Also sent two generals, Chang Yizhi and Wang Shennian, leading a navy upstream on the Huai, planning to take Shouyang; Tian Daolong raided the border cities, Lu Changping raided Wumen, and Hu Xingmao raided Kai and Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Liang also sent Generals Chang Yizhi and Wang Shennian upstream with a fleet to take Shouyang, while Tian Daolong raided border towns, Lu Changping struck Wumen, and Hu Xingmao attacked Kai and Huo.

sentences.zh: 揚州諸戍，皆被寇逼。

translations.literal: All the garrisons of Yang Province were pressed by enemy raids.
translations.idiomatic: Every garrison in Yang Province came under attack.

sentences.zh: 崇分遣諸將，與之相持；

translations.literal: Chong sent out his generals in separate columns to confront them;
translations.idiomatic: Chong sent his generals to hold the line in separate columns;

sentences.zh: 密裝船艦二百餘艘，教之水戰，以待台軍。

translations.literal: Secretly he fitted out more than two hundred ships, trained them in naval warfare, and waited for the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly fitted out more than two hundred warships, drilled them in naval combat, and waited for the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 梁霍州司馬田休等寇建安，崇遣統軍李神擊走之。

translations.literal: Tian Xiu and others, staff officers of Huo Province under Liang, raided Jian'an; Chong sent Commander Li Shen to strike and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xiu and other Liang officers from Huo Province raided Jian'an; Chong sent Commander Li Shen to drive them off.

sentences.zh: 又命邊城戍主邵申賢要其走路，破之于濡水，俘斬三千餘人。

translations.literal: Also he ordered the border garrison commander Shao Shenxian to intercept their line of retreat and broke them at the Ru River, capturing and beheading more than three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered border commander Shao Shenxian to cut their retreat and routed them at the Ru River, killing or capturing more than three thousand.

sentences.zh: 靈太后璽書勞勉。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling sent a sealed letter of labor and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling sent a sealed letter praising and encouraging him.

sentences.zh: 許昌縣令兼糸甯麻戍主陳平王南引梁軍，以戍歸之。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Xuchang County, concurrently garrison commander of Ningma, Chen Pingwang, led Liang troops southward and surrendered the garrison to them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pingwang, magistrate of Xuchang and garrison commander of Ningma, led Liang troops south and surrendered his post.

sentences.zh: 崇自秋請援，表至下餘，詔遣鎮南將軍崔亮救俠石，鎮東將軍蕭寶夤于梁堰上流決淮東注。

translations.literal: Chong from autumn requested reinforcements; memorials reached the throne in succession; an edict sent General Who Guards the South Cui Liang to relieve Xiashi, and General Who Guards the East Xiao Baoyin to breach the Huai upstream at the Liang embankment and divert the eastern flow.
translations.idiomatic: From autumn Chong pleaded for reinforcements; memorial after memorial reached court. An edict sent Cui Liang to relieve Xiashi and Xiao Baoyin to breach the Liang dam upstream and divert the Huai eastward.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以諸將不相赴，乃以尚書李平兼右僕射持節節度之。

translations.literal: The court, because the generals did not come to one another's aid, then made Minister Li Ping concurrently Vice Director, Bearer of the Staff, to coordinate them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the generals failed to coordinate, the court appointed Minister Li Ping concurrently Vice Director and Bearer of the Staff to direct operations.

sentences.zh: 崇遣李神乘鬥艦百餘艘，沿淮與李平、崔亮合攻硤石。

translations.literal: Chong sent Li Shen with more than a hundred fighting ships along the Huai to join Li Ping and Cui Liang in attacking Xiashi.
translations.idiomatic: Chong sent Li Shen with more than a hundred warships up the Huai to join Li Ping and Cui Liang in the assault on Xiashi.

sentences.zh: 李神水軍克其東北外城。

translations.literal: Li Shen's naval force captured the northeastern outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen's fleet took the northeastern outer wall.

sentences.zh: 祖悅力屈，乃降。

translations.literal: Zuyue's strength was exhausted and he then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyue's resistance collapsed and he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，進號驃騎將軍、儀同三司，刺史、都督如故。

translations.literal: The court praised this and advanced his title to General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of State with equal ceremony to the Three Dukes; Governor and Commander-in-Chief remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended the victory and promoted him to General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of State with equal ceremony to the Three Dukes; his governorship and command remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 梁淮堰未破，水勢日增。

translations.literal: Liang's Huai embankment was not yet broken, and the water's force increased daily.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Huai dam still held, and the flood grew daily.

sentences.zh: 崇乃于硤石戍間編舟為橋。

translations.literal: Chong then between the Xiashi garrisons lashed boats together to make a bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Chong lashed boats into a bridge between the Xiashi garrisons.

sentences.zh: 北更立船樓十，各高三丈；

translations.literal: To the north he further erected ten ship-towers, each three zhang high;
translations.idiomatic: North of the bridge he erected ten ship-towers, each three zhang high;

sentences.zh: 十步置一籬，至兩岸，蕃版裝治，四箱解合，賊至舉用，不戰解下。

translations.literal: Every ten paces a fence was placed, reaching both banks; boards were fitted and finished in four sections that joined and separated—when enemies came they were raised for use, and without fighting they could be lowered.
translations.idiomatic: Every ten paces he set palisades to both banks, with hinged plank sections that could be raised against attack and lowered in peace.

sentences.zh: 又于樓船之北，連覆大船，東西竟水，防賊火筏。

translations.literal: Also north of the tower-ships he linked covered great ships east and west across the water to guard against enemy fire-rafts.
translations.idiomatic: North of the tower-ships he moored covered barges across the river to block enemy fire-rafts.

sentences.zh: 又于八公山之東南，更起一城，以備大水，州人號曰魏昌城。

translations.literal: Also southeast of Bagong Mountain he further raised a city to guard against great flood; the people of the province called it Weichang City.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of Bagong Mountain he built another city against flood—the people called it Weichang City.

sentences.zh: 崇累表解州，前後十餘上，孝明乃以元志代之。

translations.literal: Chong repeatedly memorialized to resign the province, more than ten times in all; Emperor Xiaoming then replaced him with Yuan Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chong petitioned to resign more than ten times; at last Emperor Xiaoming replaced him with Yuan Zhi.

sentences.zh: 尋除中書監、驃騎大將軍，儀同如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed as Supervisor of the Secretariat and General of Agile Cavalry; Grand Master of State remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Supervisor of the Secretariat and General of Agile Cavalry, retaining his rank as Grand Master of State.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、侍中、都督四州諸軍事、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of the Four Provinces, and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He left court as Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of four provinces, and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 徵拜尚書左僕射，遷尚書令，加侍中。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing, and additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, promoted to Director, and additionally made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 崇在官和厚，明於決斷，然性好財賄，敗肆聚斂。

translations.literal: Chong in office was harmonious and generous, clear in decision—but by nature he loved wealth and bribes, and openly gathered riches.
translations.idiomatic: In office Chong was fair and decisive, yet he loved wealth, took bribes, and openly amassed riches.

sentences.zh: 孝明、靈太后嘗幸左藏，王公嬪主從者百餘人，皆令任力負布絹，即以賜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoming and Empress Dowager Ling once visited the Left Treasury; more than a hundred princes, dukes, consorts, and princesses followed, and all were ordered to carry cloth and silk according to their strength—and it was at once bestowed on them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming and Empress Dowager Ling once visited the Left Treasury; more than a hundred nobles and consorts followed, each ordered to carry as much silk as he or she could—and it was given them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 多者過二百匹，少者百餘。

translations.literal: Those who took more passed two hundred bolts; those who took less, a hundred-odd.
translations.idiomatic: The strongest carried more than two hundred bolts; the weakest still took a hundred or more.

sentences.zh: 唯長樂公兩手持絹二十匹而出，示不異眾而已，世稱其廉儉。

translations.literal: Only the Prince of Changle took twenty bolts of silk in both hands and went out, showing he was not different from the crowd—that alone; the age praised his frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Prince of Changle carried out twenty bolts in both hands, making a show of modesty—the age praised his thrift.

sentences.zh: 崇與章武王融以所負多，顛仆於地，崇乃傷腰，融至損腳。

translations.literal: Chong and Prince Zhangwu Rong, because they carried much, fell prostrate to the ground—Chong injured his waist, and Rong even damaged his leg.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Prince Zhangwu Rong, greedy for more, fell under their loads—Chong hurt his back, Rong broke his leg.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「陳留、章武，傷腰折股，貪人敗類，穢我明主。」

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying of it: 'Chenliu and Zhangwu, hurt waist and broken thigh—greedy men, a disgrace to our bright lord.'
translations.idiomatic: People mocked them in verse: 'Chenliu and Zhangwu—broken back, broken leg; greedy wretches shaming our bright sovereign.'

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕主阿那瑰犯塞，詔崇以本官都督北討諸軍事以討之。

translations.literal: The Rouran ruler Anagui violated the frontier; an edict made Chong, in his original office, Commander-in-Chief of the northern campaign to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran ruler Anagui raided the frontier, Chong was ordered, in his existing office, to command the northern campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 崇辭于顯陽殿，戎服武飾，志氣奮揚，時年六十九，幹力如少。

translations.literal: Chong took leave at Xianyang Hall in martial dress and military adornment, his spirit high and vigorous; he was then sixty-nine, yet his strength like a young man's.
translations.idiomatic: Chong bid farewell at Xianyang Hall in full armor, spirit blazing; he was sixty-nine yet strong as a young man.

sentences.zh: 孝明目而壯之，朝臣莫不稱善。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoming looked on him and found him imposing; no court official failed to praise it as good.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming looked on him with admiration; every courtier praised the sight.

sentences.zh: 遂出塞三千餘里，不及賊而還。

translations.literal: He then went beyond the frontier more than three thousand li, did not overtake the bandits, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He marched more than three thousand li beyond the frontier, failed to catch the enemy, and returned.

sentences.zh: 崇請改六鎮為州，兵編戶，太后不許。

translations.literal: Chong requested changing the Six Garrisons into provinces and registering the soldiers as households; the empress dowager did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong petitioned to convert the Six Garrisons into provinces and register soldiers as taxpayers; the empress dowager refused.

sentences.zh: 後北鎮人破落汗拔陵反，所在回應。

translations.literal: Later the men of the northern garrisons, Po Luohan and Ba Ling, rebelled; everywhere people responded in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Later Po Luohan and Ba Ling of the northern garrisons rebelled, and uprisings spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 征北將軍、臨淮王彧大敗于五原，安北將軍李叔仁尋敗于白道，賊眾日甚。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the North, Prince Linhuai Yu, was greatly defeated at Wuyuan; General Who Pacifies the North Li Shuren was soon defeated at Baidao—the rebel host grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Linhuai Yu, General Who Conquers the North, was routed at Wuyuan; Li Shuren, General Who Pacifies the North, was soon beaten at Baidao—the rebels swelled daily.

sentences.zh: 詔引丞相、令、僕、尚書、侍中、黃門于顯陽殿，曰：「賊勢侵淫，寇連恆，朔，金陵在彼，夙夜憂惶。

translations.literal: An edict summoned the Chancellor, Director, Vice Directors, Ministers, Palace Attendants, and Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate to Xianyang Hall, saying: 'The rebels' force spreads and encroaches; bandits link Heng and Shuo; Jinling is over there—we worry day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The throne summoned the chancellor, directors, ministers, and attendants to Xianyang Hall: 'The rebels spread unchecked from Heng and Shuo; Jinling lies beyond them—we fret day and night.

sentences.zh: 諸人宜陳良策。」

translations.literal: All of you should set forth good plans.
translations.idiomatic: Present your best plans.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書元修義以為須得重貴，鎮壓壓恆、朔，總彼師旅，備衛金湯。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Yuan Xiuyi considered that one must obtain a man of heavy rank to suppress and hold Heng and Shuo, command those armies, and guard the golden ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Yuan Xiuyi argued that a man of the highest rank must hold Heng and Shuo, command the armies, and guard the frontier fortresses.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「去歲阿那瑰叛逆，遣李崇北征，崇遂長驅塞北，返旆榆關，此一時之盛。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'Last year Anagui rebelled; Li Chong was sent on the northern campaign; Chong then drove straight through the northern frontier and returned his banners at Yuguan—this was a moment of glory.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: 'Last year Anagui rebelled and Li Chong was sent north. He marched deep into the frontier and returned in triumph through Yuguan—that was a moment of glory.

sentences.zh: 朕以李崇國戚望重，器識英斷，意欲還遣崇行，總督三軍，揚旌恆、朔，諸人謂可爾不？」

translations.literal: We consider Li Chong a kinsman of the state, heavy in reputation, excellent and decisive in talent and insight, and intend to send Chong again, commanding the three armies, raising banners at Heng and Shuo—do you all think this acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong is a royal kinsman of weight and reputation, skilled and resolute. I mean to send him again to command the three armies on the Heng-Shuo front—is that your wish?

sentences.zh: 僕射蕭寶夤等曰：「陛下此遣，實合群望。」

translations.literal: Vice Director Xiao Baoyin and others said: 'Your Majesty's dispatch on this occasion truly accords with the hopes of the multitude.'
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xiao Baoyin and others replied: 'Your Majesty's choice truly matches the hopes of all.'

sentences.zh: 於是詔崇以本官加使持節、開府、北討大都督，撫軍將軍崔暹、鎮軍廣陽王深皆受崇節度。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict made Chong, in his original office, additionally Bearer of the Staff, Opener of a Government Office, Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign; Pacifying General Cui Xuan and Suppressing General Prince Guangyang Shen all received Chong's direction.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was then appointed additionally Bearer of the Staff, Opener of a Government Office, and Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign; Cui Xuan and Prince Guangyang Shen served under his command.

sentences.zh: 又詔崇子光祿大夫神軌假平北將軍，隨崇北討。

translations.literal: Also an edict made Chong's son, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Shengui, acting General Who Pacifies the North, following Chong on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's son Shengui, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, was made acting General Who Pacifies the North and sent north with him.

sentences.zh: 崇至五原，崔暹大敗于白道之北，賊遂並力攻崇。

translations.literal: When Chong reached Wuyuan, Cui Xuan was greatly defeated north of Baidao; the bandits then combined their strength to attack Chong.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuyuan, Cui Xuan was routed north of Baidao; the rebels then massed against Chong.

sentences.zh: 崇與廣陽王深力戰，累破賊眾。

translations.literal: Chong and Prince Guangyang Shen fought hard and repeatedly broke the rebel host.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Prince Guangyang Shen fought hard and repeatedly broke the rebels.

sentences.zh: 相持至冬，乃引還平城。

translations.literal: They confronted each other until winter, then withdrew to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: They held the line until winter, then withdrew to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 深表崇長史祖瑩詐增功級，盜沒軍資。

translations.literal: Shen reported that Chong's chief clerk Zu Ying had falsely inflated merit grades and embezzled military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shen accused Chong's chief clerk Zu Ying of inflating merit rolls and embezzling supplies.

sentences.zh: 崇坐免官爵，征還，以後事付深。

translations.literal: Chong was punished by removal from office and rank, summoned back, and later affairs were entrusted to Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was stripped of office and rank, recalled, and Shen was left to manage affairs.

sentences.zh: 後徐州刺史元法僧以彭城南叛，時除安樂王鑒為徐州刺史以討之。

translations.literal: Later the Governor of Xuzhou, Yuan Faseng, rebelled with Pengcheng to the south; at the time Prince Anle Jian was appointed Governor of Xuzhou to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan Faseng, Governor of Xuzhou, rebelled and held Pengcheng; Prince Anle Jian was appointed Governor of Xuzhou to subdue him.

sentences.zh: 為法僧所敗，單馬之。

translations.literal: He was defeated by Faseng and fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was defeated by Faseng and fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 乃詔復崇官爵，為徐州大都督、節度諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict then restored Chong's office and rank; he was made Grand Commander of Xuzhou and Coordinator of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Chong's titles and made him Grand Commander of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會崇疾篤，乃以衛將軍、安豐王延明代之。

translations.literal: As it happened Chong was gravely ill; therefore General of the Guard Prince Yan of Anfeng was sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Chong fell gravely ill, so Prince Yan of Anfeng was sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 改除開府、相州刺史，侍中、將軍、儀同並如故。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Opener of a Government Office and Governor of Xiang Province; Palace Attendant, General, and Grand Master of State all remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Opener of a Government Office and Governor of Xiang Province, retaining his other titles.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年，薨於位。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaochang he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、司徒公、雍州刺史，諡曰武康，後重贈太尉公，余如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of the Ministry of Education, and Governor of Yong Province, with posthumous title Wukang; later he was again granted Grand Duke of the Ministry of Education, the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of the Ministry of Education, and Governor of Yong Province, with posthumous name Wukang; later he was further honored as Grand Duke of the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 長子世哲，性輕率，供奉豪侈。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shizhe was frivolous by nature and extravagant in serving the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shizhe was frivolous by nature and lived lavishly among the powerful.

sentences.zh: 少經征伐，頗有將用，為三關別將，討群蠻大破之。

translations.literal: In youth he went on campaigns and had considerable use as a general; he was Separate Commander of the Three Passes and greatly broke the barbarian bands in attack.
translations.idiomatic: Young he saw campaign service and showed real military talent; as Separate Commander of the Three Passes he routed barbarian bands.

sentences.zh: 還，拜鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 性傾巧，善事人，亦以貨賂自達。

translations.literal: By nature he was clever and artful, good at winning people, and also advanced himself through bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and ingratiating, he also bought his way forward with bribes.

sentences.zh: 高肇、劉騰之勢也，皆與親善，故世號為李錐。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhao and Liu Teng were in power, he was on intimate terms with both; therefore the age called him Li Zhui.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhao and Liu Teng held power he cultivated both; the age called him Li Zhui—'Li the awl.'

sentences.zh: 為相州刺史，斥逐百姓，遷徙佛寺，逼買其地，部內患之。

translations.literal: As Governor of Xiang Province he drove out the common people, moved Buddhist temples, and forced purchase of their land—the district suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: As Governor of Xiang Province he expelled commoners, seized temple lands, and forced purchases—the region groaned under him.

sentences.zh: 崇北征之後，征兼太常卿。

translations.literal: After Chong's northern campaign he was summoned and additionally made Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: After Chong's northern campaign he was recalled and additionally made Director of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 御史高道穆毀發其宅，表其罪過。

translations.literal: The censor Gao Daomu opened and exposed his residence and memorialized his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Gao Daomu raided his mansion and memorialized his crimes.

sentences.zh: 後除涇州刺史，賜爵衛國子。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Jing Province and granted the title Viscount of Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Governor of Jing Province and enfeoffed as Viscount of Weiguo.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈吏部尚書、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Minister of Personnel and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Minister of Personnel and Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 世哲弟神軌，小名青肫，受父爵陳留侯。

translations.literal: Shizhe's younger brother Shengui, with childhood name Qingzhun, inherited his father's title Marquis of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhe's younger brother Shengui, known in youth as Qingzhun, inherited the marquisate of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 累出征伐，頗有將領之氣。

translations.literal: Repeatedly going on campaigns, he had considerable air of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated campaigns gave him the bearing of a commander.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，靈太后淫縱，分遣腹心媼姬出外，陰求悅人。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era Empress Dowager Ling was licentious and unrestrained; she sent trusted wet-nurses and concubines abroad to secretly seek men who pleased her.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era Empress Dowager Ling lived licentiously and sent trusted nurses and concubines abroad to seek lovers in secret.

sentences.zh: 神軌為使者所薦，寵遇勢傾朝野，時雲見幸帷幄，與鄭儼為雙。

translations.literal: Shengui was recommended by an envoy, favored until his power tilted court and realm; at the time it was said he was intimate within the inner chambers, paired with Zheng Yan.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy recommended Shengui; his favor tilted the court and it was whispered he shared the empress dowager's bed with Zheng Yan.

sentences.zh: 頻遷征東將軍、武衛將軍、給事黃門侍郎，常領中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General Who Conquers the East, General of the Martial Guard, and Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, constantly holding the post of Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to General Who Conquers the East, General of the Martial Guard, and Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, constantly serving as Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時相州刺史、安樂王鑒據州反，詔神軌與都督源子邕等討平之。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Anle Jian, Governor of Xiang Province, held the province and rebelled; an edict made Shengui, together with Commander Yuan Ziyin and others, attack and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Anle Jian rebelled and held Xiang Province, Shengui was ordered with Commander Yuan Ziyin and others to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 後於河陰遇害。

translations.literal: Later he met disaster at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 建義初，贈侍中、司空公、相州刺史，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: Early in the Jianyi era he was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Governor of Xiang Province, with posthumous title Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyi era he was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Governor of Xiang Province, with posthumous name Lie.

sentences.zh: 崇從弟平。

translations.literal: Chong's younger cousin Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's younger cousin Ping.

sentences.zh: 平字雲定，少有大度；

translations.literal: Ping, styled Yunding, in youth had great breadth of mind;
translations.idiomatic: Ping, styled Yunding, showed great breadth of mind even in youth;

sentences.zh: 及長，涉獵群書，好《禮》、《易》，頗在文才。

translations.literal: When grown he ranged through many books, loved the Rites and the Changes, and had considerable literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he read widely, loved the Rites and the Changes, and possessed real literary talent.

sentences.zh: 太和初，拜通直散騎侍郎，孝文禮之甚重。

translations.literal: Early in the Taihe era he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Palace Gate; Emperor Xiaowen honored him with great weight.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe era he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Palace Gate; Emperor Xiaowen held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 頻經大憂，居喪以孝稱。

translations.literal: He repeatedly passed through great bereavements and in mourning was praised for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He endured repeated bereavements and was praised for filial mourning.

sentences.zh: 後以例降，襲爵彭城公。

translations.literal: Later, by precedent his rank was reduced; he inherited the title Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by precedent his rank was reduced and he inherited the dukedom of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子庶子。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 平請自效一郡，帝曰：「卿復欲以吏事自試也？」

translations.literal: Ping requested to prove himself in one commandery; the emperor said: 'Do you again wish to test yourself in administrative affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Ping asked to prove himself in a single commandery; the emperor said: 'Do you wish to test yourself in office again?

sentences.zh: 拜長樂太守，政務清靜，吏人懷之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Changle; his governance was clear and tranquil, and officials and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Changle; his rule was calm and clear, and officials and people loved him.

sentences.zh: 征行河南尹，豪右權戚憚之。

translations.literal: He was summoned to act as Intendant of Henan; powerful clans and kin of the mighty feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to act as Intendant of Henan, he was feared by powerful families and imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 宣武即位，除黃門郎，遷司徒左長史，行尹如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne he was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, promoted to Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Education, and continued to act as Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne he was made Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, promoted to Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Education, and continued as acting Intendant.

sentences.zh: 尋正尹，長史如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was made regular Intendant; Senior Clerk remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon confirmed as Intendant while retaining the senior clerkship.

sentences.zh: 車騎將幸鄴，平上表諫，以為：「嵩都創構，洛邑俶營，雖年跨十稔，根基未就。

translations.literal: When the General of Chariots and Cavalry was about to visit Ye, Ping submitted a memorial of remonstrance, considering: 'The capital at Song was newly founded and Luoyang just begun—though years crossed more than ten, the foundations were not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned to visit Ye, Ping remonstrated: 'Song's capital was newly raised and Luoyang just begun—though more than ten years have passed, the foundations are still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 代人至洛，始欲向盡，資產罄于遷移，牛畜斃於輦運；

translations.literal: The northerners reaching Luoyang at first intended to use up all they had; assets were exhausted in migration, cattle and livestock died in cart transport;
translations.idiomatic: Northerners reaching Luoyang spent themselves to the last; fortunes vanished in the move, livestock perished on the road;

sentences.zh: 陵太行之險，越長津之難，辛勤備經，劣達京闕；

translations.literal: Crossing the peril of Mount Taihang, surpassing the difficulty of the long ford—they toiled through every hardship and barely reached the capital gates;
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the dangers of Mount Taihang and the long fords, endured every hardship, and barely reached the capital;

sentences.zh: 富者猶損太半，貧者可以意知。

translations.literal: The rich still lost more than half; the poor can be imagined.
translations.idiomatic: Even the wealthy lost more than half their substance; the poor suffered far worse.

sentences.zh: 兼曆歲從戎，不遑啟處。

translations.literal: Moreover for years they followed the army and had no leisure to settle.
translations.idiomatic: For years they had followed campaigns and had no rest.

sentences.zh: 自景明以來，差得休息。

translations.literal: From the Jingming era onward they had barely obtained rest.
translations.idiomatic: Only since the Jingming era have they had any respite.

sentences.zh: 事農者未積一年之儲，築室者裁有數間之屋，莫不肆力伊、瀍，人急其務。

translations.literal: Those who worked the fields had not yet stored a year's grain; those who built houses had scarcely a few rooms—none failed to exert strength on the Yi and Chan, each man urgent in his task.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers had not yet laid up a year's grain; builders had only a few rooms—everyone labored on the Yi and Chan, each urgent in his work.

sentences.zh: 實宜安靜新人，勸其稼穡，令國有九載之糧，家有水旱之備。

translations.literal: Truly one should quietly settle the new people, encourage their farming and mulberry culture, so that the state has nine years' grain and households have provision against flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: This is the time to settle the newcomers in peace, encourage farming and sericulture, store nine years' grain for the state, and keep every household prepared for drought and flood.

sentences.zh: 若乘之以羈絏，則所廢多矣。」

translations.literal: If one drives them with bridles and fetters, then what is abandoned will be much.
translations.idiomatic: Drive them with bridles and shackles now, and far more will be lost.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: The throne did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 詔以本官行相州事。

translations.literal: An edict made him, in his original office, act as Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him, in his existing office, acting Governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 帝至鄴，親幸平第，見其諸子。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Ye he personally visited Ping's residence and saw his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Ye he visited Ping's home and met his sons.

sentences.zh: 尋正刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made regular Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon confirmed as governor.

sentences.zh: 平勸課農桑，修飾太學，簡試通儒以充博士，選五郡聰敏者以教之。

translations.literal: Ping encouraged farming and sericulture, restored the Imperial Academy, selected tested Confucian scholars to fill the posts of erudites, and chose clever men from five commanderies to teach them.
translations.idiomatic: Ping promoted farming and sericulture, restored the Imperial Academy, appointed tested Confucians as erudites, and chose bright students from five commanderies to instruct.

sentences.zh: 圖孔子及七十二弟子于講堂，親為立贊。

translations.literal: He painted Confucius and the seventy-two disciples in the lecture hall and personally composed encomia for them.
translations.idiomatic: He painted Confucius and the seventy-two disciples in the lecture hall and wrote encomia for each.

sentences.zh: 前來台使，頗好侵漁。

translations.literal: Previously when envoys from the capital came, they greatly loved to encroach and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from the capital had long been fond of extortion and plunder.

sentences.zh: 平乃畫「履武尾，踐薄冰」於客館，注頌其下，以示誡焉。

translations.literal: Ping then painted "treading the tiger's tail, treading thin ice" in the guest lodge, inscribing a praise-poem beneath it, to show them a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Ping then painted the words "treading the tiger's tail, treading thin ice" in the guest lodge and inscribed a verse beneath as a warning to the envoys.

sentences.zh: 徵拜度支尚書，領御史中尉。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue, concurrently holding the post of Imperial Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed minister of revenue, concurrently serving as chief imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 冀州刺史、京兆王愉反於信都，以平為持節、都督北討諸軍事、行冀州以討之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingzhao, Yu, Governor of Jizhou, rebelled at Xindu; Ping was made Commissioner with Imperial Staff, Commander of the Northern Expeditionary Forces, and Acting Governor of Jizhou to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jingzhao, Yu, governor of Jizhou, rebelled at Xindu, Ping was appointed commissioner with the imperial staff, commander of all northern expeditionary forces, and acting governor of Jizhou to suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 宣武臨式乾殿勞遣平，因曰：何圖今日，言及斯事！」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu came to Shiqian Hall to comfort and dispatch Ping, and said in the course of it: Who would have thought that today we should speak of such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu came to Shiqian Hall to see Ping off and said, "Who could have imagined we would be speaking of such a thing today!"

sentences.zh: 歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: He sighed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and wept.

sentences.zh: 平對曰：「愉天迷其心，構此梟悖。

translations.literal: Ping replied: "Yu, heaven having bewildered his heart, has contrived this rebellious wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Ping replied, "Heaven has maddened Yu's mind and driven him to this treasonous wickedness.

sentences.zh: 陛下不以臣不武，委以總督之任。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, not deeming your servant unwarlike, has entrusted me with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has not judged me unfit for war and has entrusted me with supreme command.

sentences.zh: 如其稽顙軍門，則送之大理。

translations.literal: If he prostrates himself at the army gate, then send him to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: If he comes to the camp gate and submits, send him to the court of judicial review.

sentences.zh: 若不悛待戮，則鳴鼓釁鉦，非陛下之事。」

translations.literal: If he will not repent and awaits execution, then sound the drums and consecrate the axes—these are not matters for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: If he refuses to repent and awaits punishment, then the drums will be beaten and the axes consecrated—that will not be Your Majesty's concern.

sentences.zh: 平進次經縣，諸軍大集。

translations.literal: Ping advanced and halted at Jing County; the armies assembled in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Ping marched forward and encamped at Jing County, where the armies massed in strength.

sentences.zh: 夜有蠻兵數千斫平前壘，矢及平帳，平堅臥不動，俄而乃定。

translations.literal: At night several thousand barbarian troops attacked Ping's forward rampart; arrows reached Ping's tent, yet Ping lay firm without moving, and soon all was settled.
translations.idiomatic: That night several thousand tribal soldiers stormed the forward ramparts; arrows struck Ping's tent, but he lay still without moving, and before long all was quiet.

sentences.zh: 遂至冀州城南十六里，大破逆眾，逐北至城門，遂圍城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he reached sixteen li south of Jizhou city, routed the rebels in a great defeat, pursued them north to the city gate, and then besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to a point sixteen li south of Jizhou, routed the rebels, drove them north to the city gate, and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 愉與百餘騎突門走，平遣統軍叔孫頭追之。

translations.literal: Yu with a hundred-odd horsemen burst through the gate and fled; Ping sent the commanding general Shusun Tou in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yu broke through the gate with a little over a hundred horsemen and fled; Ping sent Commander Shusun Tou in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 去信都八十里，禽愉。

translations.literal: Eighty li from Xindu, Yu was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty li from Xindu, they captured Yu.

sentences.zh: 冀州平，以本官領相州大中正。

translations.literal: When Jizhou was pacified, he retained his original office and additionally held the post of Senior Rectifier of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Jizhou was pacified, he kept his original rank and was also made senior rectifier of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 平先為尚書令高肇、侍御史王顯所恨，後顯代平為中尉，平加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Ping had earlier been hated by Chief Minister Gao Zhao and Attending Censor Wang Xian; later Xian replaced Ping as censor-in-chief, and Ping was additionally made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Ping had long been resented by Chief Minister Gao Zhao and Attending Censor Wang Xian; later Xian replaced Ping as chief censor, while Ping was promoted to regular attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 顯劾平在冀州隱截官口，肇又扶成其狀，奏除平名。

translations.literal: Xian impeached Ping for secretly intercepting corvée laborers in Jizhou; Zhao further helped establish the case, and memorialized to strike Ping's name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Xian impeached Ping for secretly seizing corvée laborers in Jizhou; Zhao helped build the case, and a memorial was submitted to strike Ping from office.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，詔復官爵，除定、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yanchang era an edict restored his offices and enfeoffments; he was appointed Governor of Ding and Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yanchang era an edict restored his rank and titles, and he was appointed governor of both Ding and Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 前來良賤之訟，多有積年不決；

translations.literal: Lawsuits over free persons and bond servants that had accumulated over many years without resolution were many;
translations.idiomatic: Many lawsuits over the status of free persons and bond servants had piled up for years without resolution;

sentences.zh: 平奏不問真偽，一以景明年前為限，於是諍訟止息。

translations.literal: Ping memorialized that without inquiring into truth or falsehood all should be limited to before the Jingming era, and thereupon contentious litigation ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Ping petitioned that all such cases, without regard to their merits, be dismissed if they arose before the Jingming era, and contentious litigation came to an end.

sentences.zh: 武川鎮人饑，鎮將任款請貸未許，擅開倉振恤，有司繩以費散之條，免其官爵。

translations.literal: The people of Wuchuan Garrison were starving; the garrison commander Ren Kuan requested a loan but was not permitted, yet he on his own opened the granary for relief; the relevant offices charged him under the statute on wasteful dispersal and stripped him of office and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Wuchuan Garrison were starving, Garrison Commander Ren Kuan asked for a grain loan but was refused; he opened the granaries on his own to give relief, and the authorities charged him with unlawful disbursement and stripped him of office and rank.

sentences.zh: 平奏款意在濟人，心無不善，帝原之。

translations.literal: Ping memorialized that Kuan's intent was to aid the people and his heart harbored no ill will; the emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Ping submitted that Kuan had meant only to save lives and harbored no evil intent, and the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 遷中書令，尚書如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat; his ministry post remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the secretariat while retaining his ministry post.

sentences.zh: 孝明初，轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming's reign he was moved to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming's reign he was made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 平高明強濟，所在有聲，但以性急為累。

translations.literal: Ping was lofty and bright, forceful and capable; wherever he served he won renown, yet only his quick temper was a handicap.
translations.idiomatic: Ping was brilliant and forceful; wherever he served he earned a reputation, though his quick temper was held against him.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、任城王澄奏理平定冀之勳，靈太后乃封武邑郡公，賜縑二千五百匹。

translations.literal: Chief Minister, the Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, memorialized to settle the merit of pacifying Jizhou; Empress Dowager Ling then enfeoffed him as Duke of Wuyi Commandery and bestowed twenty-five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Cheng, Prince of Rencheng, submitted a memorial settling Ping's merit in pacifying Jizhou; Empress Dowager Ling then enfeoffed him as Duke of Wuyi Commandery and granted him two thousand five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 先是，梁遣其趙祖悅逼壽春，鎮南崔亮攻之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liang had sent Zhao Zuyue to press upon Shouyang; the Defender of the South, Cui Liang, attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liang had sent Zhao Zuyue to threaten Shouyang, and Cui Liang, defender of the south, besieged him.

sentences.zh: 未克，又與李崇乖貳。

translations.literal: He could not take it, and moreover fell into discord with Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: The siege failed, and Cui Liang moreover fell out with Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 詔平以本官使持節、鎮軍大將軍，兼尚書左僕射為行台，節度諸軍，東西州將，一以稟之，如有乖異，以軍法從事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Ping, in his original office, Commissioner with Imperial Staff, Great General Who Pacifies the Army, and concurrently Left Vice Minister acting as Mobile Headquarters, to command all armies; Eastern and Western provincial generals were all to report to him, and where there was disobedience, military law would be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Ping was ordered, retaining his existing rank, to serve as commissioner with the imperial staff and great general who pacifies the army, concurrently left vice minister and head of the mobile headquarters, with command over all armies; eastern and western provincial generals were to obey him, and insubordination would be punished by military law.

sentences.zh: 詔平長子獎以通直郎從。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ping's eldest son Jiang to accompany him as Attendant Direct-from-the-Source.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's eldest son Jiang was ordered to accompany him as attendant direct-from-the-source.

sentences.zh: 於是率步騎二千赴壽春，嚴勒崇、亮，令水陸兼備，克期齊舉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led two thousand infantry and cavalry to Shouyang, strictly restraining Chong and Liang, ordering both land and water forces fully prepared to strike together on the set day.
translations.idiomatic: He then led two thousand infantry and cavalry to Shouyang, tightened discipline over Chong and Liang, and ordered land and naval forces to be fully ready for a coordinated assault on the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 崇、亮憚之，無敢乖互。

translations.literal: Chong and Liang feared him and did not dare to be at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Liang feared him and did not dare to defy one another.

sentences.zh: 頻日交戰，破賊軍。

translations.literal: Day after day they joined battle and broke the enemy army.
translations.idiomatic: After days of fighting they routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 安南將軍崔延伯立橋于下蔡，以拒賊之援，賊將王神念、昌義之等不得進救。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the South Cui Yanbo built a bridge at Xia Cai to block enemy reinforcements; the enemy generals Wang Shennian, Chang Yizhi, and others could not advance to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanbo, general who pacifies the south, built a bridge at Xia Cai to block enemy reinforcements, so the enemy generals Wang Shennian, Chang Yizhi, and others could not advance to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 祖悅守死窮城，平乃部分攻之，斬祖悅，送首於洛。

translations.literal: Zuyue defended the besieged city to the death; Ping then deployed forces to attack, beheaded Zuyue, and sent the head to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyue held the doomed city to the end; Ping organized the assault, killed Zuyue, and sent his head to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 以功遷尚書右僕射，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: For merit he was moved to Right Vice Minister and additionally made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: For this feat he was promoted to right vice minister and additionally made regular attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 平還京師，靈太后見於宣光殿，賜以金裝刀仗一口。

translations.literal: When Ping returned to the capital, Empress Dowager Ling received him in Xuanguang Hall and bestowed one set of gold-mounted sword and staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Ping returned to the capital, Empress Dowager Ling received him in Xuanguang Hall and granted him a gold-mounted sword and staff.

sentences.zh: 時南徐州表云：梁堰淮水，日為患。

translations.literal: At the time South Xuzhou reported: Liang had dammed the Huai River, which daily became a menace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time South Xuzhou reported that Liang had dammed the Huai River, which was becoming a daily menace.

sentences.zh: 詔公卿議之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the high ministers to deliberate on it.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the chief ministers to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 平以為不假兵力，終自毀壞。

translations.literal: Ping held that without needing military force it would in the end destroy itself.
translations.idiomatic: Ping argued that the dam needed no military action and would eventually collapse on its own.

sentences.zh: 及淮堰破，太后大悅，引群臣入宴，敕平前，孝明手賜縑布百段。

translations.literal: When the Huai dam broke, the Dowager was greatly pleased; she led the ministers in to feast, ordered Ping forward, and Emperor Xiaoming personally bestowed a hundred bolts of silk and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai dam broke, the empress dowager was delighted; she brought the ministers in to feast, summoned Ping forward, and Emperor Xiaoming personally granted him a hundred bolts of silk and cloth.

sentences.zh: 卒，遺令薄葬。

translations.literal: He died; his final instructions were for a simple burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died and left instructions for a simple burial.

sentences.zh: 詔給東園秘器、朝服一具、衣一襲、帛七百匹。

translations.literal: An edict granted Eastern Garden secret vessels, one set of court robes, one suit of clothing, and seven hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him the secret burial vessels of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, one suit of clothing, and seven hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 靈太后為舉哀於東堂。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling held mourning for him in the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling held mourning rites for him in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、冀州刺史，諡文烈公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, Palace Equal to the Three Lords, and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Duke Wenlie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant, grand general of rapid cavalry, palace equal to the three lords, and governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Duke Wenlie.

sentences.zh: 平自在度支，至於端副，夙夜在公，孜孜匪懈，凡處機密十有餘年，有獻替之稱。

translations.literal: From the time Ping was in the Revenue Ministry until he became vice minister at the apex of government, morning and night he was at his duties, tireless and unslackening; altogether he handled confidential matters for more than ten years and won praise for helpful counsel.
translations.idiomatic: From his years in the revenue ministry through his service as a vice minister at the head of government, Ping worked day and night without slackening; for more than ten years he handled sensitive affairs and was praised for offering good counsel.

sentences.zh: 所制文筆別有集錄。

translations.literal: The writings and drafts he composed were separately collected in a compilation.
translations.idiomatic: His compositions were collected in a separate anthology.

sentences.zh: 長子獎襲。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jiang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jiang inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 獎字遵穆，容貌魁偉，有當世才度。

translations.literal: Jiang's style name was Zunmu; his appearance was imposing and grand, and he had talent and bearing for his age.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, style name Zunmu, was imposing in appearance and possessed the talent and bearing befitting his generation.

sentences.zh: 位中書侍郎、吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Vice Director of the Secretariat and Director of the Personnel Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice director of the secretariat and director of the personnel bureau.

sentences.zh: 以本官兼尚書，出為相州刺史。

translations.literal: In his original office he additionally held the Ministry and went out as Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While retaining his original rank he additionally served in the ministry and was posted out as governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，元叉擅朝，獎為其親待，頻居顯職。

translations.literal: At first, when Yuan Cha monopolized the court, Jiang was his intimate favorite and repeatedly held eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when Yuan Cha dominated the court, Jiang was a favorite and repeatedly held high office.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，削除官爵。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling resumed power, his offices and enfeoffments were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling resumed power, his offices and titles were taken away.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，為散騎常侍、河南尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was made regular attendant-in-ordinary and intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 獎前後所曆，皆以明濟著稱。

translations.literal: In all the posts Jiang held before and after, he was famed for clarity and competence.
translations.idiomatic: In every post Jiang held, he was known for clear and capable administration.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，顥以獎兼尚書右僕射，慰勞徐州。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Hao made Jiang concurrently Right Vice Minister to comfort Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he appointed Jiang concurrent right vice minister to go and reassure Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 羽林及城人不承顥旨，害獎，傳首洛陽。

translations.literal: The Feathered Forest Guard and the people of the city did not accept Hao's orders; they killed Jiang and sent his head to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial guards and the townspeople refused to obey Yuan Hao and killed Jiang, sending his head to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝初，獎故吏宋遊道上書理獎，詔贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, Jiang's former subordinate Song Youdao submitted a memorial to vindicate Jiang; an edict posthumously granted him Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, Jiang's former subordinate Song Youdao petitioned to clear his name, and he was posthumously granted the title governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 子構襲。

translations.literal: His son Gou inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gou inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 構字祖基，少以方正見稱，襲爵武邑郡公。

translations.literal: Gou's style name was Zuji; in youth he was famed for uprightness, and he inherited the dukedom of Wuyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gou, style name Zuji, was known from youth for integrity and inherited the dukedom of Wuyi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，降爵為縣侯，位終太府卿，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao he was reduced to Marquis of a county; he ended as Director of the Grand Storehouse and was posthumously made Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Northern Qi's Tianbao era his title was reduced to county marquis; he ended his career as director of the grand storehouse and was posthumously made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 構早有名譽，曆官清顯，常以雅道自居，甚為名流所重。

translations.literal: Gou early won renown; in office after office he held pure and eminent posts, ever taking refinement as his standard, and was greatly esteemed by leading figures.
translations.idiomatic: Gou earned a reputation early; in one clear and eminent post after another he cultivated a refined bearing and was greatly respected by men of note.

sentences.zh: 子丕，有父風，位尚書祠部郎中。

translations.literal: His son Pi had his father's character and held the post of Director of the Sacrifices Bureau in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pi inherited his father's manner and served as director of the sacrifices bureau in the ministry.

sentences.zh: 丕弟克，通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Pi's younger brother Ke was Direct Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Pi's younger brother Ke was direct attendant-in-ordinary of the rapid cavalry.

sentences.zh: 獎弟諧。

translations.literal: Jiang's younger brother was He.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang's younger brother was He.

sentences.zh: 諧字虔和，幼有風采。

translations.literal: He's style name was Qianhe; as a child he had distinguished bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He, style name Qianhe, showed exceptional poise even as a child.

sentences.zh: 趙郡李搔嘗過元叉門下，見之，歸謂其父元忠曰：「領軍門下見一神人。」

translations.literal: Li Sao of Zhao Commandery once passed by Yuan Cha's gate, saw him, returned home and said to his father Yuan Zhong: "At the commandant-in-chief's gate I saw a divine man.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sao of Zhao Commandery once visited Yuan Cha's residence, saw He, and told his father Yuan Zhong, "At the commandant-in-chief's gate I saw a man like a god.

sentences.zh: 元忠曰：「必李諧也。」

translations.literal: Yuan Zhong said: "It must be Li He.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhong said, "That must have been Li He."

sentences.zh: 問之果然。

translations.literal: When asked, it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: When they inquired, it proved to be true.

sentences.zh: 襲父先爵彭城侯。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's former title, Marquis of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's former title of Marquis of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 文辯為時所稱，歷位位中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His literary eloquence was praised by the age; he successively held the post of Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His eloquence was widely admired, and he rose to vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天平末，魏欲與梁和好，朝議將以崔甗為使主。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianping, Wei wished to make peace with Liang; court deliberation was about to appoint Cui Yan as chief envoy.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianping era Wei sought peace with Liang, and the court planned to appoint Cui Yan as chief envoy.

sentences.zh: 甗曰：「文采與識，甗不推李諧；

translations.literal: Yan said: "In literary grace and discernment, Yan does not defer to Li He;
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "In literary grace and insight Yan does not defer to Li He;

sentences.zh: 口頰<扁頁>々，諧乃大勝。」

translations.literal: in glibness of mouth and cheek, He greatly surpasses.
translations.idiomatic: but in eloquence of tongue and cheek, He far surpasses me.

sentences.zh: 於是以諧兼常侍、盧元明兼吏部郎、李業興兼通直常侍聘焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon He was made Concurrent Regular Attendant, Lu Yuanming Concurrent Director of the Personnel Bureau, and Li Yexing Concurrent Direct Attendant-in-Ordinary, and they were sent on the mission.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore sent as concurrent regular attendant, Lu Yuanming as concurrent director of the personnel bureau, and Li Yexing as concurrent direct attendant-in-ordinary on the embassy.

sentences.zh: 梁武使硃異覘客，異言諧、元明之美。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang sent Zhu Yi to observe the guests; Yi spoke of the excellence of He and Yuanming.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang sent Zhu Yi to observe the envoys; Yi spoke of the excellence of He and Yuanming.

sentences.zh: 諧等見，及出，梁武目送之，謂左右曰：「朕今日遇勍敵，卿輩常言北間都無人物，此等何處來？」

translations.literal: When He and the others had audience and went out, Emperor Wu of Liang watched them depart and said to those beside him: "Today I have met formidable rivals. You always say the north has no men of talent—where did these come from?
translations.idiomatic: After He and the others were received and departed, Emperor Wu watched them go and said to his attendants, "Today I have met formidable opponents. You always say the north has no talent—where did these men come from?

sentences.zh: 謂異曰：「過卿所談。」

translations.literal: He said to Yi: "Beyond what you spoke of.
translations.idiomatic: He told Yi, "They surpass what you described."

sentences.zh: 是時鄴下言風流者，以諧及隴西李神俊、范陽盧元明、北海王元景、弘農楊遵彥、清河崔贍為首。

translations.literal: At that time among those spoken of as men of refinement in Ye, He ranked first together with Li Shenjun of Longxi, Lu Yuanming of Fanyang, Wang Yuanjing of Beihai, Yang Zunyan of Hongnong, and Cui Zhan of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the leading men of refinement in Ye were He, Li Shenjun of Longxi, Lu Yuanming of Fanyang, Wang Yuanjing of Beihai, Yang Zunyan of Hongnong, and Cui Zhan of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 初通梁國，妙簡行人，神俊位已高，故諧等五人繼踵，而遵彥遇疾道還，竟不行。

translations.literal: When relations with Liang were first opened, envoys were finely chosen; Shenjun's rank was already high, so He and the other five followed in succession, while Zunyan fell ill on the road and returned, and in the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When contact with Liang was first established, envoys were carefully selected; Shenjun's rank was already too high, so He and five others went in succession, though Zunyan fell ill on the road and returned without ever completing the mission.

sentences.zh: 既南北通好，務以俊乂相矜，銜命接客，必盡一時之選，無才地者不得與焉。

translations.literal: Once north and south were at peace, each side sought to display its finest men; those bearing credentials to receive guests had to be the best of the age—those without talent and standing could not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Once north and south were at peace, each side sought to parade its finest men; only the most distinguished talents of the day were chosen to receive envoys—men without proven ability had no place in such work.

sentences.zh: 梁使每入，鄴下為之傾動，貴勝子弟盛飾聚觀，禮贈優渥，館門成市。

translations.literal: Whenever Liang envoys entered, Ye was stirred by them; sons of the noble and powerful dressed splendidly and gathered to watch; gifts and courtesies were lavish—the gate of the lodge became a marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Liang envoys arrived, Ye was thrown into commotion; sons of the nobility dressed splendidly to watch; gifts and courtesies were extravagant, and the embassy gate became a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 宴日，齊文襄使左右覘之，賓司一言制勝，文襄為之拊掌。

translations.literal: On a feast day, Wen Xiang of Qi sent attendants to observe; the guest officer won the exchange with a single remark, and Wen Xiang clapped his hands for it.
translations.idiomatic: On one feast day Wen Xiang of Qi sent attendants to observe; the host officer won the exchange with a single remark, and Wen Xiang clapped in delight.

sentences.zh: 魏使至梁，亦如梁使至魏，梁武親與談說，甚相愛重。

translations.literal: When Wei envoys reached Liang, it was just as when Liang envoys reached Wei: Emperor Wu of Liang personally conversed with them and greatly favored them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei envoys reached Liang, the reception matched Liang's in Ye: Emperor Wu of Liang spoke with them personally and held them in great esteem.

sentences.zh: 諧使還後遷秘書監，卒于大司農。

translations.literal: After He returned from the mission he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat Library and died while serving as Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from his mission He was promoted to director of the secretariat library and died while serving as grand minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 諧為人短小，六指，因癭而舉頤，因跛而緩步，因謇而徐言，人言李諧善用三短。

translations.literal: He was short in stature, had six fingers, because of a goiter raised his chin, because of lameness walked slowly, and because of stammering spoke deliberately; people said Li He made good use of his three shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: He was short, had six fingers, raised his chin because of a goiter, walked slowly because of lameness, and spoke with deliberate slowness because of a stammer; people said Li He turned his three defects to advantage.

sentences.zh: 文集十餘卷。

translations.literal: His collected writings comprise more than ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings run to more than ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 諧長子岳，字祖仁，官中散大夫。

translations.literal: He's eldest son Yue, style name Zuren, held the post of Grand Master of Leisurely Dissemination.
translations.idiomatic: He's eldest son Yue, style name Zuren, served as grand master of leisurely dissemination.

sentences.zh: 性純至，居期慘，未曾聽婢過前；

translations.literal: His nature was pure and utmost; during mourning he was grief-stricken and never allowed a maid to pass before him;
translations.idiomatic: He was utterly pure by nature; in mourning he was so grief-stricken that he never let a servant girl pass in front of him;

sentences.zh: 追思二親，言則流涕。

translations.literal: when recalling both parents, at words he would weep.
translations.idiomatic: and when he spoke of his parents, tears would flow.

sentences.zh: 岳弟庶，方雅好學，甚有家風。

translations.literal: Yue's younger brother Shu was upright and refined, fond of learning, very much in the family tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's younger brother Shu was upright, refined, and studious, very much in the family tradition.

sentences.zh: 歷位尚書郎、司徒掾，以清辯知名。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Ministry Gentleman and Aide of the Minister of Education, famed for lucid debate.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a ministry gentleman and an aide in the ministry of education, and was known for lucid argument.

sentences.zh: 常攝賓司，接對梁客，梁客徐陵深歎美焉。

translations.literal: He often acted as guest officer, receiving Liang envoys; the Liang envoy Xu Ling deeply admired him.
translations.idiomatic: He often served as host officer for Liang envoys; the Liang envoy Xu Ling admired him greatly.

sentences.zh: 庶生而天閹，崔諶調之曰：「教弟種須，以錐遍刺作孔，插以馬尾。」

translations.literal: Shu was born a eunuch; Cui Chen teased him, saying: "Teach your younger brother to grow a beard—use an awl to pierce holes all over, then insert horsehair.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had been born a eunuch; Cui Chen teased him, saying, "Teach your brother to grow a beard: pierce holes all over with an awl and insert horsehair.

sentences.zh: 庶曰：「先以此方回施貴族，藝眉有效，然後樹須。

translations.literal: Shu said: "First apply this recipe to the nobility—when painting eyebrows succeeds, then plant a beard.
translations.idiomatic: Shu replied, "First try that recipe on the nobility—when eyebrow-painting works, then plant a beard.

sentences.zh: ，」世傳諶門有惡疾，以呼沱為墓田，故庶言及之。

translations.literal: It was handed down in the world that the Chen clan had a foul disease, using the Hutuo River as burial fields, therefore Shu spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held that Cui Chen's family suffered from a disfiguring ailment and used the Hutuo River valley as their burial ground—hence Shu's retort."

sentences.zh: 邢子才在傍大笑。

translations.literal: Xing Zicai laughed greatly at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Zicai burst out laughing beside them.

sentences.zh: 除臨漳令。

translations.literal: He was appointed Magistrate of Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》之出，庶與盧斐、王松年等訟共不平。

translations.literal: When the Book of Wei was published, Shu together with Lu Fei, Wang Songnian, and others jointly sued, all indignant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Book of Wei was published, Shu together with Lu Fei, Wang Songnian, and others filed suit together in outrage.

sentences.zh: 魏收書王慧龍自雲太原人，又書王瓊不善事；

translations.literal: Wei Shou wrote that Wang Huilong claimed to be a man of Taiyuan, and also wrote that Wang Qiong was inept;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou had written that Wang Huilong falsely claimed Taiyuan as his native place, and that Wang Qiong was incompetent;

sentences.zh: 以盧同附《盧玄傳》；

translations.literal: placed Lu Tong in the biography of Lu Xuan;
translations.idiomatic: placed Lu Tong in the biography of Lu Xuan rather than giving him his own;

sentences.zh: 李平為陳留人，雲其家貧賤。

translations.literal: wrote that Li Ping was from Chenliu and said his family was poor and base.
translations.idiomatic: and described Li Ping as a man of Chenliu from a poor and humble family.

sentences.zh: 故斐等喧訟，語楊愔云：「魏收合誅。

translations.literal: Therefore Fei and the others raised a clamorous suit, saying to Yang Yin: "Wei Shou ought to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Fei and the others raised a loud protest, telling Yang Yin, "Wei Shou deserves death.

sentences.zh: 愔党助魏，故遂白齊文宣，庶等並髡頭鞭杖二百，庶死於臨漳獄中。

translations.literal: Yin, partial to Wei, therefore reported to Wen Xuan of Qi; Shu and the others were all shorn and flogged two hundred strokes; Shu died in Linzhang prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sided with Wei and reported the matter to Wen Xuan of Qi; Shu and the others were shaved and flogged two hundred strokes, and Shu died in Linzhang prison.

sentences.zh: 庶兄岳痛之，終身不曆臨漳縣門。

translations.literal: Shu's elder brother Yue grieved over it and never in his life passed through the gate of Linzhang County.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's elder brother Yue grieved so deeply that he never passed through Linzhang's gates for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 庶妻，元羅女也。

translations.literal: Shu's wife was a daughter of Yuan Luo.
