translations.idiomatic: Shu's wife was a daughter of Yuan Luo.

sentences.zh: 庶亡後，岳使妻伴之寢宿。

translations.literal: After Shu's death, Yue had his wife keep her company in sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu died, Yue had his wife sleep beside hers for companionship.

sentences.zh: 積五年，元氏更適趙起。

translations.literal: For five years this continued; the lady of the Yuan clan remarried Zhao Qi.
translations.idiomatic: This continued for five years until she remarried Zhao Qi.

sentences.zh: 嘗夢庶謂己曰：「我薄福，托劉氏為女，明旦當出，彼家甚貧，恐不能見養。

translations.literal: Once she dreamed that Shu said to her: "My scant fortune—entrusted as a daughter to the Liu clan; tomorrow she will be born; that family is very poor, I fear they cannot support her.
translations.idiomatic: Once she dreamed that Shu said, "I have little merit; I have been born again as a daughter in the Liu family. She will come into the world tomorrow. They are very poor and may not be able to raise her.

sentences.zh: 夫妻舊恩，故來相見告，君宜乞取我。

translations.literal: Husband and wife's old kindness—therefore I come to meet and tell you; you ought to beg to take me back.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the old bond between husband and wife I come to tell you—you should ask to take me back.

sentences.zh: 劉家在七帝坊十字銜南，東入窮巷是也。」

translations.literal: The Liu family is south of the cross-street of Qidi Fang, east into the poor lane—that is the place.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu family lives south of the crossroads at Qidi Lane—down the poor alley to the east.

sentences.zh: 元氏不應，庶曰：「君似懼趙公意，我自說之。」

translations.literal: The lady of Yuan did not answer; Shu said: "You seem to fear Master Zhao's mind—I will speak to him myself.
translations.idiomatic: She did not respond. Shu said, "You seem to fear Zhao's feelings. I will speak to him myself."

sentences.zh: 於是起亦夢焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qi also dreamed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qi then had the same dream.

sentences.zh: 起寤問妻，言之符合。

translations.literal: When Qi awoke and asked his wife, their words matched.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke and asked his wife, their accounts matched.

sentences.zh: 遂持錢帛躬往求劉氏，如所夢得之，養女長而嫁焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took money and cloth and went in person to seek out the Liu family; as in the dream he obtained her, raised the girl, and when grown gave her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He took money and cloth and went in person to the Liu family; exactly as in the dream he found the child, raised her, and later gave her in marriage.

sentences.zh: 庶弟蔚，少清秀，有襟期倫理，涉觀史傳，兼屬文詞。

translations.literal: Shu's younger brother Wei was clear and handsome in youth, with breadth of mind and moral principle, versed in histories and annals, and also skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's younger brother Wei was refined and handsome from youth, with breadth of character and principle, well read in history, and skilled in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 昆季並尚風流，長裾廣袖，從容甚美，然頗涉疏放。

translations.literal: The brothers all admired refinement; long skirts and broad sleeves—they were very graceful, yet rather given to excess.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers all cultivated a refined style—long robes, wide sleeves, graceful bearing—though they could be somewhat unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 唯蔚能自持公幹理，甚有時譽。

translations.literal: Only Wei could restrain himself with public integrity and order, and had great repute in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wei maintained public integrity and discipline and enjoyed considerable repute.

sentences.zh: 坐兄庶事徙平州。

translations.literal: Because of his brother Shu's affair he was banished to Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled to Pingzhou because of his brother Shu's affair.

sentences.zh: 後還，位尚書左中兵郎中，仍聘陳使副。

translations.literal: Later he returned and held the post of Director of the Left Central Military Bureau in the Ministry, and again served as deputy on an embassy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned, served as director of the left central military bureau in the ministry, and again served as deputy envoy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 江南以其父曾經將命，甚重焉。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi greatly valued him because his father had once borne imperial credentials.
translations.idiomatic: The south held him in high regard because his father had once served as an imperial envoy.

sentences.zh: 還，坐將人度江私市，除名。

translations.literal: On returning, because he had secretly sent men across the river for private trade, he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was struck from the rolls for secretly sending men across the river to trade.

sentences.zh: 後卒于秘書丞，士友悼惜之。

translations.literal: Later he died as Secretary Aide; scholar-friends mourned and regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as secretary aide, and friends mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 蔚弟若，聰敏，頗傳家業，風采詞令，有聲鄴下。

translations.literal: Wei's younger brother Ruo was clever and keen, largely inheriting the family tradition; in bearing and eloquence he had a reputation in Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's younger brother Ruo was clever and keen, largely inherited the family's literary tradition, and was known in Ye for grace and eloquence.

sentences.zh: 坐兄庶事徙臨海。

translations.literal: Because of his brother Shu's affair he was banished to Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled to Linhai because of his brother Shu's affair.

sentences.zh: 乾明初，追還，後兼散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianming he was recalled, and later additionally served as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qianming era he was recalled and later served additionally as regular attendant-in-ordinary of the rapid cavalry.

sentences.zh: 大被親狎，加儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was greatly favored and drawn close, and was additionally granted Palace Equal to the Three Lords.
translations.idiomatic: He became a great favorite at court and was additionally granted palace equal to the three lords.

sentences.zh: 若性滑稽，善諷誦，數奉旨詠詩，並使說外間世事可笑樂者。

translations.literal: Ruo's nature was witty; he was skilled at satirical recitation, repeatedly received the emperor's command to compose poetry on themes, and was also made to tell amusing tales of the world's affairs outside.
translations.idiomatic: Ruo had a witty temperament, excelled at satirical verse, was often commanded to compose poetry on set themes, and was also made to recount amusing stories from beyond the court.

sentences.zh: 凡所話談，每多會旨。

translations.literal: In all his talk and discourse, he often hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: In conversation he almost always hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 嘗在省中，趨而前卻，對答學奏事之象，和士開聞而奏之。

translations.literal: Once in the Secretariat he hurried forward and back, answering in imitation of the manner of presenting memorials; He Shikai heard and reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the secretariat he ran forward and back in mockery of officials presenting memorials; He Shikai heard of it and reported him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝每狎弄之。

translations.literal: The emperor constantly played with and teased him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor constantly played with and teased him.

sentences.zh: 武成以斛律金舊老，每朝，賜羊車上殿。

translations.literal: Wucheng, because Hulu Jin was an old veteran, each morning granted him a sheep-cart to enter the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng granted the aged veteran Hulu Jin a sheep-cart to enter the audience hall each morning.

sentences.zh: 金曾使人奉啟，若為舍人，誤奏雲在闕下，詔命出羊車。

translations.literal: Jin once sent someone to submit a memorial; Ruo was serving as Attendant, mistakenly reported that Jin was below the gate, and an edict ordered the sheep-cart sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Jin once sent a messenger to submit a memorial; Ruo, serving as attendant, mistakenly reported that Jin was at the gate, and the court ordered the sheep-cart sent out.

sentences.zh: 若重思，知金不至，竊言：「羊車、鹿車何所迎？」

translations.literal: Ruo thought again, knew Jin would not come, and whispered: "Sheep-cart, deer-cart—what are they welcoming?
translations.idiomatic: Ruo reconsidered, realized Jin would not come, and muttered, "Sheep-cart, deer-cart—what are they going to fetch?

sentences.zh: 帝聞，亦笑而不責。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and also laughed without blaming him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and laughed without rebuking him.

sentences.zh: 又帝于後園講武，令若為吳將，皇后皆出，引若當前，觀其進止俯仰。

translations.literal: Again, when the emperor held military exercises in the rear garden, he made Ruo play a Wu general; the empresses all came out and drew Ruo forward to observe his advance, retreat, and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion the emperor held military drills in the rear garden and made Ruo play a Wu general; the empresses all came out and summoned Ruo forward to watch his movements.

sentences.zh: 事罷，遣使謝之，厚加賞賜。

translations.literal: When the affair ended, he sent envoys to thank him and richly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When it was over he sent a messenger to thank Ruo and gave him a generous reward.

sentences.zh: 韓長鸞等忌惡之，密構其短，坐免官。

translations.literal: Han Changluan and others hated and envied him; secretly they fabricated his faults and he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Han Changluan and others envied him; they secretly built a case against him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔復本官。

translations.literal: Before long an edict restored his original office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict restored him to his former office.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，卒于秦王府諮議。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died as Adviser of the Prince of Qin's domain.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Kaihuang era of Sui while serving as adviser to the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 諧弟邕，字修穆，幼而俊爽，有逸才。

translations.literal: He's younger brother Yong, style name Xiumu, was handsome and bright in youth and had outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: He's younger brother Yong, style name Xiumu, was brilliant from youth and possessed exceptional talent.

sentences.zh: 位高陽王雍友。

translations.literal: He held the post of Companion to the Prince of Gaoyang, Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as companion to the Prince of Gaoyang, Yong.

sentences.zh: 幾所交遊，皆倍年俊秀。

translations.literal: Most of those with whom he associated were talented youths older than himself.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his companions were gifted men older than himself.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈洛州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Governor of Luozhou, with the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made governor of Luozhou with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 論曰：郭祚才幹敏實，有世務之長。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Guo Zuo's talent and ability were quick and solid; he had the strengths of worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In appraisal: Guo Zuo was quick and solid in talent, with a gift for practical affairs.

sentences.zh: 孝文經綸之始，獨在勤勞之地。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's governance, he alone stood in the place of toil.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he alone bore the burden of arduous labor.

sentences.zh: 居官任事，可稱述焉。

translations.literal: In holding office and answering to affairs, he may be commended.
translations.idiomatic: In holding office and performing his duties, he is worth commending.

sentences.zh: 張彝風力謇謇，有王臣之氣，銜命擁旄，風聲克舉。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi was forceful and sternly upright, with the bearing of a royal minister; bearing imperial command and leading armies, his renown was fully raised.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi was forceful and sternly upright, with the bearing of a royal minister; entrusted with command and leading armies, his reputation was fully achieved.

sentences.zh: 俱魏氏器能之臣乎！

translations.literal: Are they not both capable ministers of Wei!
translations.idiomatic: Both were capable ministers of Wei!

sentences.zh: 遭隨有命，二子俱逢世亂，悲哉！

translations.literal: Meeting with the decree of fate, both sons encountered a chaotic age—how sad!
translations.idiomatic: Fate turned against them; both sons met a turbulent age—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 晏之、乾威，可謂亡焉不絕。

translations.literal: Yan Zhi and Qianwei may be said to have perished yet not ended.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhi and Qianwei may be said to have perished yet not ended—their lines survived.

sentences.zh: 邢巒以文武才策，當軍國之任，內參機揆，外寄折沖，其緯世之器歟！

translations.literal: Xing Luan, by civil and military talent and strategy, bore the charge of army and state; within he participated in the pivot of power, without he was entrusted with repelling the foe—is he not an instrument for ordering the age!
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan, with civil and military talent, bore the nation's military burdens; within he advised on state strategy, without he was trusted to repel enemies—is this not the stuff of one who orders an age!

sentences.zh: 子才少有盛名，鼓動京洛，文宗學府，獨秀當年，舉必任真，情無飾智，疏通簡易，罕見其人，足為一代之模楷也。

translations.literal: Zicai early had great fame, stirring the capital; in the literary canon of the academy he stood alone in his year; in action he always relied on sincerity, in feeling he had no pretense of wisdom; open, clear, and simple—rare is such a man; he is enough to be a model of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Zicai won great fame early and stirred the capital; in scholarship he stood alone in his generation; in action he was always sincere, never feigning wisdom; open, clear, and plain-spoken—such men are rare, and he is fit to be a model of his age.

sentences.zh: 及明崔甗之謗言，執侯景之奸使，昔人稱孟軻為勇，于文簡公見之。

translations.literal: And in clarifying Cui Yan's slander, in seizing the treacherous envoy of Hou Jing—the ancients called Meng Ke brave; in Wen Jian Gong this may be seen.
translations.idiomatic: In exposing Cui Yan's slander and arresting Hou Jing's treacherous envoy, he showed the courage the ancients ascribed to Mencius—as Wen Jian Gong he proved it.

sentences.zh: 唯嘗短崔暹，頗為累德。

translations.literal: Only that he once spoke ill of Cui Xian somewhat marred his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Only his past criticism of Cui Xian somewhat tarnished his moral standing.

sentences.zh: 阮籍未嘗品藻人物，斯亦良有以焉。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji never ranked and appraised persons; on this point too there is good reason.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ji never appraised and ranked other people—there was good reason for that.

sentences.zh: 李崇風質英重，毅然秀立，任當將相，望高朝野。

translations.literal: Li Chong's character was heroic and grave, erect and outstanding in elegance; fit for general or minister, his renown was high in court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong was heroic and grave in character, upright and distinguished in bearing; fit for general or minister, his renown stood high in court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 平以高明幹略，效智于時，出入當官，功名克著，贊務之材也。

translations.literal: Ping, by loftiness and brightness in resource and strategy, offered his wisdom to the age; entering and leaving office, his achievements and fame were fully established—he was material for assisting in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ping offered his brilliance and strategic ability to his age; in every office his achievements and fame were fully realized—he was a man fit to assist in governance.

sentences.zh: 諧風流文辯，蓋人望乎！

translations.literal: He, in refinement and literary eloquence—surely he is a man the multitude looks up to!
translations.idiomatic: He, with his refinement and literary eloquence—is he not a man the world looks up to!
